title: 13 Tibetan Associations Unite in Zurich in a Powerful Candlelight March to Honour Pawo Lobga Rangzen on the 33rd Day Since His Passing
author: oot_admin
content: Thirteen Tibetan associations in Switzerland jointly organised a peaceful candle march in Zurich on 5 August 2026 to commemorate the 33rd day since the passing of Tibetan self-immolator Pawo Lobga Rangzen. More than 700 people participated in the march, which began at Werdmühleplatz Zurich and proceeded towards the Chinese Embassy in Zurich. During the programme, representatives of the organising associations delivered speeches and jointly read a press statement explaining the purpose of the gathering and remembering Lobga Rangzen’s final message. The Tibet Bureau Geneva’s UN Advocacy Officer, Phuntsok Topgyal, attended the event on behalf of Representative Thinlay Chukki. In his address, he spoke about the circumstances surrounding Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation, including the location, timing, final message, and the circumstances of his passing. Phuntsok Topgyal stated that Lobga Rangzen carried out his self-immolation following the implementation of what he described as China’s ethnic unity and related policies, which, according to him, threatened Tibetan culture, language, and identity. He said that Lobga Rangzen’s action was intended to draw international attention to the situation in Tibet, seek greater international support for the Tibetan cause, and call for the repeal of those policies. Speaking about Lobga Rangzen’s final message, Phuntsok Topgyal emphasised that his words should not be interpreted as suggesting that Tibetans lack unity. Phuntsok Topgyal said,“Today, more than 700 people have gathered for this protest, and 13 different Tibetan associations have come together to organise this event. This reflects the unity of our people.” He further explained that Lobga Rangzen had witnessed the situation inside Tibet, experienced life in exile in India, and observed the decades of dedicated work carried out by His Holiness the Dalai Lama for Tibet and the Tibetan people. After moving to the United States, Lobga Rangzen also witnessed the lives of Tibetans living in the diaspora. According to Phuntsok Topgyal, Lobga Rangzen acknowledged that many Tibetans overseas had achieved economic stability and had himself said,“It is not that I lack food or shelter. I have everything.”However, despite having a comfortable life, he carried deep emotional pain every day because, in his view, some Tibetans who fully understood the situation in Tibet had nevertheless become involved with the Chinese government. Phuntsok Topgyal said that this was why Lobga Rangzen urged Tibetans to remember their identity, encouraging everyone to think,“I am Tibetan.” Phuntsok Topgyal also explained why Lobga Rangzen chose the United Nations Headquarters in New York, rather than the Chinese Embassy, as the location for his self-immolation. He noted that Lobga Rangzen was not the first person to self-immolate in front of the UN Headquarters in New York. According to him, Roger Allen LaPorte self-immolated there in 1965 in protest against the Vietnam War, making Lobga Rangzen the second known person to do so. He also noted that there have been three recorded incidents of self-immolation in front of the United Nations Office at Geneva. According to Phuntsok Topgyal, while Lobga Rangzen was not the first Tibetan to self-immolate, he was the first Tibetan to carry out a self-immolation in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York. Recalling Lobga Rangzen’s final moments, Phuntsok Topgyal said that, despite suffering extreme pain, he remained calm and did not run, shout, or jump. Instead, he stood motionless, “like a burning lamp or candle.” According to Phuntsok Topgyal, after his body had been severely burned, Lobga Rangzen slowly lowered himself, extended his hands forward, and fell into a full prostration facing the United Nations Headquarters building. Phuntsok Topgyal said this reflected Lobga Rangzen’s belief that, even in his final moments, the United Nations Headquarters was akin to a temple, a place where his prayers and message could reach the international community and where support for the Tibetan cause might be found. Phuntsok Topgyal further stated that Lobga Rangzen’s decision reflected his commitment to the principles of non-violence taught by His Holiness the Dalai Lama. He said that although Lobga Rangzen could have chosen violence, he instead followed the path of non-violence and sacrificed his life to convey his message to Tibetans and to the wider international community. In his closing remarks, Phuntsok Topgyal expressed concern that more than one month had passed since Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation, yet, according to him, the United Nations had not publicly responded. He called on Tibetans around the world to continue submitting appeals and messages of concern to the United Nations, parliamentarians, and governments in order to promote greater international awareness and support for the Tibetan cause. He added that while international recognition alone may not restore Tibet’s freedom, acknowledging Lobga Rangzen’s sacrifice would ensure that his action is recorded in international history as a peaceful self-immolation carried out in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York for the cause of Tibetan freedom. He concluded by expressing the hope that representatives of all 193 United Nations Member States would have the opportunity to learn about and better understand the Tibetan issue and the message left behind by Pawo Lobga Rangzen.

title: Austria Tibetan Community Leads Peaceful Rally to Mark One Month Since Pawo Lobga Rangzen’s Passing
author: oot_admin
content: Tibetan communities and supporters around the world are organising a global day of action to commemorate Pawo Lobga Rangzen, who carried out a self-immolation on 2 July 2026, in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York, United States. The action has drawn attention from Tibetan communities, human rights advocates, and supporters worldwide, who are using this occasion to raise awareness about the ongoing concerns surrounding human rights, cultural preservation, and the future of the Tibetan people. On 2 August 2026 marks one month since the passing of Pawo Lobga Rangzen. In remembrance, Tibetan communities and solidarity groups in different parts of the world are organising peaceful gatherings, demonstrations, and awareness activities. In Vienna, Austria, a joint peaceful protest rally is being organised by the Tibetan Community, Voluntary Tibet Advocacy Group (VTAG), Save Tibet, Students for a Free Tibet (SFT), and Friends of Tibet. The rally will begin in front of the Chinese Embassy and proceed towards Stephansplatz. Participants are expected to gather to express their solidarity and to call for greater international attention to the human rights situation in Tibet. The organisers stated that the demonstration aims to provide a platform for Tibetans and supporters to peacefully express their concerns, remember the sacrifice of Pawo Lobga Rangzen, and highlight issues related to human rights, religious freedom, cultural identity, and the preservation of Tibetan heritage. The event is also intended to encourage governments, international organisations, and the global community to continue monitoring developments related to Tibet and to support peaceful dialogue and respect for fundamental human rights. Tibetan communities and supporters participating in the worldwide activities have emphasised that the gatherings will be conducted peacefully and with respect for public order, while seeking to amplify awareness and international engagement on issues affecting Tibetans.

title: Lobga Rangzen’s Sacrifice Renews Attention on the Tibet Cause at UNHRC 63 as CTA’s UN Advocacy Officer Challenges China’s Policies
author: oot_admin
content: UN Advocacy Officer Phuntsok Topgyal from the Office of Tibet in Geneva delivered an oral statement during the 63rd Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC) under General Debate, Item 3, on behalf of the Society for Threatened Peoples. Addressing the Vice-President of the Council, the CTA’s UN Advocacy Officer expressed serious concern over policies that, according to Tibetan representatives and human rights organisations, threaten Tibetans’ cultural rights, freedom of religion or belief, and ability to preserve and transmit their language and cultural identity. He highlighted the case of Lobga Rangzen, who died after self-immolating outside United Nations Headquarters in New York on 2 July 2026, one day after China’s new “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress” entered into force. International Tibet Network reports that Lobga Rangzen’s act took place outside the UN Headquarters on 2 July, while Amnesty International has also called for renewed international scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding his death and the broader human rights situation in Tibet. UN Advocacy Officer Phuntsok Topgyal stated that Rangzen had chosen the United Nations because he believed the institution stood for justice, peace and human dignity, and stressed that his death should not become another forgotten tragedy. He also raised concerns regarding reported demolitions at Larung Gar Buddhist Academy, as well as cases involving the detention of Tibetan monks, educators and community leaders. He referred specifically to Chogtrul Dorje Ten, Geshe Konchok Choedak, Gen Pema, Tenzin Sangpo, Palden Yeshi and Lobsang Lungrik, whose cases, he said, raise serious concerns regarding fundamental rights and due process. He further highlighted concerns surrounding China’s new ethnic unity legislation. The law was adopted by China’s National People’s Congress on 12 March 2026 and entered into force on 1 July 2026. UN Special Procedures have expressed concern that the law could have serious implications for the linguistic, cultural and religious rights of ethnic communities, including Tibetans. In his concluding remarks, UN Advocacy Officer Phuntsok Topgyal said “A culture does not disappear in one day. It disappears when one language is silenced, one monastery destroyed, one teacher detained, one family left without answers.” He urged China to halt the reported demolitions, end arbitrary detention and enforced disappearance, protect Tibetans’ cultural, religious and linguistic rights, and grant independent UN human rights mechanisms unfettered access to the Tibet Autonomous Region and other Tibetan areas. The statement forms part of the Office of Tibet in Geneva’s continued advocacy during the 63rd Session of the Human Rights Council. In August, Representative Thinlay Chukki and UN Advocacy Officer Phuntsok Topgyal met representatives of more than 32 countries, OHCHR officials and UN Special Procedures mandate holders to raise concerns regarding the human rights situation in Tibet ahead of the Council session.

title: Representative Thinlay Chukki Highlights Growing Challenges to Tibet’s Cultural and Religious Identity At “Fenix” Event in Rome
author: oot_admin
content: At the National Youth “Fenix” event in Rome, Thinlay Chukki, Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama and the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) at the Tibet Bureau in Geneva, delivered a live online address highlighting continuing concerns over human rights, religious freedom, and the preservation of Tibetan linguistic and cultural identity under the policies of the People’s Republic of China. In her address, Representative Thinlay Chukki underscored the continuing erosion of Tibet’s distinct linguistic, cultural and religious identity and stressed the urgent need for sustained international attention to policies affecting the fundamental rights and freedoms of the Tibetan people. She emphasised that preserving and transmitting Tibet’s language, culture, religion and traditions remain essential to safeguarding the identity and heritage of the Tibetan people. Particular attention was drawn to restrictions affecting religious freedom and Tibetan cultural and linguistic expression, including increasing pressure on the use of the Tibetan language in education and public life. The Representative also highlighted concerns surrounding the “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress”, which Tibetan representatives and human rights advocates have raised in connection with the preservation of Tibetan identity, language and cultural rights. Representative Thinlay Chukki emphasised the importance of continued engagement by governments, parliamentarians, international institutions and civil society. She called for sustained attention to universal human rights principles and for respect for the rights of Tibetans to preserve and freely transmit their language, culture, religion and way of life. The programme was attended by Claudio Cardelli, President of the Italy-Tibet Association; National Councillors Pier Francesco Quaglietti and Nicola Misiani; and Umbria Representative Moreno Primieri. Leonardo Mallozzi, President of La Consolazione–ETAB, and its councillors Gianluca Moretti and Annalisa Aluigi also participated in the event. The event provided a broader platform for discussion of the human rights situations of Tibetans, Uyghurs and other communities affected by restrictive policies in China. A representative of the World Uyghur Congress also addressed concerns relating to Uyghur cultural identity, religious freedom, family separation, surveillance and the challenges faced by Uyghurs living abroad.

title: Tibetan Community in Switzerland Marks 66th Anniversary of Tibetan Democracy
author: oot_admin
content: The Tibetan Community in Switzerland commemorated the 66th Anniversary of Tibetan Democracy with a gathering of nearly 200 community members at Grosshalle Töss, Tössstalstrasse, bringing together religious leaders, former members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, representatives of Tibetan organisations, community leaders and guests. Among the distinguished guests were Rikon Khen Rinpoche Tenzin Jangchup, Thinlay Chukki, Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, former members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, Phuntsok Topgyal, UN Advocacy Officer of the Office of Tibet, Geneva, and representatives of Tibetan NGOs. The programme began with traditional prayers, followed by the Tibetan national anthem, a minute of silence in remembrance of those who sacrificed their lives for Tibet, and the Tibetan Democracy Day song. Representatives of the Tibetan Community subsequently presented their annual activity reports and financial accounts, reflecting the community’s commitment to transparency, accountability and democratic participation. Addressing the gathering, Thinlay Chukki highlighted the significance of Tibetan democracy and the responsibility it places on every Tibetan. Recalling her earlier participation in a conference in Berlin, she spoke of an encounter with young boy from Hong Kong who expressed their desire to contribute to the future of their nation but were uncertain about how they could do so. The experience, she said, reinforced her appreciation of the democratic institutions available to Tibetans today, established under the visionary leadership of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. Thinlay Chukki also briefed the community on recent developments concerning China’s ethnic policies and proposed ethnic unity legislation, expressing concern over their potential long-term implications for Tibetan language, culture, religion, traditions and identity. She emphasised that preserving Tibetan identity is a collective responsibility requiring active engagement from every generation. She further called on Tibetans to exercise responsibility and sensitivity in their use of social media, noting that Tibetans inside Tibet closely follow the activities and statements of Tibetans living abroad. She urged community members to ensure that their public expressions do not unintentionally cause discouragement or distress to those living under difficult circumstances inside Tibet. Following the address, Phuntsok Topgyal, UN Advocacy Officer of the Office of Tibet, Geneva, presented an overview of the Bureau’s international advocacy and outreach work. His presentation covered the Bureau’s activities from 2022 to 2025, providing the community with a broader understanding of its engagement at the international level. The presentation highlighted the Office of Tibet’s engagement with the United Nations, diplomatic missions, international organisations and civil society, as well as its efforts to maintain international attention on the human rights situation in Tibet and the preservation of Tibet’s distinct cultural, religious and linguistic identity. It also underlined the importance of sustained and long-term international engagement, particularly as the Tibet issue may require continued advocacy for many years to come. The celebration concluded with a renewed commitment among members of the Tibetan community to safeguard their democratic heritage, preserve Tibetan identity and culture, support Tibetans inside Tibet, and uphold the principles of non-violence, democracy, human rights and compassion championed by His Holiness the Dalai Lama.

title: UN Human Rights Chief Expresses Concern Over Restrictions on Tibetans
author: oot_admin
content: The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk expressed deep concern over the deteriorating human rights situation in Tibet, particularly restrictions affecting the Tibetan people’s freedom of religion. Addressing the opening of the 63rd session of the United Nations Human Rights Council in Geneva, the High Commissioner highlighted a range of pressing global human rights concerns, including armed conflicts, restrictions on civic space, discrimination, and violations affecting vulnerable and minority communities. In a significant reference to Tibet, the High Commissioner stated that “tightening restrictions on the rights of the Tibetan people, including their freedom of religion, are deeply troubling” and appealed for an urgent change in these policies. The statement is particularly significant as concerns continue to grow over restrictions on the exercise of religious and cultural rights in Tibet. The High Commissioner’s call underscores the importance of respecting fundamental human rights and ensuring that Tibetans are able to exercise their rights and freedoms without undue restrictions. The Tibet Bureau, Geneva, welcomes the explicit attention given to the human rights situation in Tibet and reiterates the importance of sustained international engagement on the protection of Tibetan religious, cultural and fundamental rights. The Bureau will continue to engage with UN mechanisms, diplomatic missions and international partners to ensure that developments in Tibet remain part of the international human rights discourse. The High Commissioner reaffirmed that human rights must remain central to international cooperation, accountability and the pursuit of lasting peace, emphasising that universal human rights provide a framework for addressing contemporary global challenges.

title: 7th Tibetan Language and Culture Summer Camp Inspires Young Tibetans in Switzerland
author: oot_admin
content: The 7th Tibetan Language and Culture Summer Camp, organised by the Tibetan Language and Culture Schools under the Tibetan Community in Switzerland, was successfully held from 19 to 25 July 2026 in Einsiedeln, Switzerland. The week-long camp brought together 24 Tibetan children, aged 9 to 14, providing them with a valuable opportunity to strengthen their knowledge of Tibetan language, culture, history, and identity. On the auspicious occasion of Lhakar, Thinlay Chukki, Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama at the Office of Tibet, Geneva, addressed the participants on the importance of preserving Tibetan language, culture, and identity. She also highlighted the challenges facing Tibetan children inside Tibet, particularly concerns over the residential boarding school system and its impact on Tibetan language, culture, and traditional values. Khenpo Tenzin Jangchup, Abbot of the Rikon Tibet Institute, spoke on the meaning and significance of Lhakar, while Kalsang Kangrang, Vice President of the Tibetan Community in Switzerland, encouraged the children to remain committed to learning and preserving their cultural heritage. Throughout the seven-day programme, participants attended classes on Tibetan language, Tibetan Buddhism, Tibetan history, Tibetan songs and musical instruments, Lhakar and Sangsol, and the introduction to Central Tibetan Administration (CTA). They also took part in practical activities such as momo making, Tibetan cooking, traditional Gorshey dance, games, quizzes, Tibetan Tombola, and talent shows based on Tibetan themes. Each day began with yoga, meditation, and prayers, creating a positive environment for learning and personal growth. A key highlight of the camp was an interactive workshop led by Phuntsok Topgyal, UN Advocacy Officer at the Office of Tibet, Geneva. He introduced the children to Tibet’s history, geography, culture, and the establishment and evolution of the Central Tibetan Administration. He also explained the development of Tibetan democracy and encouraged the participants to recognise their responsibility as the future generation of Tibetans by learning their history, actively engaging with the Tibetan community, and preserving their language and cultural identity. Throughout the camp, children were encouraged to communicate in Tibetan, helping them build confidence in speaking their mother tongue and strengthening their connection to their heritage. Parents expressed their appreciation for the camp, noting its positive impact on their children’s confidence, cultural awareness, and sense of identity. The successful completion of the 7th Tibetan Language and Culture Summer Camp reflects the continued commitment of the Tibetan Community in Switzerland to nurturing the next generation and ensuring that Tibetan language, culture, and identity continue to thrive in the free world.

title: The 43rd Sakya Trizin Kyabgon Gyana Vajra Rinpoche Presides Over Sixth European Sakya Monlam for Universal Peace and Happiness in Zurich
author: oot_admin
content: The 43rd Sakya Trizin Gyana Vajra Rinpoche presided over the Sixth European Sakya Monlam for Universal Peace and Happiness organised by the European Sakya Monlam Committee in the city of Turbenthal in the canton of Zurich, Switzerland. The three-day European Sakya Monlam held from 24 to 26 July brought together monks, nuns, and practitioners from various traditions. title: Tibetan Community in Italy Holds Peaceful Demonstration in Rome in Memory of Lobga Rangzen
author: oot_admin
content: The Tibetan Community in Italy, together with Italian supporters and friends of Tibet, organised a peaceful demonstration outside the Chinese Embassy in Rome on 11 July, 2026, to honour the memory of Tibetan activist Lobga Rangzen (Lobsang Palden), who passed away following a self-immolation protest near the United Nations Headquarters in New York. The gathering took place at Via Bruxelles, Rome, where Tibetan community members assembled to pay tribute to Lobga Rangzen, express their condolences, and raise awareness of issues concerning Tibetan identity, cultural preservation, religious freedom, and human rights. Participants observed the demonstration peacefully, carrying Tibetan flags, banners, and messages of remembrance. Community representatives and supporters delivered speeches highlighting the importance of preserving Tibetan language, culture, traditions, and spiritual heritage. The event served as a platform for the Tibetan community in Italy to express solidarity and to share their concerns with the international community. Lobga Rangzen carried out the self-immolation protest on 2 July 2026 near the United Nations Headquarters in New York. Tibetan organisations and supporters described his action as a call for international attention to the challenges faced by Tibetans and issues related to the protection of Tibetan identity and cultural rights. He later died as a result of injuries sustained during the incident. The Rome demonstration formed part of a wider series of memorial gatherings and solidarity events organised by Tibetan communities following Lobga Rangzen’s death. These events reflected the Tibetan diaspora’s continued efforts to peacefully raise awareness and seek international attention through public expressions of remembrance and advocacy. The Tibetan Community in Italy stated that the demonstration was held in a spirit of peace, dignity, and respect. Participants called for continued dialogue, understanding, and support for the preservation of cultural and religious traditions. The Chinese government has consistently rejected allegations of human rights violations in Tibet and maintains that Tibet is an integral part of China. Meanwhile, Tibetan organisations and supporters continue to raise concerns regarding cultural, religious, and social issues affecting Tibetans. The Rome gathering concluded with prayers, tributes, and moments of remembrance for Lobga Rangzen. Participants reaffirmed their commitment to peaceful advocacy and to continuing efforts to promote awareness of Tibetan issues among the international community.

title: Representative Thinlay Chukki Attends Inaugural Liu Xiaobo Human Rights Award Ceremony and Symposium on Constitutional Democracy in China in Leipzig; Presents CTA’s Middle Way Policy
author: oot_admin
content: Representative Thinlay Chukki, accompanied by Chinese Liaison Officer for European Countries Sangay Kyab, from the Tibet Bureau (Office of Tibet) in Geneva attended the inaugural of Liu Xiaobo Human Rights Award Ceremony and Symposium on Constitutional Democracy in China in Leipzig, Germany, on 13 an 14 July 2026. The Tibetan delegation spoke about the Central Tibetan Administration’s official policy of Middle Way Approach during the event jointly organised by two Chinesepro-democracy advocacy groups based in Europe, namelySino Euro Voice (aka Voice of Europe)and China Studies. In the morning of the first day, Chinese scholars researchers, and friends ofLiu Xiaobo delivered talks reflecting on Nobel LaureateLiu Xiaobo’s life, ideas, and legacy. In the afternoon, at 2:00 PM, the first Liu Xiaobo Human Rights Award Ceremony was held at Leipzig Town Hall. On the morning of 14 July, during a session focusing on Tibet, East Turkestan, and Southern Mongolia, Representative Thinlay Chukki delivered a presentation highlighting His Holiness the Dalai Lama’s Middle Way Policy as the Foundation for Resolving the Tibet-China Conflict. She expressed her appreciation for being invited to the commemoration marking the 9th anniversary of Liu Xiaobo’spassing, noting that His Holiness the Dalai Lama had consistently supported and cared for Liu Xiaobo, who himself was a follower of His Holiness’ philosophy of non-violence. She explained that the Middle Way Policy, proposed by His Holiness in the 1970s, is a path that avoids two extremes and is fundamentally rooted in the philosophy of non-violence. She said the policy neither advocates Tibetan independence nor accepts the current situation in Tibet. Instead, it calls for meaningful changes in Tibet and seeks to bring all traditional Tibetan areas under a single administrative entity without challenging the unity and stability of the PRC, thereby improving efficiency and effectiveness in preserving and promoting unique Tibetan characteristics. Representative Thinlay Chukki also referred to a book by Chinese scholarLau Han Shiang, who, through years of research and the use of credible Chinese historical documents, argued that Tibet was not part of China’s territory during the Ming and Qing dynasties. She said that despite many historical changes, Tibet had remained an independent nation, citing the Shimla Accord and other historical records as evidence. She further noted that during the time of the 13th Dalai Lama, Chinese officials and soldiers were expelled from Tibet, adding that Tibet’s historical independence is well documented. However, echoing the words of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama, she emphasised that “history should be researched by historians; we must focus on the future,” underscoring that the priority should be resolving the issue through a forward-looking approach rather than debating historical claims. Her presentation was followed by a question-and-answer session, during which participants raised various questions that were addressed. The conference was attended by representatives from the United States, Australia, New Zealand, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Taiwan, Poland, and France, along with Chinese, Mongolian, Tibetan, and other international participants.Taiwan’s Representative to the EU and Belgium, Ambassador Shieh Jhy-Wey, also attended the conference and delivered a speech.

title: The Flames of Resistance: Tibetan Diaspora Across Europe Under the Office of Tibet-Geneva Unites in Mourning Following the Self-Immolation of Lobga Rangzen
author: oot_admin
content: One day after China began implementing its new Ethnic Progress and Unity Law, Lobga Rangzen carried out a self-immolation in front of the United Nations Headquarters. Rangzen believed that this law posed a grave threat to the survival of Tibetan identity, culture, language, and religion. Through his final act of protest, he appealed to the Chinese government to reconsider and repeal policies that he believed would further undermine the distinct identity and rights of the Tibetan people. At the same time, he sought to draw the attention of the international community to ongoing human rights concerns in Tibet. He was not the first Tibetan to self-immolate in protest, nor was he the first individual to undertake such an act in front of the United Nations Headquarters. However, he was the first Tibetan in history to carry out such an act at this significant UN Headquarter. His choice of location carried profound symbolic meaning. Rather than directing his action against any individual Chinese and CCP, he chose a place that represents the hope of international justice and human dignity. His action reflected his belief in the power of peaceful protest and the principles of non-violence and dialogue. According to witnesses, before his passing, Rangzen stood in front of the United Nations building like a straight burning lamp, and at the final moment, he prostrated himself toward the building. For many Tibetans, this gesture represented prayer, hope, and faith in the international community. It symbolised his belief that his final appeal would be heard and that it would inspire renewed efforts toward a peaceful and just resolution of the Tibetan issue. On 3 July, the German Tibetan Community convened an emergency prayer gathering and public vigil in Berlin and other places of Germany engaging local media and human rights advocates to draw attention to the situation in Tibet. On the same day, the Tibetan Community in Austria, together with youth organisations including V-TAG Austria and Students for a Free Tibet (SFT), organised coordinated prayer services and solidarity gatherings in Vienna, Salzburg, Steiermark/Graz and Linz, reinforcing a shared message of unity, resilience, and peaceful advocacy. On 4 July, the Tibetan Community of Geneva held a special prayer service, bringing together members of the local Tibetan community to honor Rangzen’s memory while highlighting Geneva’s unique position as the home of major United Nations human rights institutions. The following day, 5 July, hundreds of Tibetans assembled at the Tibet Institute Rikon for a solemn Monlam memorial prayer ceremony organised by the Tibetan Community of Switzerland & Liechtenstein. During the prayer ceremony, Representative Thinlay Chukki, Advocacy Officer Phuntsok Topgyal, Accountant Tenzin Choesang, and EU–China Liaison Officer Sangay Kyab, President and members of the Tibetan community in offering prayers and paying tribute to Rangzen’s life, sacrifice, and unwavering call for Tibetan unity. life, sacrifice, and unwavering call for Tibetan unity.

title: Tibetan Community of Switzerland and Liechtenstein Celebrate His Holiness the Dalai Lama’s 91st Birthday in Bülach
author: oot_admin
content: On 11 July 2026, the Tibetan Community of Switzerland and Liechtenstein celebrated the 91st birthday of His Holiness the Great 14th Dalai Lama in Bülach, Switzerland. The celebration was attended by Swiss National Councillor Katharina Prelicz-Huber as the chief guest, along with the Abbot of Rikon Monastery, Representative Thinlay Chukki of the Tibet Bureau in Geneva, former Members of the Tibetan Parliament in Exile, and the President and Vice-President of the Tibetan Community of Switzerland and Liechtenstein. Following the ceremonial procession and enthronement of the portrait of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, the distinguished guests offered a mandala and the three auspicious representations of the Buddha’s body, speech, and mind before the portrait. The Swiss Tibetan Opera Troupe then led the gathering in the rendition of the Tibetan national anthem, after which a moment of silence was observed in remembrance of the selfless martyrs who sacrificed their lives for the Tibetan cause. Led by the monks of Rikon Monastery, the gathering recited long-life prayers for His Holiness the Dalai Lama and theWords of Truth. A prayer service was also held in memory of the Tibetan hero Lobga Rangzen, who self-immolated on 2 July 2026 in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York. Addresses were delivered by chief guest National Councillor Katharina Prelicz-Huber, President of the Tibetan Community of Switzerland and Liechtenstein Ngedun Gyatso, the Abbot of Rikon Monastery, and Representative Thinlay Chukki. In her address, Representative Thinlay Chukki underscored the importance of preserving Tibet’s unique language and culture. She urged Tibetans to remember the immeasurable benevolence of His Holiness the Dalai Lama and stressed the importance of fulfilling His Holiness’ aspirations and following his guidance. The Representative also called upon the Tibetan community in exile to honour the sacrifice of Lobga Rangzen and all Tibetans who have self-immolated for the Tibetan cause, urging everyone to strengthen their commitment to the Tibetan struggle. As part of the annual celebration, certificates of recognition from the Department of Education, Central Tibetan Administration, were presented to outstanding students of the Tibetan Weekend Language Schools. The programme concluded with cultural performances, including traditional songs and dances presented by the Tibetan Weekend Language Schools and local Tibetan NGOs in honour of His Holiness’ birthday. The Vice-President of the Tibetan Community of Switzerland and Liechtenstein delivered the vote of thanks, bringing the celebration to a successful conclusion.

title: Tibetan Delegation Attends U.S. Independence 250th Anniversary Celebration Hosted by the U.S. Mission in Geneva
author: oot_admin
content: Thinlay Chukki, Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama at the Tibet Bureau in Geneva, and Phuntsok Topgyal, UN Advocacy Officer, attended the commemoration marking the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States, hosted by the United States Mission to the United Nations and Other International Organisations in Geneva on 30 June 2026. The commemorative event brought together ambassadors, senior diplomats, representatives of permanent missions, officials from the United Nations and other international organisations, as well as members of civil society, reflecting the enduring global partnerships and shared democratic ideals celebrated on this historic occasion. On the sidelines of the celebration, the Tibetan delegation met with Tressa Rae Finerty, Chargé d’Affaires of the United States Mission to the United Nations and Other International Organisations in Geneva. They also had the opportunity to engage with representatives of numerous diplomatic missions, international organisations, and civil society groups. These cordial exchanges provided a valuable platform to strengthen existing relationships, foster new connections, and discuss issues of mutual interest, including the promotion of democracy, human rights, freedom, and international cooperation. The event offered an important occasion for meaningful dialogue and networking among the international diplomatic community, further enhancing the Tibet Bureau’s engagement with key partners and stakeholders in Geneva. The Bureau du Tibet extends its heartfelt congratulations to the people and Government of the United States on the historic occasion of the nation’s 250th anniversary. It also expresses its sincere appreciation for the United States’ longstandingcommitment to the promotion of democracy, human rights, religious freedom, and the peaceful resolution of global challenges, and conveys its best wishes for continued peace, prosperity, and success.

title: Tibet Bureau-Geneva Celebrates His Holiness the Dalai Lama’s 91st Birthday, Honours Memorial Service for Tibetan Martyr Lobga Rangzen
author: oot_admin
content: The Tibetan Association in Geneva observed the 91st birthday of His Holiness the Dalai Lama with a commemorative gathering that also included a memorial service for Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen. The event was attended by Representative Thinlay Chukki of the Tibet Bureau in Geneva and its staff, the President and Vice President of the Geneva Tibetan Association, monks from Dharma centres of Gyudmed Tantric Monastery and Salève, and members of the local Tibetan community. Representative Thinlay Chukki delivered a keynote address highlighting moral responsibility and community engagement. The programme, held on the morning of 4 July, began with a ceremonial procession of His Holiness the Dalai Lama’s portrait to the throne, followed by the singing of the Tibetan national anthem. Participants then paid tribute to the Tibetan martyrs who sacrificed their lives for the Tibetan cause. Addressing the gathering, the President of the Geneva Tibetan Association explained that although the event had been organised to celebrate His Holiness’s 91st birthday, the recent self-immolation of Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen on 2 July had prompted changes to the programme. He announced that the celebration would begin with a memorial service and prayers for Lobga Rangzen, followed by the ceremonial cake cutting. Student performances were limited to a few songs, while the remaining cultural programmes were cancelled as a mark of respect. Following the memorial prayers, Representative Thinlay Chukki addressed the gathering, reflecting on the significance of His Holiness the Dalai Lama’s birthday and paying tribute to Lobga Rangzen’s courage, commitment, and his final message. She praised the Geneva Tibetan Association for transforming the birthday celebration into a solemn occasion of prayer and remembrance, acknowledging the difficulty of revising the planned festivities in order to honour Lobga Rangzen’s sacrifice for the Tibetan cause. She also encouraged community members to openly share constructive feedback with the Tibet Bureau, noting that such engagement would strengthen its work and development. She further emphasised that every Tibetan in the region has a personal responsibility to contribute to the Tibetan cause and should not depend solely on the Tibet Bureau or local Tibetan associations. Even those unable to organise activities themselves, she said, should actively support the efforts of others. She concluded by expressing confidence that meaningful progress could be achieved if every Tibetan accepted this shared responsibility. The ceremony concluded with Representative Thinlay Chukki presenting tokens of appreciation to the teachers of the Geneva Weekend Tibetan School.

title: Geneva Lawmaker Condemns China’s Ethnic Unity Law as “A Dark Day” for Cultural Diversity
author: oot_admin
content: Cedric Jeanneret, Member of the Grand Council of the Republic and Canton of Geneva, hasstrongly condemnedthe entry into force of China’s new Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress, describing 1 July 2026 as “a dark day” for the country’s ethnic minorities and cultural diversity. He warned that the legislation represents a serious assault on the cultural identities and constitutional rights of Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, and other non-Han peoples living under the People’s Republic of China. In a statement issued following the implementation of the law, Jeanneret rejected Beijing’s characterisation of the legislation as a measure to promote ethnic harmony. “Today, 1 July 2026, is a dark day as the Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress comes into effect in China. This law does not entail any ethnic progress whatsoever. On the contrary, it aims to standardise the diverse cultural riches currently present in the People’s Republic of China—whether among the Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, and so many others.” Jeanneret stressed that the law contradicts the guarantees contained in China’s own Constitution. “Article 4 of the Chinese Constitution provides for regional autonomy. This autonomy is being flouted by this law, which constitutes a standardisation, an attempt to homogenise and destroy China’s historical cultural richness.” He argued that the legislation undermines the very diversity that has shaped China for centuries by placing state-defined national identity above the distinct languages, religions, histories, and cultures of its many ethnic communities. Speaking from Geneva, Jeanneret also voiced concern over what he described as the Chinese government’s increasingly repressive policies toward ethnic minorities and its activities beyond China’s borders. “Here in Geneva, we are deeply concerned to witness this development—the evolution of the Chinese regime, which does not respect its minorities, seeks to stifle them, and even goes so far as to persecute its own citizens here in Geneva and elsewhere.” He said these developments should concern democratic societies worldwide, warning that repression directed at Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, and other communities is no longer confined within China’s borders. Expressing solidarity with those affected, Jeanneret called on Beijing to reverse course. “We are today in solidarity with all the peoples suffering this repression by the Beijing regime, and we call on the Beijing regime to repeal this law and return to conditions more in line with human rights and more in keeping with the richness of the People’s Republic of China—to the eternal richness of China, to the richness of Tibet, and to the richness of all these peoples who constitute a precious legacy for humanity.” Representative Thinlay Chukki welcomed the growing international concern over the legislation, emphasising that the protection of cultural identity is a fundamental human rights issue. She stated that the preservation of Tibet’s language, religion, and cultural heritage is inseparable from the dignity and rights of the Tibetan people. She further stressed that policies aimed at forced assimilation threaten not only Tibetans but also Uyghurs, Mongolians, and other ethnic communities whose distinct identities are protected under international human rights principles. Calling for greater international engagement, Representative Thinlay Chukki urged democratic governments, parliaments, and international institutions to stand together in defending cultural diversity, religious freedom, and the universal rights of all peoples against policies that seek to erase their identities.

title: Peaceful Demonstration in Switzerland Calls for Repeal of China’s “Ethnic Unity Law”
author: oot_admin
content: A peaceful march and demonstration from Werdmühleplatz to the Chinese Consulate General in Zurich was organised by the Tibetan Community of Switzerland and Liechtenstein in partnership with the Tibetan Youth Association in Europe (TYAE), the Tibetan Friendship Association Switzerland (GSTF), the World Uyghur Congress, the Swiss Tibetan Women’s Association, and The Church of Almighty God. The demonstration called on the international community to oppose China’s recently enacted “Ethnic Unity Law.” The event began with an opening ceremony featuring addresses by Thinlay Chukki, Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama to Central and Eastern Europe, and Venerable Khenpo Tenzin Jangchup of Rikon Monastery. Thomas Buchli, President of GSTF, read a statement issued by the Swiss Parliamentary Group for Tibet, while Pema Dhakyel, Spokesperson of the Tibetan Youth Association in Europe, delivered the organisers’ joint press statement on the new ethnic law. Representatives of the World Uyghur Congress, the Swiss Tibetan Women’s Association, and The Church of Almighty God also expressed their grave concerns over China’s “Ethnic Unity Law,” describing it as a policy that threatens the cultural, linguistic, and religious identities of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and other ethnic minorities. Representative Thinlay Chukki mentioned that: “We have also seen the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights call for the repeal of this law because it is clear that this legislation is not intended to promote unity. Rather, it is designed to facilitate the complete erasure and forced assimilation of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and other so-called ethnic minorities. Today, I also stand in solidarity with the more than 157 Tibetans who have self-immolated in Tibet, calling for the return of His Holiness the Dalai Lama and for freedom in Tibet. Today, I stand with the Tibetan Community of Switzerland and Liechtenstein and with non-governmental organizations around the world that are calling for the repeal, rejection, and opposition of this law. As our political leader, President Penpa Tsering, has urged in his recent appeal to governments around the world, it is high time for the international community to break its silence. It is time to call for freedom in Tibet, to stand with the Uyghur people, and to take meaningful action against the Chinese government’s assimilation policies targeting ethnic minorities. It is also time for the international community to fulfill the responsibilities it has pledged to uphold under international law and various human rights conventions by demanding accountability from China for the human rights violations it continues to perpetrate in Tibet and the Uyghur regions. It is time for parliamentary groups around the world—such as the Parliamentary Group for Tibet in Switzerland, the Parliamentary Group for Tibet in the Czech Republic, and the Parliamentary Group for Tibet in Italy—to stand together in opposing this law and to call unequivocally for its repeal. On behalf of the Central Tibetan Administration, I express my sincere gratitude to all of you who have gathered here today to demand the repeal of this law and to stand for human rights, justice, and humanity. Once again, I say that this law is not aimed at unity. This law is not aimed at progress. This law is aimed at forced assimilation. This law is aimed at the complete erasure and cultural genocide of Tibetans and other ethnic minorities. Perhaps most alarming of all, this law seeks to silence not only Tibetans and Uyghurs but also those around the world who stand in solidarity with them. Through its claim of extraterritorial jurisdiction, the law attempts to legitimize the transnational repression that China carries out beyond its borders—not only against Tibetans and Uyghurs, but also against Swiss, Germans, Italians, Czechs, and people everywhere who stand with Tibet, who stand for human rights, and who stand for freedom. Therefore, I once again say that it is high time for the international community to reflect seriously, assume its responsibility, and call unequivocally for the repeal of this law.” More than 400 people, including Phuntsok Topgyal, UN Advocacy Officer from the Tibet Bureau, participated in the peaceful demonstration. Participants marched through the streets of Zurich to the Chinese Consulate General, urging the international community to reject the legislation and take concrete action to protect the human rights and fundamental freedoms of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and other affected communities. The demonstration concluded with a renewed call on governments, international organisations, and parliamentarians to oppose China’s assimilation policies and advocate for the repeal of the “Ethnic Unity Law.”

title: Tibetan Community in Austria Holds Peaceful Protest in Vienna Against China’s New Ethnic Unity Law
author: oot_admin
content: The Tibetan Community in Austria, together with members of V-TAG Austria and Students for a Free Tibet (SFT) Austria, held a peaceful protest outside the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Vienna on 1 July 2026, as the China’s Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress came into force. Participants expressed concern that the new law could further reinforce policies of cultural, linguistic, and ideological assimilation in Tibet. Protesters carried Tibetan flags, banners, and placards calling for human rights, religious freedom, and the protection of Tibetan identity. Addressing the gathering, Dhundup, President of the Tibetan Community in Austria, said the law poses a serious threat to the identity, language, religion, and cultural heritage of the Tibetan people. He said it formalises coercive assimilation policies under the banner of national unity. Dhundup also noted that, according to the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), the law conflicts with the principle of ethnic regional autonomy under the Constitution of the People’s Republic of China and with international human rights standards. He called on the international community to monitor its implementation closely. Norzi, a member of Students for a Free Tibet (SFT) Austria, briefly spoke about the impact of the new policy, warning that it could further restrict the Tibetan language and culture. She urged continued support for Tibetans and greater awareness of the situation. The protest remained peaceful throughout, with participants chanting slogans in support of Tibet and calling for respect for human rights and cultural diversity. Organisers said the event aimed to raise awareness of the law’s implications and encourage international attention to the situation in Tibet. The demonstration concluded peacefully with a renewed appeal to governments, international institutions, and human rights organisations to stand with the Tibetan people and defend their rights, dignity, and cultural identity.

title: Protest Held Outside Chinese Embassy in Berlin Against China’s New Ethnic Unity Law
author: oot_admin
content: Representatives of the Tibetan Community in Germany (Verein der Tibeter in Deutschland e.V.), Tibet Initiative Deutschland, the Society for Threatened Peoples (Gesellschaft für bedrohte Völker), together with members of the Uyghur and Hong Kong communities, held a peaceful protest outside the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Berlin on Wednesday, 1 July 2026, marking the day China’s Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress officially entered into force. The demonstration was organised to express opposition to the new legislation, which participants described as a legal instrument that strengthens state control over ethnic minorities while accelerating policies of forced assimilation. Protesters argued that the law threatens the cultural, linguistic, religious, and historical identities of Tibetans, Uyghurs, Southern Mongolians, and other ethnic communities living under Chinese rule. Addressing the gathering, Dundup Donka, President of the Tibetan Community in Germany, stated that the legislation represents a serious violation of internationally recognised human rights principles. He said the law should not be viewed as a measure promoting ethnic unity, but rather as a mechanism designed to institutionalise assimilation policies and further restrict the fundamental rights and freedoms of minority peoples. He warned that its implementation could contribute to the continued erosion of minority languages, cultures, traditions, and religious practices. Speakers representing the Uyghur and Hong Kong communities also voiced concern over the implications of the legislation, stating that it further consolidates state authority over ethnic and cultural expression while limiting the ability of minority communities to preserve their distinct identities. During the demonstration, participants called upon the Federal Government of Germany, the European Union, the United Nations, and the international human rights community to take a clear and principled position regarding the new law. They urged democratic governments and international institutions to intensify diplomatic engagement with the People’s Republic of China, advocate for the protection of ethnic minority rights, and call for the repeal of legislation that, in their view, undermines internationally recognised human rights standards. The organisers further appealed to the international community not to remain silent in the face of ongoing human rights concerns affecting Tibetans, Uyghurs, Hong Kongers, Southern Mongolians, and other ethnic minorities. They stressed the importance of sustained international attention and accountability to safeguard the rights to cultural identity, religious freedom, linguistic diversity, and self-expression.

title: States Condemn China’s Human Rights Violations and Raise Alarm Over ‘Ethnic Unity Law’ at the 62nd Session of UNHRC
author: oot_admin
content: The United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and the Czech Republic expressed continued concern over the human rights situation in Tibet, East Turkestan and Hong Kong during the 62nd Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC), warning that it could serve as a mechanism for forced assimilation and further restrict the rights of ethnic and religious minorities. The United Kingdom noted that, four years after the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) released its assessment on East Turkestan, China has yet to implement its recommendations. It stated that human rights violations in Tibet and East Turkestan continue and expressed support for OHCHR’s efforts to assess the impact of the Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress on the rights of ethnic and religious minorities. Canada expressed concern over China’s Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress and called for full respect for the human rights of ethnic and religious minorities. Australia reiterated its grave concern over ongoing human rights violations in Tibet and East Turkestan, as well as the continued erosion of rights and freedoms in Hong Kong. It also highlighted the human rights implications of China’s Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress. Referring to the reported 78 per cent increase in global executions in 2025, Australia further called on all States to abolish the death penalty. The Czech Republic reaffirmed its serious concern over the human rights situation in China, including in Hong Kong, East Turkestan, and Tibet. It emphasised that the PRC’s Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress, adopted earlier this year, raises significant concerns about facilitating the forced assimilation of ethnic minorities across China. Addressing the High Commissioner, the Czech Republic asked,“Mr. High Commissioner, where do you see the greatest added value of OHCHR engagement in preventing further deterioration of this situation?” Following the interventions by several Member States, China swiftly rejected the concerns as “false and unfounded”, refusing to acknowledge or engage with the allegations raised. Representative Thinlay Chukki welcomed the principled statements delivered by the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and the Czech Republic, noting their shared concern over the continuing human rights situation in East Turkestan, Tibet, and Hong Kong, as well as the implications of China’s Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress. She observed that the convergence of these interventions reflects growing international concern that the law may institutionalise forced assimilation and further undermine the cultural, linguistic, religious, and identity rights of ethnic and religious minorities. Responding to China’s Right of Reply, Representative Thinlay Chukki stated that dismissing concerns raised by Member States does not address the substantive human rights issues documented by the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights and other UN human rights mechanisms. She emphasised that meaningful engagement with the Human Rights Council requires constructive dialogue, transparency, and accountability. She further underscored the importance of sustained OHCHR monitoring, independent reporting, and continued international engagement to help prevent further deterioration of the human rights situation and to uphold China’s obligations under international human rights law.

title: Former Hungarian MP Ferenc József Gelencsér Condemns China’s New Ethnic Unity Law, Warns of Forced Assimilation
author: oot_admin
content: Ferenc József Gelencsér, Hungarian politician, Former member of Parliament, and leader of the Momentum Movement, hasexpressed deep concernover China’s newly adopted law promoting “unity and progress” among ethnic groups, warning that its true purpose is not inclusion but the institutionalisation of forced assimilation. “Today, China has introduced a new law promoting ‘unity and progress’ among ethnic groups. On paper, the language of this law may sound harmless. Unity, progress, and harmony between peoples are values that no one would normally reject. However, we must look beyond the language and examine the political reality,” Gelencsér stated. He argued that the legislation is “not a law about genuine equality among peoples” but rather “a law that gives legal form to forced assimilation.” According to Gelencsér, for Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, and other non-Han peoples living under the rule of the People’s Republic of China, language, religion, history, education, and culture are the foundations of their survival. “When a state uses the language of unity to weaken these foundations, it is not protecting diversity—it is replacing diversity with uniformity,” he said. Gelencsér noted that the law places the concept of a single Chinese national identity at the centre of ethnic policy. In practice, he warned, this means that Tibetan, Uyghur, Mongolian, and other ethnic identities are tolerated only to the extent that they are subordinated to a state-defined national identity shaped by the Chinese Communist Party. He highlighted particular concerns over education and language policy, arguing that the promotion of Mandarin Chinese at the expense of minority languages is not a neutral administrative measure. “When children are gradually separated from their mother tongue, they are also separated from their history, their culture, and their community,” he said. Turning to Tibet, Gelencsér emphasised that Tibetan identity cannot be separated from Tibetan Buddhism, monasteries, the spiritual authority of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, and the continuity of Tibetan cultural memory. “Any attempt by the Chinese state to control, redefine, or subordinate these traditions is not merely cultural policy—it is political control,” he stated. Gelencsér also raised concerns about the potential extraterritorial implications of the new legislation, warning that Beijing increasingly claims the authority to act against individuals and organisations outside China if they are accused of undermining ethnic unity or promoting separatism. He said this sends “a clear message to diaspora communities: even outside China’s borders, speaking up for Tibetan, Uyghur, or Mongolian identity may be treated as a threat.” According to Gelencsér, the legislation reflects a broader authoritarian strategy. “First redefine identity, then criminalise dissent, and finally silence communities both at home and abroad,” he said. He stressed that unity cannot be achieved by erasing differences, nor can stability be built by forcing people to abandon their language, religion, and culture. “Progress cannot be built on fear,” he added. Calling on the international community to respond, Gelencsér said the law should be recognised for what it is: “a tool of forced assimilation that threatens the cultural survival of Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, and all communities whose identities are being pushed into silence.” He further emphasised that “cultural survival is not separatism. Speaking one’s mother tongue is not extremism. Practicing one’s religion is not a threat to national security. Defending human rights is not interference in China’s territorial integrity—it is a universal moral and legal obligation.” “If China truly believes this law is only about unity, then it should have no reason to fear independent Tibetan culture, Uyghur language education, Mongolians preserving their heritage, or Buddhists practicing their religion freely,” Gelencsér concluded. Echoing these concerns, Representative Thinlay Chukki emphasised that the preservation of Tibetan identity, language, religion, and culture is inseparable from the protection of fundamental human rights. She called on democratic governments and international institutions to remain vigilant against policies of forced assimilation and to stand in solidarity with Tibetans and all communities whose cultural heritage and freedoms are under increasing pressure.

title: German Parliamentary State Secretary Michael Brand Urges Repeal of China’s “Ethnic Unity Law,” Warns of Threat to Tibetan Ancient Cultures
author: oot_admin
content: Hon. Michael Brand, Member of the German Parliament and Parliamentary State Secretary to the German Government, has issued a strongly worded video statement condemning China’s new “Ethnic Unity Law.” In his message, he called on people around the world to join the protest and urge China’s leaders to repeal what he described as a racist attack on ancient cultures and peoples. In his video statement, Michael Brand said: ” China is tumbling into a new level of extreme racism, posing a threat not only to the citizens of China but also to the wider region and the world. China’s so-called “Ethnic Unity Law” is one of the most racist pieces of legislation enacted since the end of World War II. Its foundation is Han Chinese extremism, and its goal is the extinction of non-Chinese peoples and nations numbering in the millions across China and beyond. The world must not remain silent in the face of this repressive and coercive attempt to erode the thousand-year-old Tibetan culture, the Uyghur people, and other historic nations and peoples. If China succeeds in implementing this policy, this racist concept could become an example for other countries around the world. As a result, hundreds of millions of people and their cultures could be threatened with extinction. Like the European Parliament in April and the Czech Senate in March, we categorically condemn this racist legislation. Experts have warned against it, and the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights has called for its repeal as recently as June 2026. Please join our protest and urge China’s leaders to repeal this racist attack on ancient cultures and peoples.” In this regard Sikyong Penpa Tsering has issued an urgent global appeal to governments, foreign ministries, parliamentarians, think tanks, and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) worldwide through official correspondence and virtual distribution, calling for repeal of the law. The German foreign ministry has also expressed great concern about the law noting that it poses “a risk of transnational repression” and that the German government “resolutely opposes any form of transnational repression, regardless of its origin.” Representative Thinlay Chukki welcomed the statement and said: “Hon’ble Michael Brand’s statement reflects a growing international recognition of the serious consequences of China’s policies in Tibet. By identifying this law as part of a broader effort to undermine Tibetan identity, language, and culture, it underscores the urgent need for sustained international attention and action. We call on parliamentarians and governments around the world to stand in support of the fundamental rights, dignity, and unique cultural heritage of the Tibetan people and all communities facing similar threats.”

title: アリヤ・ツェワン・ギャルポ代表、東京の人文学フォーラムで在日中国人らと対話
author: Tashi Yangzom
content: 東京：中国系の学術シンクタンクである「東京人文学論壇（Tokyo Humanities Forum）」は、「世界平和のための中国とチベット」をテーマにした講演および討論会を開催し、8月16日に東京都新宿区（早稲田町）の会場へ、ダライ・ラマ法王日本・東アジア代表部事務所の代表であるアリヤ・ツェワン・ギャルポ博士を招き、講演を行った。 フォーラムの幹事長であり、亡命中の中国の人権派弁護士である李金星（リー・ジンシン）氏が、日中の参加者およびメディア関係者を歓迎した。同氏はアリヤ代表を聴衆に紹介し、中国チベット問題およびその解決の必要性について簡潔に説明した。 アリヤ代表は、中国コミュニティと直接対話する機会を提供してくれた主催者に謝意を述べた。この対話が、中国共産党（CCP）体制が両コミュニティの間に作り出してきた多くの疑念や誤解を解く助けとなるからだ。 代表は、亡命中のチベット人、中国人、ウイグル人、南モンゴル人、香港人が、自由、民主主義、正義の追求において皆同じ立場にあり、この目的の一体性こそが、母国における弾圧や不正義と闘うために団結の力となるべきであると語った。また、チベット人は、天安門広場の中国人学生の要求や闘争、ノーベル平和賞受賞者である劉暁波氏らによる「08憲章」の請願、2020年の香港デモ参加者の要求、そして2022年の「白紙革命」を通じた中国の人々の要求に連帯を感じていると述べた。 さらに、中国の人々とチベットの人々の要求は同じであり、それらの要求は中国憲法の枠内のものであるにもかかわらず、中国共産党政権が国家憲法を踏みにじっていると詳説した。そして、ダライ・ラマ法王とチベット亡命政府が掲げる「中道アプローチ」は、中国チベット問題の解決だけでなく、中国とチベットが世界平和と安定の推進においてより大きな役割を果たすことを可能にするものであると語った。 40名を超える日中の学者や知識人が討論に参加し、チベットの自治の性質、ダライ・ラマ法王の転生とその後の影響、中国の民族団結法とその進展、焼身抗議などについて質問を投げかけた。中国の民主化後にチベット人は独立を主張しないのかという質問に対し、アリヤ代表は、「まず畑を手に入れずして、収穫の取り分を議論するのは時期尚早であり、本質的ではない」と回答した。 中国人の参加者からは、今回のイベントを通じてチベット人の視点や願いがより明確に理解できたこと、またチベット人は中国共産党政権が描くような反中・反中国人ではないことが分かったとして、主催者に対し同様のイベントの継続を求める声があがった。 会場では、アリヤ・ツェワン・ギャルポ代表の著作の『チベットの反論』の中国語版や、中道アプローチに関する書籍、植民地的寄宿制学校に関する報告書が参加者に配布された。また、台湾のチベット事務所は、ダライ・ラマ法王の著作『声なきものの声』の中国語版を数冊、イベントに際して寄贈した。 通訳は浦氏が務め、チベットハウス・ジャパンのチサ・ツェラ氏が司会進行および参加者への書籍配布の調整を補佐した。当日の討論の様子はこちら。 ――ダライ・ラマ法王日本代表部事務所による報告

title: アリヤ・ツェワン・ギャルポ代表、1週間のフィリピン訪問を終了
author: Tashi Yangzom
content: マニラ：ダライ・ラマ法王日本・東アジア代表部事務所のアリヤ・ツェワン・ギャルポ代表は、フィリピン公式訪問を終えた。一週間に及ぶ滞在中、ダライ・ラマ法王の生涯と使命に関する写真展と一連の講演会、ファー・イースタン大学およびフィリピン大学アジアセンターでのチベットについての講演、フィリピン国会議員らとの面会、マニラ市内での異宗教間対話への参加など精力的な活動を展開した。 チベットハウス・ジャパンは、ラモン・マグサイサイ賞財団（RMAF）との共催で、8月22日から25日まで同財団ホールにてダライ・ラマ法王の生涯と使命に関する4日間の写真展と講演会を開催した。財団の特別賓客をはじめ、学者、芸術家、学生、一般市民など多くの人々が会場を訪れ、講演を聞き、質疑応答に参加した。RMAFのスザンナ・B・アファン会長は開会の辞で聴衆を歓迎し、同財団とチベットの長年の関係、2003年および2004年のダライ・ラマ法王への謁見や平和と非暴力のメッセージについて語った。 アリヤ・ツェワン・ギャルポ代表は、写真展や講演会の開催にあたり温かいサポートをしてくれた財団へ謝意を表明した。また、1959年に同財団からダライ・ラマ法王に対するリーダーシップ賞の授与が、当時チベットで起きていたことへの関心を高めるうえで大いに役立ったことにも感謝の意を表した。さらに、1960年代初頭に国連でチベット問題が取り上げられた際におけるフィリピン政府と国民の支援にも謝辞を述べた。代表は来賓や学者、一般市民に対し、チベット問題を説明するとともに、ダライ・ラマ法王の4つの使命（人間の価値の促進、宗教間の調和の促進、チベット文化の保存、古代インドのナランダ仏教教学の復興）について詳しく述べ、これらすべての使命が、普遍的な責任感を伴う国際社会の実現に向けられていることを解説した。 写真展および講演会の開会式では、市内のニンマ派およびカギュ派のチベット人僧侶らが祈りの読誦を行った。 財団は書籍『He Will Be Called Great: The Life of H.H. the 14th Dalai Lama』を発行した。同書は著名な女優兼演劇アーティストであるセシリア・B・ガルチョによって聴衆に朗読された。この書籍は、世界中の子どもたちに偉大な指導者を紹介するため、マグサイサイ賞受賞者の生涯を扱ったシリーズの一環である。 財団は、アリヤ代表とフィリピン・イスラムと民主主義センターのアミナ・ラスル＝ベルナルド会長を招き、「異宗教間の調和と共通の人間性に関する議論」を開催した。アルジャジーラのジャーナリストであるジャメラ・アリンドガンが司会を務めた。議論は主要宗教間における宗教的調和と対話の重要性や、宗教的調和の促進におけるダライ・ラマ法王の役割と貢献に焦点を当てた。登壇者らは、中国共産党政権が無神論でありながら宗教に介入し、宗教的弾圧を正当化するための宗教法を制定している実態について議論した。 アリヤ代表は、ファー・イースタン大学とフィリピン大学アジアセンターでそれぞれ講演を行い、学生や教職員とチベット問題、ダライ・ラマ法王の使命、両国の関係について意見を交わした。学生たちに対し、チベットの政治史や中国共産党による不法占領の経緯を説明し、1960年代初頭の国連総会におけるチベット問題の審議でフィリピンの国民と政府が示した支援に謝意を表した。さらに、学生たちに向けてグローバルな視点を持つよう促し、世界の平和と調和に対するフィリピンの貢献の可能性について語った。学生からは、ダライ・ラマの転生、中道アプローチ、国連の役割などについて質問が寄せられた。講演の様子はこちら。 ファー・イースタン大学のレックス・ロノラ教授は、チベット問題に関する有益な講演を行った代表に謝意を表した。フィリピン大学アジアセンター学部長のノエル・クリスチャン・モラティラ博士とアリエル・ロペス教授は、チベット問題に関する多角的な講演に対して感謝を述べ、アリヤ代表に感謝状を贈呈した。両大学は、インドの中央チベット政権（CTA）の情報・国際関係省（DIIR）およびチベット政策研究所（TPI）を通じてチベット問題に関する書籍を寄贈してくれたチベットハウス・ジャパンに謝意を表明した。 8月25日、アリヤ代表はフィリピン・イスラムと民主主義センターのアミナ・ラスル＝ベルナルドとともに、ポッドキャスト番組「She Talks Peace」に出演し、ダライ・ラマ法王、チベットの平和的な闘争、世界へのメッセージをテーマに議論を行った。質問に対し、アリヤ代表はダライ・ラマ法王のマルクス主義に対する見解、慈悲、中道アプローチ、そしてモンゴルの元朝、中国の明朝、満州の清朝の時代にチベットが平和と調和の促進にいかに貢献したかを説明した。また、信教の自由の侵害や、中国およびその支配地域における主要宗教の指導者選出に対する中国の強引な介入について視聴者に伝えた。 8月27日、フィリピン国会議事堂の儀典官はアリヤ代表とタシ・ヤンゾム事務局長に対し、議事堂の公式案内を行った。その後、エウヘニオ・ペレス・ラウンジにおいて、エイドリアン・アマトン、ルーファス・ロドリゲス、ダダ・イスムラ、ペルシ・センダナの各下院議員が両名を迎え、最近の「中国民族団結進歩促進法」や殉国者ロブガ・ランゼンの焼身自殺について協議した。また、チベット仏教機関の信教の自由と自治を保護するため議員らが提案した議会法案や、両国議会間の議員連盟の設立についても話し合われた。チベット亡命議会のドルマ・ツェリング・テイカン議長からの、「中国民族団結進歩促進法」の過酷さを訴える嘆願書が議員らに提出された。 8日間にわたる日程は8月28日に締めくくられた。ダライ・ラマ法王日本・東アジア代表部事務所のタシ・ヤンゾム事務局長がアリヤ代表に同行し、写真展や講演会、書籍の配布の調整を補佐した。 ――ダライ・ラマ法王日本・東アジア代表部事務所による報告

title: ダライ・ラマ法王、キロン・ラスワ国境沿いの甚大な洪水被害に際し哀悼の意を表明
author: Tashi Yangzom
content: ネパールのラスワ地域およびチベットのキロンにおける大洪水により、尊い人命が失われ、建物に甚大な被害が出たとの報に接し、深く心を痛めております。犠牲となられたすべての方々に祈りを捧げるとともに、遺族の皆様、そしてこの悲劇に見舞われたすべての被災者の方々に、心からお見舞いと哀悼の意を表明いたします。 同地域では過去にも災害が発生していることから、これらは気候変動であれその他の要因であれ、間違いなくより根深い原因の表れに他なりません。今後こうした災害が二度と繰り返されないよう、可能な限りの適切な対策が講じられることを切に願います。

title: プレスリリース
author: Tashi Yangzom
content: これまでにさまざまな報道チャンネルやネパール現地のチベット人居住区事務所を通じて得た情報によると、チベットとネパールの国境にあるラデプ（レンデ川）を襲った鉄砲水により甚大な被害が発生し、チベット側のキロン（吉隆）およびネパールのラスワ郡において、川沿いの多数の家屋が流されました。1,500人を超える人々が死亡、負傷、または行方不明と報じられており、甚大な被害をもたらしています。 防犯カメラの映像やメディアを通じて拡散している個人の動画クリップによれば、キロン（国境）ゲートだけでも、洪水が一瞬にして家屋や数百人もの人々を押し流していました。中国政府は死者数の発表を渋った後、丸一日経った本日になって死者3人、行方不明者または安否不明者558人と発表しました。そのうち約260人はチベット内に滞在していた外国人であるとされていますが、詳細な情報は依然として不明です。 ネパールを拠点とするシャワラスム・チベット人居住区事務所の管轄内では、ネパール政府が、シャブル集落、近隣のシャブル市場、およびキロン国境のティムレを、今回の洪水によって最も大きな被害を受けた地域として認定しています。 同地域には、点在する5つのチベット人集落・コミュニティがあります。 今朝の報道によると、ネパール政府は6人のチベット人を救助できたとのことですが、この情報は現在確認中です。 ネパールでは広い範囲で甚大な被害が出ており、現時点で少なくとも165人が死亡、826人が行方不明となっています。 この未曾有の洪水により、チベットとネパール全体で、800人を超える外国人を含む、1,500人以上の人々が死亡または行方不明となっています。 ダライ・ラマ法王は五十年以上にわたり、地球環境全般、そして特にチベットの自然環境を保護する必要性について繰り返し説いてきました。中央チベット政権がチベットの環境問題について、国際社会への注意喚起を一貫して取り組み続けておりますが、これに呼応した環境保護団体はごく少数にすぎず、関係各国が十分な懸念を表明することは依然として稀です。 チベット高原において、中国政府は開発を口実にさまざまな環境破壊活動を行っており、気温の上昇を倍の速度で引き起こしています。現在、中国政府は「グリーン」エネルギー源と称して、貯水池やダムの建設、太陽光発電事業、鉄道接続事業など、ヒマラヤ山脈全域にわたるプロジェクトを公然かつ容赦なく拡大しています。これらの無責任な行為は、人類全体に深刻な悪影響をもたらしています。さらなる重大な危機につながりかねない状況に直面する今、沈黙してよい時ではありません。 本日、ダライ・ラマ法王はラダックから、チベットおよびネパールの洪水災害の被災者に向けて祈りを捧げました。法王は、この先このような災禍が再び起こることのないよう、同地域の自然環境を保護し大切にするよう強く求めました。 中央チベット政権は、今回の洪水災害によるすべての被災者（生存者および犠牲者）に対し、心からの哀悼の意を表し、連帯を表明します。本日、テチェン・チョリング寺院で開催された祈祷会において、我々は負傷者の速やかな回復、亡くされた方々の解脱、そして遺族が苦しみから解放されることを祈念いたします。 中央チベット政権は、関係事務所および関係者に対し、遅滞なく緊急救援活動を行うよう指示を出しました。 同様に、シャワラサム・チベット人居住区内のチベット人居住地域における被災者を支援するため、またネパール政府および国民に対する連帯と哀悼の意を表すため、中央チベット政権の救援活動を支援するよう、亡命チベット人の皆様に対しそれぞれのチベット事務所およびチベット人居住区事務所を通じて自発的な寄付を行うよう呼びかけます。

title: 在日チベット人およびチベット支援者ら、故ロブガ・ランゼン氏を追悼する四十九日法要を執り行う
author: Tashi Yangzom
content: 東京：チベットハウス・ジャパンは8月23日、東京の事務所で追悼法要を執り行った。2026年7月2日にニューヨークの国連本部前で身を焼いて抗議し、命を落とした殉教者パウォ・ロブガ・ランゼン氏の四十九日を迎えたためである。同氏は、中国政府の弾圧政策や、チベットのアイデンティティ、文化、伝統を消し去ろうとする動きに抗議して命を捧げた。 法要には、東京周辺からチベット人と日本の支援者ら35人が参列した。集会は、殉教者ロブガ・ランゼン氏と、チベットの大義のために命を捧げたすべてのチベット人への追悼の意を込め、1分間の黙祷から始まった。 チベット・ハウス・ジャパンのチサ・ツェラ氏が挨拶に立ち、チベット亡命政府（カシャック）の声明を発表して参列者に配布した。また、2009年以降、抗議のため焼身自殺を図った157人のチベット人の犠牲に言及した。同じくチベット・ハウス・ジャパンの高松海氏が、声明の内容と集会の趣旨を日本語で解説した。 ステューデンツ・フォー・フリーチベット・ジャパン（SFTJ）のツェリン・ドルジェ代表は、8月22日に自身とテンジン・チュジン氏が東京で行った24時間のハンガーストライキについて参列者に報告した。SFTJが主催したこの抗議活動は、中国のいわゆる「民族団結進歩促進法」に反対するため、渋谷の国連大学前で実施された。 二人は一般市民と対話し、新法に対する懸念や、チベット人その他の民族コミュニティに及ぼす影響について訴えた。抗議活動の締めくくりとして、焼身抗議を行ったチベット人たちへの連帯の意思表示として、ツェリン・ドルジェ氏は自身の頭髪を剃り落とした。 ツェリン・ドルジェ氏は、チベット・ハウス・ジャパンのツェラ氏、日本の支援者たち、そしてハンガーストライキの現場を訪れてカタ（チベットの伝統的なスカーフ）を捧げ、連帯を表明してくれたチベットコミュニティのメンバーに謝意を述べた。 チベット・ハウス・ジャパンでの祈念集会は、ロサン・イシ氏が導師による1時間の法要をもって締めくくられた。参列者らは、ロブガ・ランゼン氏および命を捧げたすべてのチベット人の魂の平安を祈り、遺族に対して心からの哀悼の意を捧げた。 ――ダライ・ラマ法王日本代表部事務所による報告

title: ダライ・ラマ法王日本代表部事務所代表ご挨拶
author: Tashi Yangzom
content: 日本に戻って来たことを大変嬉しく思います。この度、ダライ・ラマ法王日本代表部事務所の新代表に任命されたことを大変光栄に思うと同時に、非常に重い責任を感じております。 私は大学卒業後、チベット亡命政権の公務員として主に情報・国際関係省,カシャック(内閣)の対策委員会、選挙管理委員会に勤めました。 日本は、私にとって大変親しみのある国です。2016年に長野県の西方寺の金子英昭ご住職が留学生として受け入れてくださって、日本語と日本文化を勉学する貴重な機会をいただきました。その結果、2017-2021年、ダライ・ラマ法王日本代表部事務所の事務局長として勤めることができたのです。この場をお借りして、チベットに深い関心を寄せ、日本とチベットの絆を育むチベット人材育成に貢献なさっている金子先生に心より感謝申し上げます。 歴史を辿ると、チベットと日本は仏教国として古代より共通した部分が多くあります。6～7世紀頃、日本では聖徳太子が、チベットではソンツェン・ガンポ王が、それぞれ憲法を定め、道徳と倫理を国家の指導理念にしたといわれています。また、20世紀初頭から仏教と文化面で親密な交流があったことについても心に留める価値があると思います。 我々チベット人は古代より守り続けてきた固有の文化、宗教、言語、民族アイデンティティを大変誇りに思っております。また、チベットは緩衝国としてアジアの平和を維持してきました。チベット高原はアジアの多くの大河の源であり、数億人の生活を支えています。また、大量の氷河や雪氷が蓄えられているチベット高原は地球の第三極とみなされ、地球の気候と生態を守る重要な役割を果たしてきました。 しかし、1950年に中国に軍事的侵略されて以来、チベットでは、独自の文化、宗教、言語、民族アイデンティティーを消滅させる同化政策が進んでいます。同時に、中国政府による無謀なインフラ開発、大規模な資源採掘、水力発電事業がチベット高原の生態系を破壊するだけでなく、下流域の国々において、洪水や干ばつの危険を発生し、アジア大陸の水安全保障に対する直接的な脅威ともなり続けています。 今日、我々チベット人が深刻に懸念しているのは、中国政府が進めている強制的同化政策の法制化であります。今年7月1日に施行された「民族団結進歩促進法」は、中国政府は民族の団結と社会的調和を強化するものだと主張していますが、実際には「民族の団結」の名目の下でチベット、ウィグル、モンゴルなどの人々から固有の言語、文化、宗教、アイデンティティを奪い、漢民族に同化させるための包括的な法的根拠とするものです。この新法の施行に先立ち、チベット内にいる子どもの約8割（約80万人）が家族から強制的に引き離されて寄宿学校に送られ、中国標準語での教育が義務付けられています。これによって、世代全体の独自の言語、文化、宗教的アイデンティティが根絶されようとしています。更に、この新法には中国国外にいる人権活動家、研究者、チベット人らを追及する条項も含まれており、他国の主権を脅かす国境を越えた抑圧となることが指摘されています。 民主主義、自由、正義を尊重する国際社会が連携して、この新法に強く抵抗し、撤廃を呼びかけています。日本においても、超党派の四つの議員連盟が中国のこの法律を「民主国家として到底容認できない」と厳しく非難する声明を発表されました。このような声明が中国共産党政権による弾圧と迫害に苦しむチベット国内のチベット人達に、希望と励みを与えるのです。この力強いご支持に深く感謝を申し上げます。 ダライ・ラマ法王のご指導の元、チベット人達は自らの言語、宗教、文化、そして民族としてのアイデンティティを維持し続けることができています。これは、自由と正義を重んじる国際社会の支援なしには成し得なかったことです。チベット本土においても、我々の同朋たちが自らのアイデンティティを大切にし、守り抜こうとする勇気と決意は揺るぎないものであり、それこそが私たちの活動の原動力となっているのです。 チベット亡命政権は、中国政府との対話を通じてチベットの真の自治を求める「中道政策」を堅持しています。ダライ・ラマ法王には、主に四つの使命があります。それは、1）思いやり、寛容、許しといった普遍的価値の促進、2）世界の主要な宗教の間における相互尊重と理解の促進、3）チベット独自の仏教的遺産、言語、そして自然環境の保全、4）古代インドの英知の復興、です。 このダライ・ラマ法王の使命とチベット中央政権の方針に沿って、私は日本の人々、政治家の皆様、メディアにチベット問題への理解を深めていただけるよう、全力を尽くしてまいります。お一人でも多くの日本の方々から理解と支援をいただくことが、チベット問題の解決に向けた大きな力となります。 ダライ・ラマ法王日本代表部事務所（チベット・ハウス・ジャパン）の活動が今日まで成果を上げてこられたのは、多くの支援者やボランティアの皆様のおかげです。私、およびスタッフ一同、チベットと日本の友好および文化交流をさらに促進すべく努力を続けてまいりますので、今後とも温かいご支援とご協力を賜りますよう、心よりお願い申し上げます。 2026年10月９ダライ・ラマ法王日本代表部事務所代表：ロブサン・チョダ Tashi Delek. Konnichiwa. I am happy to come back to Japan. I am deeply honoured to have been appointed the new Representative of the Liaison Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama in Japan and East Asia, and at the same time I feel a heavy sense of responsibility. After graduating from university, I served as a civil servant in the Central Tibetan Administration, working mainly in the Department of Information and International Relations, the Kashag Secretariat (Cabinet) Permanent Strategy Committee, and the Election Commission. Japan is a country close to my heart. In 2016, I received the precious opportunity to study the Japanese language and culture because of the generous support from Reverend Hideaki Kaneko, head priest of Saihoji Temple in Nagano Prefecture. As a result, I was able to serve as Secretary of the Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama in Japan from 2017 to 2021. I would like to take this opportunity to express my heartfelt gratitude to Rev. Kaneko, who has taken a deep interest in Tibet and has contributed to nurturing Tibetan human resources who foster the bonds between Japan and Tibet. Looking back through history, Tibet and Japan, as Buddhist nations, have shared much in common since ancient times. It is said that around the 6th and 7th centuries, Prince Shotoku in Japan and King Songtsen Gampo in Tibet each established a constitution and made morality and ethics the guiding principles of their nations. It is also worth remembering that the two countries enjoyed close Buddhist and cultural exchanges from the early twentieth century onward. We Tibetans take great pride in our distinct culture, religion, language, and national identity that we have preserved since ancient times. Historically, as an independent nation, Tibet has played a vital role in maintaining peace and harmony in Asia as a buffer state. Moreover, the Tibetan Plateau is the source of many of Asia’s great rivers and sustains the lives of hundreds of millions of people. Moreover, the Tibetan Plateau, which stores vast quantities of glaciers and snow and ice, is regarded as the Earth’s “Third Pole” and has played an important role in safeguarding the planet’s climate and ecology. However, since the military invasion of Tibet by the People’s Republic of China in 1950, assimilation policies aimed at eradicating Tibet’s distinct culture, religion, language, and national identity have been advancing. At the same time, reckless infrastructure development, large-scale resource extraction, and hydropower projects carried out by the Chinese government not only destroy the ecosystem of the Tibetan Plateau but also continue to pose a direct risks of floods, droughts, and water and food security in downstream countries in the Asian continent. Today, what we Tibetans are deeply concerned about is the codification into law of the forced assimilation policies pursued by the Chinese government. The “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress,” which came into effect on July 1 of this year, is claimed by the Chinese government to strengthen ethnic unity and social harmony. In reality, however, under the pretext of “ethnic unity,” it serves as a comprehensive legal basis for stripping the Tibetan, Uyghur, Mongolian, and other peoples of their distinct languages, cultures, religions, and identities, and for assimilating them into the Han Chinese majority. Shortly before this new law came into force, approximately 80 percent of children in Tibet (about 800,000) had been forcibly separated from their families and sent to colonial boarding schools, where education in Chinese language is compulsory. As a result, an entire generation of Tibetans is in danger of losing its distinct language, culture, and religious identity. Furthermore, the new law contains provisions that target human rights activists, researchers, and Tibetans living outside China, and it has been pointed out that this constitutes transnational repression that threatens the sovereignty of other nations. The international community, which values democracy, freedom, and justice, has united in strongly opposing this new law and calling for its repeal. In Japan, as a democratic nation, four cross-party parliamentary support groups issued statements strongly condemning the new law as “totally unacceptable.” It sends a strong message of hope and inspiration to Tibetans inside Tibet who suffer repression and persecution of the Chinese communist government. I would like to express my deepest gratitude for this powerful show of support. Under the guidance of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, Tibetans have been able to continue preserving their language, religion, culture, and identity as a people. This would not have been possible without the support of the international community, which values freedom and justice. In Tibet itself as well, the courage and determination of our compatriots to cherish and protect their identity remain unshakable, and this is precisely what drives our work. The Central Tibetan Administration remains firmly committed to the Middle Way Approach policy, which seeks genuine autonomy for Tibet through dialogue with the Chinese government. His Holiness the Dalai Lama has four main commitments: (1) the promotion of universal values such as compassion, tolerance, and forgiveness; (2) the promotion of mutual respect and understanding among the world’s major religious traditions; (3) the preservation of Tibetan language and culture, the Buddhist heritage, and protection of Tibet’s natural environment; and (4) the revival of ancient Indian wisdom. In keeping with these commitments of His Holiness the Dalai Lama and the policies of the Central Tibetan Administration, I will do my utmost to deepen the understanding of the Tibet issue among the people of Japan, political leaders, and the media.
