author: Dawa Sangmo
content: Canberra: His Holiness the Dalai Lama’s 90th birthday was celebrated with great enthusiasm by Tibetans, supporters, and friends of Tibet across Australia. In the Blue Mountains, to honour His Holiness the Dalai Lama on this significant occasion and to celebrate the Year of Compassion, the Tibetan community and friends of His Holiness hosted 113 Tibetan flags at various locations in the Blue Mountains City. The flag-raising ceremony was held in front of the Blue Mountains City Council and was attended by several prominent figures, including Mayor Mark Greenhill, Deputy Mayor Romola Hollywood, Federal MP Susan Templeman, State MP Trish Doyle, City Councillor Suzie Van Opdorp, Aboriginal elder Aunty Carol OAM, Tibetan MP Tenzin Phuntsok Doring, and Representative Karma Singey. Later, a formal event was held at Katoomba Public School to celebrate the occasion, where Federal MP Susan Templeman, co-chair of the Australian All-Party Parliamentary Group for Tibet, read a statement issued by the Parliamentary Friendship Group for Tibet on His Holiness’ 90th birthday. The statement expressed: “As His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama celebrates his 90th birthday this year, the Australian All-Party Parliamentary Group for Tibet would like to offer our deepest respect and heartfelt congratulations to His Holiness. We wish him a long and healthy life so he can continue to serve humanity and all sentient beings.” It further emphasised: “As Australian parliamentarians, we reiterate that the Tibetan people are entitled to their fundamental rights and freedoms, including the right to choose their own religious and spiritual leaders without government interference.” This milestone was also celebrated grandly in Sydney, Newcastle, Nowra, the Central Coast, Canberra, Brisbane, Melbourne, and other regions. Many prominent Australian parliamentarians and Tibet supporters, including Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives Hon. Sharon Claydon MP, Dr. Sophie Scamps MP, Senator Paul Scarr, Senator Penny Allman-Payne, former Senator Janet Rice, ACT Greens leader Shane Rattenbury, along with many religious and community leaders, joined Tibetan communities in their respective regions. In New Zealand, the Tibetan community in Auckland celebrated His Holiness’s birthday, attended by many prominent guests, including MPs Ingrid Leary and Helen White, Friends of Tibet, and members of the Tibetan Chinese Friendship Association. -Report filed by Tibet Information Office, Canberra

title: Statement Affirming the Continuation of the Institution of Dalai Lama
author: Dawa Sangmo
content: (Translated from the original Tibetan) On 24 September 2011, at a meeting of the heads of Tibetan spiritual traditions, I made a statement to fellow Tibetans in and outside Tibet, followers of Tibetan Buddhism, and those who have a connection with Tibet and Tibetans, regarding whether the institution of the Dalai Lama should continue. I stated, “As far back as 1969, I made clear that concerned people should decide whether the Dalai Lama’s reincarnations should continue in the future.” I also said, “When I am about ninety I will consult the high Lamas of the Tibetan Buddhist traditions, the Tibetan public, and other concerned people who follow Tibetan Buddhism, to re-evaluate whether or not the institution of the Dalai Lama should continue.” Although I have had no public discussions on this issue, over the last 14 years leaders of Tibet’s spiritual traditions, members of the Tibetan Parliament in Exile, participants in a Special General Body Meeting, members of the Central Tibetan Administration, NGOs, Buddhists from the Himalayan region, Mongolia, Buddhist republics of the Russian Federation and Buddhists in Asia including mainland China, have written to me with reasons, earnestly requesting that the institution of the Dalai Lama continue. In particular, I have received messages through various channels from Tibetans in Tibet making the same appeal. In accordance with all these requests, I am affirming that the institution of the Dalai Lama will continue. The process by which a future Dalai Lama is to be recognized has been clearly established in the 24 September 2011 statement which states that responsibility for doing so will rest exclusively with members of the Gaden Phodrang Trust, the Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. They should consult the various heads of the Tibetan Buddhist traditions and the reliable oath-bound Dharma Protectors who are linked inseparably to the lineage of the Dalai Lamas. They should accordingly carry out the procedures of search and recognition in accordance with past tradition. I hereby reiterate that the Gaden Phodrang Trust has sole authority to recognize the future reincarnation; no one else has any such authority to interfere in this matter. Dharamshala21 May 2025 https://www.dalailama.com/news/statement-affirming-the-continuation-of-the-institution-of-dalai-lama

title: Public Service Commission Begins Tibetan Language Workshop for CTA Settlement Office Secretaries
author: Palden Choedon
content: Sarah: The Public Service Commission of the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) inaugurated a ten-day Tibetan Language Workshop for Tibetan Settlement Office staff this morning at College for Higher Tibetan Studies (CHTS), Sarah. The workshop has brought together 21 CTA officials currently serving as office secretaries in various Tibetan settlement offices in India and Nepal. The inaugural ceremony was attended by Public Service Commissioner Karma Yeshi as the chief guest. Also present were CHTS Principal Passang Tsering, Public Service Commission Secretary Tenzin Legdup, and the workshop instructors, who are faculty members of the college. The programme commenced with the lighting of the traditional ceremonial butter lamp by Commissioner Karma Yeshi and Principal Passang Tsering. Following the inauguration, the participating CTA officials introduced themselves, sharing their respective settlement offices and providing the gathering with an overview of their backgrounds. Passang Tsering, Principal of CHTS, addressed the participants by highlighting the improvements made to the workshop facilities, the minor revisions to the course structure, and introducing the new batch of college faculty members assigned to conduct the sessions. He underscored the importance of teaching and learning Tibetan history, noting the growing challenge posed by false narratives promoted by some Western Tibetologists. He stressed that individuals should be well-equipped with an accurate understanding of Tibetan history so they can confidently explain and uphold the truth whenever the need arises. Speaking about the workshop’s objectives, he states that the Tibetan Language Workshop for Tibetan Settlement Offices is specifically designed to strengthen participants’ Tibetan language proficiency in relation to their current professional responsibilities. Unlike courses intended to prepare candidates for the CTA Civil Service Entrance Examination, the workshop aims to support the continuous development of Tibetan language skills throughout participants’ careers. Public Service Commissioner, Karma Yeshi, emphasised that learning is a lifelong pursuit, drawing on the Buddhist belief that knowledge and wisdom benefit an individual not only in this life but also in future lives. He stressed the enduring value of continuous learning and self-improvement. He spoke about the CTA staff Training Policy, which provides training at three different stages of a civil servant’s career. In this context, he highlighted the importance of Tibetan language proficiency, particularly in drafting official correspondence, and urged participants to pay close attention to the nuances of formal writing and avoid Tibetan spelling errors. Encouraging participants to make the most of the programme, he urged them to reflect on what they had learned and assess how much they had improved by the end of the workshop. He also stressed the importance of overall personal development, including maintaining good handwriting, noting that such qualities are especially significant for settlement office secretaries and reflect both professionalism and personal discipline. He further encouraged participants to openly share the experiences and challenges they encounter in their respective settlements among each other and to actively engage with the faculty by seeking clarification whenever they had questions or doubts. Concluding his address, Karma Yeshi reflected on the current challenges facing the Tibetan cause and His Holiness the Dalai Lama’s advancing age. He reminded CTA civil servants to remain mindful of the sacrifices made by Tibetans, while encouraging them to take care of their health, preserve Tibetan culture and language, and carry out their responsibilities with dedication. The ten-day workshop will comprise a total of 52 sessions covering Tibetan history, Tibetan grammar, official letter writing, lexicography, and phonetics.

title: Tibetans and Japanese Observe Unite for Tibet and Global Day of Action to Honour Martyr Lobga Rangzen in Tokyo
author: Palden Choedon
content: Tokyo: The Students for Free Tibet Japan and the Tibetan Community in Japan organised a function and peace march yesterday to observe the Global Day of Action to remember and honour Martyr Lobsang Palden (Lobga Rangzen), who self-immolated before the United Nations building a month ago. Tibetans and Japanese supporters gathered at Jingu-dori Park carrying Tibetan national flags and posters of Lobsang Palden. Dr. Tsewang Gyalpo Arya, Representative of the Liaison Office of H.H. the Dalai Lama for Japan and East Asia, briefed the participants on what this Global Day of Action is about and how Martyr Lobsang Palden self-immolated to protest the Chinese Ethnic Unity and Progress Law and to draw the United Nations and the international community’s attention to the Chinese heinous intention behind this Ethnic Unity Law. He urged all to remember Martyr Lobsang Palden’s words and protest the Ethnic Unity Law and the injustices happening in China and the occupied regions of Tibet, East Turkistan, Southern Mongolia and other regions. Dorjee Shiota of the Tibetan Community in Japan and Tsering Dorjee of Students for Free Tibet Japan thanked the participants and called on all Tibetans to unite and work to fulfill the last wishes of Martyr Lobsang Palden by keeping the issue of Tibet alive. Tenzin Chodon of the Students for Free Tibet read the biography of Martyr Lobsang Palden. After the function, the participants started the Peace March from Jingu-dori Park and marched around the busy Shibuya street, raising slogans for freedom and justice for Tibet, asking the United Nations to take action and urge the CCP regime to repeal the repressive law and send a fact-finding delegation to Tibet. In the afternoon, a film show and panel discussion on the Self-immolation and the Ethnic Unity Law were organised at Tokyo University Komaba Complex. A two-hour 2015 documentary film “Lungta”, directed by Ikeya Kaoru, was screened, in which the Tibetans’ struggle in Tibet and in exile and the life story of some self-immolators were delineated. Director Ikeya, during the panel discussion, talked about his experience in working with the Tibetans and the compassionate culture of Tibet. He lamented that the Tibet issue has not received much attention lately and the Tibetans are forced to self-immolate to draw the international community’s attention. Prof Ako Tomoko of the University of Tokyo moderated the panel discussion and talked about how Lobga Rangzen committed self-immolation before the UN building. She urged the international community to pay attention and do more in resolving the problems the Tibetans, Uyghurs, Southern Mongolians and other minority nationals are facing under the CCP regime. Representative Dr. Tsewang Gyalpo Arya thanked the Director Ikeya and Nakahara for the film in which Tibetan struggle and self-immolation aspects have been conveyed succinctly. He thanked Prof. Ako for her cooperation in making this film and panel discussion possible at the university. Representative Arya briefly explained why Tibetans are forced to commit self-immolation and why Martyr Lobga Rangzen burnt himself before the United Nations building. He said the worsening human rights and religious repression in Tibet, and the silence of the international community and the implementation of China’s Ethnic Unity and Progress law as major reasons that forced Lobga Rangzen to self-immolate to protest the CCP regime and to draw the United Nations’ attention. Tsering Dorjee of the Students for Tibet Japan spoke about China’s colonial boarding schools and how more than one million Tibetan children are forced into these boarding schools for indoctrination in communist ideology and are deprived of education in their mother tongue and religious culture. Fujita Yoko of the Students for Free Tibet emceed the event. Participants posed many questions to the panels on: Ethnic Law, the situation in Tibet and other occupied nationals, colonial boarding schools, India and China relations, the Tibetan middle way approach, and so on. The film screening and the panel discussion took around four hours, exceeding the time limit. Around two hundred people participated in the event at Tokyo University. Information booklets on the colonial boarding schools, Chinese interference in the selection of H.H. the Dalai Lama’s reincarnation, and Tibetan bulletins were distributed to the audience. -Report filed by the Office of Tibet, Japan

title: 43rd Tibetan Terminology Standardising Board Meeting Finalises 560 Standard Terms
author: Ngawang Tsepak
content: Dharamshala: The Tibetan Terminology Standardising Board held its 43d meeting for six days from 27 July to 1 August 2026, at the Department of Education, Central Tibetan Administration. Additional Secretary Kunga Gyaltsen from the Department of Education, the president of the Tibetan Terminology Standardising Board, along with board members Geshe Ngawang Namdol,MenrampaSonam Dolkar Oshoe, former TCV English teacher Tenzin Dargye,former director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives’ science department Karma Thubten,the secretary and a member of the Committee Urgyen Tenzin, and the Terminology section staff attended this meeting. Over the course of this meeting,a total of560 terms were finalised from the list of 700 proposed terms for application in Science, Education, Law, Politics, Economics,Accounting, Environment, and Technology. The Term Book series, up to volume 19, has been published, and a dedicated website for searching terms(www.tibterminology.net), along with application software, has been developed. This meeting was supported by DANIDA. – Report filed by Department of Education, CTA

title: Members of Parliament Geshe Lharampa Atuk Tseten and Lharong Successfully Complete Their Official Visit to Delhi
author: Dawa Tsering
content: Dharamshala: As part of the program of the 18th Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, Parliamentarians Geshe Lharampa Atuk Tseten and Lharong successfully concluded their official visitation program with their final program in Delhi from 28 to 30 July, 2026. On the morning of July 30 at 9:30 AM, the two Parliamentarians departed from Samyeling, Delhi, and visited the Bureau of His Holiness the Dalai Lama in Delhi. Upon arrival, Representative Jigme Tsering, the Secretary, and other staff members extended a warm welcome and presented a briefing on the office’s operations. The Parliamentarians first expressed their congratulations to the newly appointed Representative. They then provided guidance emphasizing the general status of the Indian Registration Certificate (RC) and the Identity Certificate (IC), stressing the need to exercise strict attention and diligence regarding these two documents, particularly for Tibetans residing in South India and Dharamshala. At 12:30 PM, the Parliamentarians paid visits to local religious centers including Jangtse Lhamo Khang, Jangchup Lhakhang, and Drepung Ngagpa Dratsang, as well as administrative offices such as the Local Assembly, the Tibetan Medical & Astro-Institute, the Regional Tibetan Freedom Movement (BRDL), and the local Health Clinic. Later in the afternoon, they visited the Central Executive Office of Dokham Chushi Gangdruk, where General Secretary Karma Samdup and Treasurer Geshe Tenzin Ngodup introduced their ongoing initiatives aligned with the guidance of His Holiness the Dalai Lama before guiding a tour of the Heroes Memorial Hall. At 5:00 PM, a public gathering was convened at the Samyeling Local Assembly Hall, Geshe Lharampa Atuk Tseten spoke on the vast accomplishments of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, international geopolitics, and the unifying inspiration of patriot Rangzen Lobga self-immolation. He highlighted the nationwide support and campaigns sparked by this noble act of sacrifice, urging everyone across the three traditional provinces and religious sects to stand united and continue advocating for the Tibetan cause in accordance with the martyr’s hopes. While Parliamentarian Lharong addressed the critical situation inside Tibet, the official resolution of solidarity passed unanimously during the 1st session of the 18th Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile regarding the grave conditions in Tibet, and the critical dangers law posed by the Chinese Communist Government’s so-called “Ethnic Unity and Progress Law” which was enforced starting 1 July, 2026, designed to eradicate Tibet’s distinct religion, culture, language, and national identity, along with strategies to counter these policies. Following the speeches, an open Q&A session was held. The Parliamentarians provided detailed responses and clarifications to questions and views expressed by the attendees, successfully concluding the gathering. In the evening, 26 local associations hosted a farewell dinner for the visiting delegates, marking the official conclusion of all programs scheduled for the Delhi visit. – Report filed by Tibetan Parliamentary Secretariat

title: A Global Appeal- Open letter from the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile On the People’s Republic of China’s Ethnic Unity and Progress Law
author: Dawa Tsering
content: A Call to Defend Human Rights, Cultural Diversity, Religious Freedom, and the Peaceful Resolution of the Tibet-China Conflict To: Heads of State and Government, Parliamentary Leaders and Members, the United Nations, Human Rights Organizations, Religious and Interfaith leaders and Friends of Tibet. The Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile the democratically elected legislative institution representing the Tibetan people across the globe calls to act with urgency in response to the People’s Republic of China’s Ethnic Unity and Progress Law, which came into force on 1 July 2026. Presented as a measure to promote “national unity,” this law deepens policies that threaten the Tibetan people’s language, religion, culture, identity, and fundamental human rights. The gravity of this moment was tragically underscored by the sacrifice of Tibetan activist Lobga Rangzen, who died after setting himself on fire outside the United Nations Headquarters in New York on 2nd July 2026. His final appeal was for a free Tibet where Tibetans can live with dignity, freedom, and the protection of their fundamental rights. We respectfully call upon governments, parliaments, the United Nations, and the international community to: A Defining Test of the International Human Rights System The implementation of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law is not solely a Tibetan concern. It is a test of the international community’s commitment to protecting cultural diversity, freedom of religion or belief, linguistic rights, minority protections, and the rule of international human rights law. When the identity of a people is threatened, the principles upon which the international human rights system is built are also put at risk. The Tibetan people’s struggle has always been guided by truth, compassion, and non-violence. We believe that silence in the face of injustice only emboldens oppression. We therefore urge the international community to stand with the Tibetan people in defending human dignity, religious freedom, cultural diversity, and the universal values that unite us all. Lasting peace cannot be achieved through forced assimilation. Lasting unity cannot be built by erasing identity. A stable and harmonious future can only be founded on respect for human dignity, cultural diversity, religious freedom, and meaningful dialogue The future of Tibet should be shaped through dialogue—not assimilation; through justice—not coercion. Dolma Tsering TeykhangDated: 1 August 2026SpeakerTibetan Parliament-in-ExileGangchen Kyishong, DharamshalaHimachal Pradesh, India

title: The Tibetan Institute of Performing Arts Concludes 4th Summer Tibetan Performing Arts Training Programme
author: Ngawang Tsepak
content: Dharamshala: The Tibetan Institute of Performing Arts (TIPA) held the closing ceremony of its 4th Summer Tibetan Performing Arts Training Programme this morning at 10:30 a.m. in the institute’s auditorium. Secretary of the Department of Education Karma Choeying attended the ceremony as the chief guest. The event was also attended by the parents and family members of the participating students, along with TIPA staff members. At the opening ceremony, the TIPA Director,Dhundup Tsering,welcomed the Chief guest and all the students, parents, and family members who had come specially from abroad to attend the closing ceremony. He spoke about TIPA’s objectives and noted that interest in Tibet’s unique performing arts among young Tibetans living abroad has been growing steadily. Since 2023, this training has been organised to coincide with the summer holidays of young Tibetans raised abroad. What began with around thirty students has now reached its fourth summer training programme. During the training, teachers dedicated their full effort to teaching the students the Tibetan language as well as Tibetan opera arts, musical instruments, dance, and folk songs. Students were also encouraged to carry forward and promote Tibetan performing arts and their own identity when they return to their residence. Following this, the students who took part in the training performed around twelve different pieces, including song and dance performances, instrumental music, and traditional folk songs. On this occasion, Chief guest Secretary Karma Choeying presented certificates and ceremonial scarves (khatags) to all the students who successfully completed the training programme. Addressing the gathering, he said it was encouraging to see the students show such keen interest in learning Tibetan performing arts and commended the parents for their unwavering support. He also expressed appreciation to the TIPA instructor for their month-long commitment, under the Institute’s guidance, worked diligently for a month to teach the students song, dance, and instrumental performance, resulting in today’s excellent presentation. He noted that this work constitutes the preservation of Tibetan culture. Referring to the challenges facing Tibet under Chinese rule, he stressed that safeguarding Tibetan religion, language, and culture remains essential to preserving Tibetan identity. He also cited His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama’s quoting “hold on to hope while preparing for hardship”, noting that the Tibetan struggle is a shared responsibility. He said the responsibility for protecting Tibetan identity rests with every Tibetan, and that instilling the language, religion, and culture passed down from their ancestors into the hearts of young Tibetans must begin at home — if parents speak to their children in Tibetan and cultivate this habit, Tibetan identity can be protected and preserved. The month-long training programme, organised by TIPA from1 July to 1 August 2026to coincide with the summer holidays of young Tibetans living abroad, concluded successfully, marking the completion of its fourth edition. -Report filed by Tibetan Institute of Performing Arts

title: Department of Education Concludes In-Service Workshop for Science and Mathematics Teachers
author: Dawa Tsering
content: Dharamshala: The Department of Education (DoE), Central Tibetan Administration (CTA), successfully concluded a four-day in-service workshop on constructivist pedagogy and “Make Your Lab” activities for science and mathematics teachers. Held at the Agastya Creativity Campus in Kuppam, Andhra Pradesh, the programme was followed by a two-day training on the effective use of mathematics laboratory teaching materials for selected Tibetan schools. The workshop brought together 50 teachers from Tibetan schools across India, comprising 25 science teachers and 25 mathematics teachers. With each school deputing one science teacher and one mathematics teacher. The programme aimed to strengthen classroom practices and promote engaging, activity-based, and learner-centred approaches to science and mathematics education. The programme began on 22 August, when the participating teachers assembled at the Dalai Lama Institute for Higher Education in Bengaluru. The Department conducted an orientation programme, followed by a seminar on the current educational situation in Tibet. On 23 August, the teachers travelled to the Agastya Creativity Campus in Kuppam for the main training programme. The four-day workshop commenced on 24 August under the guidance of Mr. Manjunath, Head Trainer of the Agastya training team at Agastya Vidyachal Academy. During the initial sessions, participants explored the principles of constructivist teaching and learning, which emphasise that students learn more effectively by actively engaging with ideas through experiences, interaction, questioning, discussion, inquiry, and reflection. The sessions focused on the Zone of Proximal Development and the 5E instructional model—Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, and Evaluate. These approaches helped teachers plan learner-centred lessons, identify students’ prior knowledge, provide suitable scaffolding, and support them in becoming more confident and independent learners. Teachers were encouraged to move beyond textbook-based instruction by creating opportunities for students to observe, investigate, test ideas, and draw conclusions. The Agastya team conducted a model classroom session with local Grade VIII students, allowing participants to observe activity-based and inquiry-oriented teaching in practice. Teachers witnessed how hands-on activities, group work, guided questions, discussion, and appropriate teacher support can improve students’ conceptual understanding. Science and mathematics teachers were later divided into separate groups for “Make Your Lab” sessions. They learned to design and develop low-cost teaching-learning materials using locally available resources. The sessions showed that meaningful science and mathematics learning need not depend on expensive equipment; simple, affordable materials can make abstract concepts practical, visual, engaging, and easier for students to understand. Participants also visited the science and mathematics laboratories, Ramanujan Math Park, Bio-Discovery Centre, and Akash Telescope Viewing Station at the Agastya Creativity Campus. Located across approximately 172 acres at the tri-junction of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka, the campus provides an innovative and eco-friendly setting for STEM education, creativity, design thinking, scientific exploration, and innovation. The closing ceremony was held on 27 August, during which all participants received certificates of participation. With support from Mrs. Thinley Pelmo la and Gen Nyime Tsering, Mr. Dorjee Wangdue, Science Education Officer, DoE, presented tokens of appreciation to the Agastya trainers and master trainers for their commitment, teamwork, and contribution to the programme. Following the workshop, 45 participants returned to their respective schools. Mathematics teachers from STS Chandragiri, STS Kalimpong, STS Darjeeling, and TCV Ladakh remained for a further two-day training on the effective use of mathematics laboratory teaching materials. The additional training formed part of the Department’s plan to establish well-designed mathematics laboratories and strengthen mathematics learning environments in Tibetan schools. The four selected schools are developing or renovating their mathematics laboratories, while Agastya will provide relevant teaching aids. The training enabled teachers to identify, handle, and use the materials confidently in their classrooms. Subject to fund availability, the Department plans to establish well-equipped mathematics laboratories in Tibetan schools over the next five years. The sessions were led by. Gowri Satya, a Bengaluru-based former mathematics educator and content developer. She introduced the teaching aids, explained their classroom applications, and demonstrated practical methods for helping students understand and visualise mathematical concepts. The Department also developed customised mathematics teaching kits for Tibetan children in Grades I–V, with support from former TCV Mathematics Mentor Thinley Pelmo la and Ms. S. M. Peereshavli of Agastya. Following the programme, Mr. Dorjee Wangdue visited the National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS), Bengaluru, to express the Department’s appreciation for its continued support. He met Professor L. S. Shashidhara, Centre Director, and Dr. Kirthi Nandimath , Education Officer. Discussions focused on continuing research-level internship opportunities for Tibetan science students, the annual STEM excursion programme for Tibetan schools in South India, and possible collaboration on future teacher-training programmes and other STEM education initiatives. The programme was supported by the Government of the United States through the Tibet Fund. – Report filed by Department of Education, CTA

title: Tibetan Community in Switzerland Marks 66th Anniversary of Tibetan Democracy
author: Palden Choedon
content: Töss, Switzerland: The Tibetan Community in Switzerland commemorated the 66th Anniversary of Tibetan Democracy with a gathering of nearly 200 community members at Grosshalle Töss, Tössstalstrasse, bringing together religious leaders, former members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, representatives of Tibetan organisations, community leaders and guests. Among the distinguished guests were Rikon Khen Rinpoche Tenzin Jangchup, Thinlay Chukki, Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, former members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, Phuntsok Topgyal, UN Advocacy Officer of the Office of Tibet, Geneva, and representatives of Tibetan NGOs. The programme began with traditional prayers, followed by the Tibetan national anthem, a minute of silence in remembrance of those who sacrificed their lives for Tibet, and the Tibetan Democracy Day song. Representatives of the Tibetan Community subsequently presented their annual activity reports and financial accounts, reflecting the community’s commitment to transparency, accountability and democratic participation. Addressing the gathering, Thinlay Chukki highlighted the significance of Tibetan democracy and the responsibility it places on every Tibetan. Recalling her earlier participation in a conference in Berlin, she spoke of an encounter with young boy from Hong Kong who expressed their desire to contribute to the future of their nation but were uncertain about how they could do so. The experience, she said, reinforced her appreciation of the democratic institutions available to Tibetans today, established under the visionary leadership of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. Thinlay Chukki also briefed the community on recent developments concerning China’s ethnic policies and proposed ethnic unity legislation, expressing concern over their potential long-term implications for Tibetan language, culture, religion, traditions and identity. She emphasised that preserving Tibetan identity is a collective responsibility requiring active engagement from every generation. She further called on Tibetans to exercise responsibility and sensitivity in their use of social media, noting that Tibetans inside Tibet closely follow the activities and statements of Tibetans living abroad. She urged community members to ensure that their public expressions do not unintentionally cause discouragement or distress to those living under difficult circumstances inside Tibet. Following the address, Phuntsok Topgyal, UN Advocacy Officer of the Office of Tibet, Geneva, presented an overview of the Bureau’s international advocacy and outreach work. His presentation covered the Bureau’s activities from 2022 to 2025, providing the community with a broader understanding of its engagement at the international level. The presentation highlighted the Office of Tibet’s engagement with the United Nations, diplomatic missions, international organisations and civil society, as well as its efforts to maintain international attention on the human rights situation in Tibet and the preservation of Tibet’s distinct cultural, religious and linguistic identity. It also underlined the importance of sustained and long-term international engagement, particularly as the Tibet issue may require continued advocacy for many years to come. The celebration concluded with a renewed commitment among members of the Tibetan community to safeguard their democratic heritage, preserve Tibetan identity and culture, support Tibetans inside Tibet, and uphold the principles of non-violence, democracy, human rights and compassion championed by His Holiness the Dalai Lama. -Report filed by Office of Tibet, Geneva

title: UN Human Rights Chief Expresses Concern Over Restrictions on Tibetans
author: Ngawang Tsepak
content: Geneva, 7 September 2026 : The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk expressed deep concern over the deteriorating human rights situation in Tibet, particularly restrictions affecting the Tibetan people’s freedom of religion. Addressing the opening of the 63rd session of the United Nations Human Rights Council in Geneva, the High Commissioner highlighted a range of pressing global human rights concerns, including armed conflicts, restrictions on civic space, discrimination, and violations affecting vulnerable and minority communities. In a significant reference to Tibet, the High Commissioner stated that “tightening restrictions on the rights of the Tibetan people, including their freedom of religion, are deeply troubling” and appealed for an urgent change in these policies. The statement is particularly significant as concerns continue to grow over restrictions on the exercise of religious and cultural rights in Tibet. The High Commissioner’s call underscores the importance of respecting fundamental human rights and ensuring that Tibetans are able to exercise their rights and freedoms without undue restrictions. The Tibet Bureau, Geneva, welcomes the explicit attention given to the human rights situation in Tibet and reiterates the importance of sustained international engagement on the protection of Tibetan religious, cultural and fundamental rights. The Bureau will continue to engage with UN mechanisms, diplomatic missions and international partners to ensure that developments in Tibet remain part of the international human rights discourse. The High Commissioner reaffirmed that human rights must remain central to international cooperation, accountability and the pursuit of lasting peace, emphasising that universal human rights provide a framework for addressing contemporary global challenges. -Report filed by Office of Tibet, Geneva

title: Parliamentarian Kalsang Tsering Attends Memorial Gathering for Patriot Lobga Rangzen and Tibetan Democracy Day Celebration in Australia
author: Ngawang Tsepak
content: Dharamshala: On 22 August 2026, at the invitation of the Tibetan Community of Western Australia, Kalsang Tsering, a Member of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile representing Australasia and Asia (excluding India, Nepal, and Bhutan), attended a memorial gathering commemorating the 49th day since the passing of patriotic martyr Lobga Rangzen, who died after self-immolating in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York, USA, on 2 July. Upon arrival at Perth Airport, Parliamentarian Kalsang Tsering was warmly welcomed by Sonam Lhamo (Doljang), President of the Tibetan Community of Western Australia, and Tenpa Dargye, Secretary of the association. The official ceremony commenced at 5:00 PM. The chief guest was Senator Dean Smith, a supporter of the Tibetan cause and a member of the Australian Senate. The special guest was Representative Karma Singye of the Tibet Information Office. The gathering was also attended by Friends of Tibet, supporters of the Tibetan cause, and members of the regional Tibetan community. In his address, Parliamentarian Kalsang Tsering paid tribute to the sacrifice of patriotic hero Lobga Rangzen. Referring to Lobga Rangzen’s final testament, he emphasised the responsibility of all Tibetans to remain united and actively contribute to the struggle for Tibetan freedom. Speeches were also delivered by chief guest Senator Dean Smith, other supporters of the Tibetan cause, and Representative Karma Singye. Members of the Tibetan association recited poetry in honour of Lobga Rangzen and his sacrifice. During the gathering, Tenpa Dargye, Secretary of the association, launched a website featuring photographs and information about individuals who have self-immolated both inside and outside Tibet in connection with the cause of Tibetan religion, politics, and nationality. On the following day, 23 August, the Tibetan Community of Western Australia celebrated the 66th Tibetan Democracy Day ahead of schedule, in the presence of both the Tibetan Parliamentarian and the Representative from the Office of Tibet. The programme began with a welcome address by the President of the Tibetan Association, followed by a brief presentation of the community’s financial accounts by the Secretary. Young members of the community also performed the traditional Ling Kordo dance. Community members shared updates on local issues and raised questions with the Parliamentarian and the Representative from the Office of Tibet, who responded accordingly. Parliamentarian Kalsang Tsering delivered an address providing a brief overview of the evolution of Tibetan democracy. He emphasised the importance of supporting and strengthening the Central Tibetan Administration, preserving and strengthening local Tibetan community organisations regardless of their size, and prioritising the teaching of the Tibetan language to children attending weekend schools through the joint efforts of parents and teachers. Representative Karma Singye also delivered an address on the significance of Tibetan Democracy Day. In addition, recommendations were shared regarding amendments to and the finalisation of the Regulations of the Tibetan Community of Western Australia. – Report filed by Tibetan Parliamentary Secretariat

title: Tibetans in Japan and South Korea Observe Tibetan Democracy Day
author: Ngawang Tsepak
content: Tokyo: Tibetans in Japan and South Korea observed the 66th Anniversary of Tibetan Democracy Day at the Tibet House Japan office and online on 6 September 2026. Representative Dr. Tsewang Gyalpo Arya of the Liaison Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama for Japan and East Asia and Dorjee Shiota of the Tibetan Community Japan offered prostrations and Khata to the portrait of His Holiness the 14th the Dalai Lama. This was followed by the singing of the Tibetan National Anthem and Tibetan Democracy song by the participants. Representative Dr. Arya read the Kashag’s message on the occasion and briefly explained the gist of the message and urged the audience to live by the dream and aspiration of H.H. the Dalai Lama to practice and achieve a clean and vibrant democracy in exile and for future Tibet. He reminded the Tibetans of the sacrifice made by Martyr Lobga Rangzen before the U.N. building on 2 July and lamented the poor attendance by the Tibetans on this important national day. Dorjee Shiota and Rev. Geshe Tenzin Sangpo of the Tibetan community in Japan and Korea greeted the audience and briefly explained the respective community’s annual activity reports. They further requested the gathering to treat this democratic vision of the Central Tibetan Administration and unite beyond the provincial and religious affiliations. Tsering Dorjee of the Students for Free Tibet report the SFT Japan’s activities and urged the gathering to encourage and acknowledge the contribution and support rendered by the Japanese brothers and sisters in raising the Tibet issue. Participants offered views on organizing events and the need for active participation in the Tibetan events by the Tibetans. Before the Democracy Day event, Tibetans and Japanese gathered at Tibet House to offer a prayer service for the people who lost their lives and to show solidarity with bereaved and missing people due to the recent Tibet-Nepal devastating flash flood. Many voiced dissatisfaction with the way the Chinese communist leadership handled the disaster despite being the engineer of this man-made disaster. Kunchok Sithar of Potala College presided over the prayer service. Tibetan Community Japan Committee’s two-year stint was to end that day, and an online election of the President and committee members was announced at the event. -Report filed by Office of Tibet, Japan

title: Sikyong Penpa Tsering Meets Czech Ambassador H.E. Dr. Eliska Zigova, Expresses Appreciations for Her Stanch Support for Tibetans
author: OOT - DC
content: New Delhi, 24 August 2026: Sikyong Penpa Tsering of the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) met Her Excellency Dr. Eliska Zigova, Ambassador of the Czech Republic to India, at the Embassy of the Czech Republic today, on the occasion of the completion of her tenure as Ambassador to India. The meeting lasted for about an hour and focused primarily on the current Sinicisation practices of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) in Tibet, including the introduction of the “Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress Law” and its grave implications for the preservation of Tibetan identity. They also discussed the shifting global balance of power, the current situation of the Tibetan people, and the CTA’s continued commitment to the Middle Way Approach, which seeks a peaceful resolution of the Tibet cause through dialogue and genuine autonomy for the Tibetan people. As a token of appreciation for Her Excellency’s long-standing support and warm engagement with the Tibetan community, Sikyong presented her with a traditional white scarf and a Green Tara thangka . Her Excellency reaffirmed her commitment to supporting the Tibetan people and the CTA in their continued efforts to uphold the values of peace, dialogue, democracy and human rights. Sikyong conveyed his best wishes to Her Excellency for her future endeavours and expressed his appreciation for her long-standing support and engagement with the Tibetan community. The farewell meeting was accompanied by Representative Jigme Tsering, Secretary Tashi Dekyi, and Protocol Officer Tenzin Passang from the Bureau of His Holiness the Dalai Lama in New Delhi. The meeting concluded on a cordial note, with both sides expressing hope that the close relations and mutual understanding between the Czech Republic and the Tibetan people would continue in the future.

title: CTA Leadership Leads 49th-Day Prayer Ceremony and Peaceful March Honouring Tibetan Martyr Lobga Rangzen in Dharamshala
author: OOT - DC
content: Dharamshala: A strong sense of solidarity and collective remembrance was evident in Dharamshala this morning as Tibetans from all sections of the community gathered at the Tsuglagkhang courtyard for a special prayer service marking the 49th day since the passing of Tibetan self-immolator Lobga Rangzen. Jointly organised by the 17th Kashag and the 18th Tibetan Parliament in Exile of the Central Tibetan Administration, the service was held from 10:00 am to 12:00 noon and honoured Lobga Rangzen’s martyrdom for the cause of Tibet, while also paying tribute to the memory of Tibetan patriots who have lost their lives both inside and outside Tibet. Monks, students and schoolchildren, CTA officials, NGOs and local Tibetans gathered in large numbers, making the morning’s commemoration a significant public expression of solidarity with those who have sacrificed their lives for the cause of Tibet. Prayers and solidarity were also extended to the bereaved families. The prayer service was led by the abbot of Namgyal Monastery and monks. Those notables in attendance included Chief Justice Commissioner Yeshi Wangmo, Speaker Dolma Tsering Teykhang, Sikyong Penpa Tsering, the Deputy Speaker, other Justice Commissioners, heads of the CTA’s three autonomous bodies, Kalons of the 17th Kashag, and members of the 18th Tibetan Parliament in Exile. Sikyong Penpa Tsering spoke briefly to local media ahead of the prayer service, noting that the 49th day following a person’s passing is considered an important day in Tibetan Buddhism. Over the past seven weeks, Tibetans around the world have undertaken various forms of activism to draw international attention to the issue. In recognition of this, the 17th Kashag and the 18th Tibetan Parliament in Exile organised today’s memorial prayer service to honour Lobga Rangzen and all other Tibetans who have self-immolated for the Tibetan cause. Sikyong stressed that these individuals did not seek to harm others or promote violence, but made the ultimate sacrifice in the hope of drawing greater attention to the Tibetan cause. He said that today’s service was an expression of remembrance, solidarity and support for those who had given their lives. Sikyong further expressed concern that the Chinese government continues to pursue policies aimed at eroding and ultimately destroying Tibetan identity, despite presenting them under the guise of “ethnic unity and progress.” He said that China is seeking to extend its influence across the world through initiatives such as the Global Governance System, Global Security Initiative, and Global Cultural Initiative , presenting these as mechanisms to shape the international order. He cautioned that if China’s growing influence and control continue to expand globally, the free world may gradually become accustomed to accepting its influence, raising serious questions about the future of freedom and democratic values. He urged the world to recognise that these developments are not only about Tibet, but also have implications for other peoples and regions, including East Turkestan and Southern Mongolia. During the prayer service, Sikyong Penpa Tsering shared a brief account of Lobga Rangzen’s life and his lifelong commitment to and activism for the Tibetan cause. He also read out Lobga’s final message, delivered before his self-immolation, in which he called on Tibetans to remain united and continue their efforts for Tibet’s freedom. As the prayer service concluded, Sikyong Penpa Tsering broke the chain of the hunger strike organised by the Tibetan Youth Congress for over a month opposite the entrance to Tsuglagkhang, before leading the march towards Police Ground, Dharamshala. Alongside the Tibetan leadership and representatives of Tibetan civil society organisations, Shri Ajit Nehria, President of the Indo-Tibetan Friendship Association; Shri Shamsher Singh Nehria, Mayor of Dharamshala Municipal Corporation; and other friends and supporters of Tibet joined the peaceful march. Holding placards, raising slogans, and waving vibrant Tibetan national flags, the participants marched through the major areas of Dharamshala before reaching Police Ground, Dharamshala, where another event was held. During the event, the statements of the Kashag and the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile were read by Sikyong and Speaker of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, respectively. A message in support of Tibetans from former Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh, Shri Shanta Kumar, was also delivered to the gathering by Additional Secretary Tenzin Norbu. The event also featured an address by Tashi Dhargyal, Vice President of the Tibetan Youth Congress, followed by the rendition of the Tibetan and Indian national anthems.

title: Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile’s Statement During the Peace March Organised Jointly by the Kashag and the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile on the 49th Day (7th Week) Observance of the Sacrifice of Patriotic Hero Rangzen Lobga
author: OOT - DC
content: Greetings to everyone participating in the Peace March today. On July 2, 2026—the second day after the Chinese communist regime officially implemented its so-called “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress” on July 1, 2026—patriotic hero Rangzen Lobga carried the Tibetan national flag in front of the United Nations headquarters in New York City and set himself on fire in protest against the Chinese Communist Party for Tibetan independence. Today marks the 49th day (7th weekly) observance of his passing. We pay our deepest homage to the late hero and to all patriotic heroes both inside and outside Tibet who have sacrificed their lives, for the just cause of Tibet’s religion, politics, and nationality, Under the joint organization of the Kashag (Cabinet) and the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile (TPiE), an extensive prayer service was held this morning at the Thekchen Choling Tsuglagkhang, followed by this Peace March. Since the illegal invasion and occupation of Tibet, the Chinese communist government has continuously exploited and inflicted unprecedented destruction on Tibet’s natural resources across its three traditional provinces through mining, deforestation, the South-to-North Water Diversion project, and the damming and diverting of rivers for hydropower construction. Furthermore, Tibetans have been completely deprived of their fundamental human rights, with severe restrictions on freedom of religion, movement, speech, and the preservation and promotion of Tibetan language. Over a million Tibetan children have been forcibly placed in Chinese state-run colonial boarding schools, leaving them with no opportunity to study their own religion, culture, and language except for the Chinese language. At the initial stage with the implementation of its “second-generation ethnic policies” against the will of the Tibetan people, the Chinese Communist Party has repeatedly enforced cruel measures impacting both the people and the environment of Tibet. Tibetans inside and outside Tibet have launched numerous protest movements against these policies. In particular, since 2009, around 157 known cases of Self-immolations have happened inside Tibet to protest against the Chinese Communist Party’s hardline policies. Recently on July 2, before his self-immolation, the late patriotic hero Rangzen Lobga stated in his final video testament: “The Chinese Communist Party is implementing policies aimed at completely eradicating the Tibetan identity… Therefore, from now on, what I want to tell you is that the Chinese Communists have persecuted all of us Tibetans, irrespective of whether we belong to Dotoe, Domed or Utsang province (the three traditional provinces of Tibet). We are all Tibetans. Therefore, we should work together for the Tibetan nation; we should work for the people of Tibet. Today, when we say that we do not have human rights, that we do not have freedom of speech, that we do not have the freedom to display a portrait of His Holiness the Dalai Lama – if we examine why we do not have these freedoms, it is because we lost the independence of Tibet. That’s why, from today onwards, whether it is the Tibetan government (in exile), the Tibetan parliament (in exile), or the Tibetan people, it is important that we should all be united and work for the cause of the Tibetan nation and the Tibetan people. As stated in his final testament, such immense sacrifices are direct consequences of successive ruthless policies enforced by the Chinese communist Party. Despite these sacrifices—which are clear to the entire world—the Chinese government continues to disregard and trample upon them, spreading false and irresponsible disinformation through media and social channels to mislead the public. During this critical and urgent time, we strongly appeal the international community to take a moral and just responsibility through the following actions: Closely monitor the implementation and human rights implications of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law and ensure sustained international scrutiny. Support independent investigations through United Nations human rights mechanisms, including the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights, Special Rapporteurs, Treaty Bodies, and the Universal Periodic Review process. Publicly express concern regarding the implementation and consequences of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law. Raise the issue in bilateral engagements and multilateral forums, including the United Nations and other international institutions. Support the protection of the cultural, linguistic, religious, and human rights of Tibetans and other affected nationalities. Strengthen measures to counter transnational repression and protect Tibetan communities, human rights defenders, and advocates living within your country. Oppose all forms of transnational repression that threaten democratic freedoms in the world. Recognize that Tibet was historically an independent nation, prior to the forceful invasion and occupation of Tibet. Impress upon the leadership of PRC to engage in peaceful dialogue to resolve the conflict between Tibet and China supporting the peaceful, non-violent aspirations of the Tibetan people in accordance with the vision of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. The implementation of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law is not solely a Tibetan concern. It is a test of the international community’s commitment to protecting cultural diversity, freedom of religion or belief, linguistic rights, minority protections, and the rule of international human rights law. When the identity of a people is threatened, the principles upon which the international human rights system is built are also put at risk. The Tibetan struggle is rooted in truth and non-violence. We believe that remaining silent in the face of injustice anywhere gives perpetrators the confidence to continue their misdeeds. Therefore, lasting peace cannot be achieved through forced assimilation. Lasting unity cannot be built by erasing identity. A stable and harmonious future can only be founded on respect for human dignity, cultural diversity, religious freedom, and meaningful dialogue. The future of Tibet should be shaped through dialogue—not assimilation; through justice—not coercion. The sacrifice of patriotic hero Lobga Rangzen through his act of self-immolation highlighted the suffering of Tibetans to the United Nations, governments, and people around the world. By directly confronting and protesting Chinese policies, his action has opened a new chapter in the history of the Tibetan struggle for truth. Accordingly, on July 3, the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile issued an official press release. Following that, a total of 837 official appeal letters regarding these issues were dispatched to governments, parliaments, the United Nations, the European Union and international bodies worldwide. Appeals were also sent electronically to international media outlets. Furthermore, instructions were sent to the Offices of Tibet via the Kashag to follow up with Parliamentary Support Groups for Tibet and local Tibetan associations. Additionally, written guidance was provided to all Members of Parliament to inform local communities about Rangzen Lobga’s sacrifice during their official visitation programs across Tibetan settlements in India. In late July, coinciding with the Monsoon Session of the Indian Parliament, two parliamentary delegation teams led by the Deputy Speaker met with Indian Central Cabinet Ministers, Members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha), and other key dignitaries to advocate for Tibet and hand over official appeal documents regarding the late Lobga Rangzen’s sacrifice and the Chinese government’s recently implemented ‘Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress’. Furthermore, during the upcoming Parliamentary session in September, all Members of Parliament will hold a special deliberation to discuss future action plans. We express our deep appreciation to Tibetans and Tibet supporters worldwide who have continuously organized diverse and large-scale campaigns following the sacrifice of patriotic hero Rangzen Lobga—especially the Tibetans and non-governmental organizations in New York. We urge everyone, both publicly and individually, to maintain strong resolve in their hearts and intensify efforts for the common Tibetan cause until truth prevails. In conclusion: We pray deeply for the long life of His Holiness the Great 14th Dalai Lama—the savior and guide of all sentient beings across the three realms and especially the people of the Land of Snows—that He may live for a hundred eons, that all His noble aspirations be spontaneously fulfilled without impediment, and that the ultimate noble wishes of all departed Martyrs who sacrificed their precious lives for the cause of the Tibetan nation and people be fully realized. title: Statement of the Kashag on the 49th-day of the Passing of the Late Martyr Lobga Rangzen
author: OOT - DC
content: Today marks the Seventh Week (49th-day) of the self-immolation and passing of the martyr Lobsang Palden, popularly known as Lobga Rangzen. He sacrificed his life on July 2, 2026, in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York City, United States, leaving behind a final testament stating that his action was undertaken in protest against the Chinese Communist Party’s policies and its systematic eradication of the Tibetan identity in Tibet, while calling on all Tibetans to unite and campaign for Tibet’s independence. In observance of the 49th-Day, the Kashag and the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile today, are jointly organising this official solidarity prayer service and peace march to express our deep condolences and respect to the late Lobga Rangzen and all those Tibetans who have sacrificed their lives for the cause of Tibet. We express our strong opposition to the Chinese Communist Party’s implementation of repressive policies in Tibet, particularly the so-called “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress”. Immediately upon receiving news of the Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation protest, the Office of Tibet, Washington, D.C., coordinated with the International Campaign for Tibet in convening an urgent online meeting to disseminate verified information to media outlets and instructed Tibetan associations across North America to organise solidarity prayer services. Simultaneously, a request was made through the Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, to seek His Holiness’ prayers for the late Lobga Rangzen. The message from the Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama was relayed to the immediate family members. Furthermore, on behalf of the Kashag, Kalon Kunga Tashi of the Department of Security visited the Phuntsok De-zhi community hall of the New York & New Jersey Tibetan Association that very night to extend our heartfelt condolences. In the official public statement issued on July 3rd, the Sikyong said: “ The unfolding genocide inside Tibet and the enforcement of the draconian ‘ Ethnic Unity and Progress Law ’ on 1 July are what drove Lobga Rangzen to this tragic decision.” An official prayer service was organised that day. To draw international attention to the Chinese government’s ongoing policy of eradicating the Tibetan identity, 157 Tibetans inside Tibet have been known to have self-immolated since 2009, out of which 136 died, 9 have survived, and the status of 12 remains unknown. In exile, including the late Lobga Rangzen, 11 Tibetans have self-immolated, of which 9 died and 2 survived. Not a single brave Tibetan who self-immolated—whether inside Tibet or in exile—ever harmed the lives or property of others. Rather, they sacrificed their own precious lives with the sole motivation of drawing the attention of the Chinese government and the international community to the plight of the Tibetan people. The Special Tibetan General Meeting on September 28, 2012, recognised self-immolation as the highest form of nonviolent act of protest and passed a resolution urging “ all Tibetans to preserve their precious human lives henceforth. ” The Kashag reiterates its appeal to all Tibetans to remain steadfast in serving the Tibetan cause throughout their lives.” Following the tragic death of the late Lobga Rangzen, Tibetans and friends of Tibet around the world continue to hold various peaceful commemorative events in his honour and protest the Chinese government. We express our heartfelt gratitude and deep appreciation to all media outlets for their widespread coverage of these campaigns and to everyone involved for their steadfast expressions of solidarity and support. The Kashag appeals to the Tibetans both inside and outside Tibet to stay vigilant, prudent and united in resisting the policies of the Chinese government aimed at eradicating the Tibetan identity. The sinister intent behind the Chinese Communist Party’s so-called “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress”, implemented on July 1, 2026, includes: Erosion of Tibetan Language: The Chinese government has placed nearly one million Tibetan children into colonial-style residential schools, forcing them to learn Chinese and adopt a Chinese identity while demanding absolute loyalty to the Chinese Communist Party. This education system strips away their right to grow up within their own culture and learn their mother tongue. Even private study of the Tibetan language during summer and winter vacations is prohibited. Furthermore, this legislation mandates Chinese as the medium of instruction from preschool, eliminating environments for using the Tibetan language in government offices and severely restricting the scope of Tibetan language. Distortion of Tibetan History and Identity: The legislation directs the Chinese central government to conduct “concentrated and diverse forms of publicity and educational activities to forge a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation ( Zhonghua Minzu ).” Under the guise of “ethnic unity”, this legislation also authorises intensified control and surveillance over the way of life, gatherings, and expressions of opinion of the Tibetan people, thus establishing a legal pretext to punish even minor cultural preservation efforts. Forced Cultural Assimilation at the Grassroots Level: By ordering to conduct traditional practices such as weddings and funerals as per “public order and good customs” and to incorporate “consciousness of the common identity of the Chinese nation” into grassroots village regulations, Tibet’s unique culture and traditions are being forcibly assimilated. Sinicisation of Tibetan Buddhism: For years, the Chinese Communist Party has exercised total control over the properties, administration, and education of Tibetan monasteries while politicising the recognition of reincarnated Lamas. The provisions of this legislation further demand religious sites to “adhere to the direction of Sinicising religion,” thereby undermining the authentic spiritual tradition of Tibetan Buddhism developed over thousands of years and converting it into a tool for communist ideology and political compliance. Ethnic Integration: By promoting a “social environment of mutual integration,” implementing specific “measures regarding housing and population management, strengthening service platforms for cross-regional population transfers, supporting cross-regional recruitment between higher education institutions in ethnic and non-ethnic areas, and encouraging cadres to go to grassroots ethnic regions, the Chinese government is pushing intermarriage to reduce Tibetans into minority in their own homeland. Technological Surveillance: Ethnic affairs are being integrated into the overall “social governance mechanism.” Supported by technology such as AI surveillance, electronic ID tracking, facial recognition, GPS location systems, DNA profiling, iris scanning, and grid-based social management systems, every aspect of an individual’s daily life and movement is being strictly monitored and controlled. Political and Social Coercion: All economic and social development projects are contingent upon “firmly forging the consciousness of the common identity of the Chinese nation,” “safeguarding national unity,” and “opposing separatism.” By combining economic incentives with political intimidation, Tibetans are subjected to forced assimilation into the dominant Han society. Political Vetting of Tibetan Cadres: Cadres or entities failing to strictly implement these regulations face investigations and criminal prosecution. Since the recruitment, selection, deployment, and management of cadres must undergo political vetting, Tibetan cadres are targeted as potential offenders. Simply failing to “strictly enforce” the law—let alone causing harm to “ethnic unity”—is deemed a criminal offence, forcing Tibetan cadres to live in constant fear under this regulation day and night. Violation of Autonomy Rights: The legislation denies even the nominal rights and authority to establish local autonomous bodies, formulate and enact local autonomous regulations guaranteed under the Chinese constitution and the Regional Ethnic Autonomy Law by declaring to “uphold and improve the structure of ethnic work with the Party committee’s unified leadership, government management in accordance with law, and in which the United Front Work Department takes the lead in coordination, the ethnic work departments perform their duties, all departments join forces to cooperate, and the whole society participates, to improve the ethnic work coordination mechanism.” Establishment of Extraterritorial Jurisdiction: By asserting legal accountability against overseas individuals or organisations that undermine the implementation of this legislation or engage in ethnic separatist activities, the Chinese Communist Party seeks to bring Tibetans abroad, supporters of other oppressed peoples under Chinese government’s rule, and critics of these regulations under its extraterritorial legal jurisdiction. In short, whether the objectives of this law succeed in the long run depends on how Tibetans inside and outside Tibet resist this sinister strategy and the extent to which the international community supports the truth and the just cause of the Tibetan people. We appeal to the Tibetans in exile living in free countries to conduct various campaigns non-violently, lawfully, and with dignity. Starting from our households, Tibetans both inside and outside Tibet must make greater efforts to preserve Tibet’s unique religion, culture, language, and traditions to counter the Chinese government’s policies aimed at eradicating Tibetan identity. We appeal to Governments and Parliaments of free nations around the world to confront the Chinese government’s implementation of genocidal policies in Tibet through its blatant violation of international law and global order. We urge the international community to recognise the Sino-Tibetan conflict as an unresolved international legal issue and not an internal matter of China. And we seek your support in the resumption of Sino-Tibetan dialogue based on the mutually beneficial Middle-Way Approach policy without preconditions. We also request the think tanks and media organisations to conduct fair, objective analyses and accurate reporting. We also urge the authorities of the Chinese government to stop acting against the progress of human society, cease clinging solely to the perpetuation of their power, and immediately halt policies aimed at eradicating the identities of other non-Chinese nationalities. The Central Tibetan Administration remains firmly committed to pursuing resolution of the Sino-Tibetan conflict based on the Middle-Way Approach policy unanimously adopted by the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile. Holding the courageous spirit of the Tibetans who sacrificed their lives for our cause deep in our hearts, we hold an unyielding pledge to continue working tirelessly so that their sacrifices do not go in vain. In conclusion, we offer our deepest condolences and solidarity to the family members and relatives of the late Lobga Rangzen and all the other Tibetan martyrs who sacrificed their lives for Tibet. We pray that they may be embraced by the supreme compassionate Chenrezig (Avalokiteshvara) and be reborn as Tibetans to continue serving the cause of Tibet. Kashag August 20, 2026 ……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………… * Disclaimer: This document is an English translation of the original Tibetan text. title: Central Tibetan Administration Marks India’s 80th Independence Day
author: OOT - DC
content: Dharamshala: On the occasion of the 80th Independence Day of India, the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) observed a brief ceremony at Gangchen Kyishong on 15 August 2026 to commemorate the historic occasion and express solidarity with the people of India. The ceremony was attended by the heads of the three pillars of the Central Tibetan Administration, Kalon (Minister), Members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile (TPiE), Secretaries, senior officials and staff of various departments of the CTA. The ceremony commenced with the hoisting of the Indian national flag by Sikyong Penpa Tsering, followed by the rendition of the Indian national anthem. Addressing the media on the occasion, Sikyong Penpa Tsering expressed gratitude to the Government and people of India for their longstanding support and hospitality towards the Tibetan people. He said that the participation of the CTA leadership, dignitaries and staff in the flag-hoisting ceremony and singing the Indian national anthem was a meaningful expression of solidarity with the people of India. Reflecting on India’s struggle for independence, Sikyong said the occasion serves as a reminder to Tibetans outside – the value of freedom and democracy, particularly as Tibetans inside Tibet continue to face a critical situation under the rule of the People’s Republic of China (PRC). He noted that India’s independence was achieved through generations of struggle and the sacrifices which will serve as a source of inspiration and hope for Tibetans. Sikyong recalled the sacrifices of Tibetan freedom fighters, including the recent self-immolation of Lobga Rangzen, who made the ultimate sacrifice for the cause of Tibet. He said that while such sacrifices may not bring immediate responses, the courage and sacrifices of those who have given their lives for Tibet will remain part of world history and be remembered by future generations. He reaffirmed that the Tibetan people will continue their peaceful struggle for freedom while expressing their deep appreciation to the Government and people of India for their continued support. In response to questions from the media, Sikyong Penpa Tsering commended the CTA and the TPiE for their plans to hold an official prayer service in Dharamshala on 20 August 2026, commemorating the 49th day since the passing of Lobga Rangzen.
