title: 24th Annual Conference of Tibetan Associations of North America Held in New York
author: OOT - DC
content: New York City: The 24th Annual Conference of the Tibetan Associations of North America was successfully held from 4 to 7 September 2026 in New York City. The conference was attended by the Secretary of the Department of Information and International Relations (DIIR) of the Central Tibetan Administration, two incumbent members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile from North and South America constituency, and 51 delegates representing 25 Tibetan associations across the United States and Canada. The meeting was also attended by the Executive Director of the International Campaign for Tibet, the Director of the Canada Tibet Committee (CTC), a representative of the Tibet Fund, and the Representative of the Office of Tibet for North America, along with a staff. On the evening of 4 September, participants from different states across North America gathered at Phuntsok Deshe Hall for introductions and a reception. The conference formally commenced on 5 September with the lighting of the lamp in the presence of the Secretary of DIIR, the Representative of the Office of Tibet, the two members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, and other distinguished guests. This was followed by the singing of the Tibetan national anthem and observed a minute of silence in mourning for the Tibetan patriots. The Representative, Dr Namgyal Choedup, spoke on the significance of the annual conference of Tibetan communities in North America. He also reiterated the Kashag’s announcement concerning the “Ethnic Unity and Progress law” and its appeal to observe the fourth week of September each year as a Tibetan Identity Preservation Week, dedicated to preserving and strengthening the unique linguistic, cultural, and religious heritage of the Tibetan people. The two members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile and the Secretary of DIIR also delivered speeches on the occasion. Following this, Sonam Topden, President of the New York Tibetan Community, delivered a welcome address and introduced the community organisation. During the three-day conference, held from 5 to 7 September, participants deliberated on a range of issues concerning the Tibetan community and the Tibetan cause. The discussions covered His Holiness the Dalai Lama’s security; measures and guidelines for conducting religious services for the welfare and well-being of the Tibetan people and the preservation of their spiritual heritage; advocacy campaigns; preparations for commemorating the 20th anniversary of the 2008 Tibetan Uprising in 2028; weekend Tibetan language schools; the Tibetan Voluntary Contribution Book (Green Book or Chatrel); the Solidarity Partnership (Blue Book); the promotion of Social, Emotional, and Ethical (SEE) Learning; and other educational programmes. Following extensive deliberations on the 10 agenda items, the conference adopted 27 resolutions. A special resolution was also passed to express solidarity with the 168 Tibetans, both inside and outside Tibet, who have sacrificed their lives, bodies, and possessions for the cause of Tibet and its people. The resolution further expressed admiration for the courage of Tibetans living in Tibet and solidarity with them in the hardships they continue to endure. The conference concluded on 7 September with a closing ceremony. The Representative expressed gratitude to all the participating Tibetan community organisations and formally announced the conclusion of the conference until its next meeting. -Report filed by Office of Tibet, Washington DC

title: UN Human Rights Chief Expresses Concern Over Restrictions on Tibetans
author: OOT - DC
content: Geneva, 7 September 2026 : The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk expressed deep concern over the deteriorating human rights situation in Tibet, particularly restrictions affecting the Tibetan people’s freedom of religion. Addressing the opening of the 63rd session of the United Nations Human Rights Council in Geneva, the High Commissioner highlighted a range of pressing global human rights concerns, including armed conflicts, restrictions on civic space, discrimination, and violations affecting vulnerable and minority communities. In a significant reference to Tibet, the High Commissioner stated that “ tightening restrictions on the rights of the Tibetan people, including their freedom of religion, are deeply troubling ” and appealed for an urgent change in these policies. The statement is particularly significant as concerns continue to grow over restrictions on the exercise of religious and cultural rights in Tibet. The High Commissioner’s call underscores the importance of respecting fundamental human rights and ensuring that Tibetans are able to exercise their rights and freedoms without undue restrictions. The Tibet Bureau, Geneva, welcomes the explicit attention given to the human rights situation in Tibet and reiterates the importance of sustained international engagement on the protection of Tibetan religious, cultural and fundamental rights. The Bureau will continue to engage with UN mechanisms, diplomatic missions and international partners to ensure that developments in Tibet remain part of the international human rights discourse. The High Commissioner reaffirmed that human rights must remain central to international cooperation, accountability and the pursuit of lasting peace, emphasising that universal human rights provide a framework for addressing contemporary global challenges. -Report filed by Office of Tibet, Geneva

title: His Holiness the Dalai Lama Safely Returns to Dharamshala After a Long Sojourn in Ladakh
author: OOT - DC
content: Dharamshala: His Holiness the Dalai Lama safely returned to His official residence in Dharamshala earlier this morning, 4 September 2026, following a two-month-and-one-week sojourn in Leh, Ladakh. Upon His arrival at Kangra Airport, His Holiness was accorded a warm welcome by Tibetan Chief Justice Commissioner Yeshi Wangmo, Speaker Dolma Tsering Teykhang, and officiating Sikyong Tsegyal Chukya Dranyi, Kalon of the Department of Religion and Culture. The reception was accompanied by a vibrant performance of the auspicious Tashi Sholpa dance by a group of artistes at the airport exit. A large number of Tibetans, well-wishers, devotees, supporters, and local residents thronged major points along the route from the airport to His Holiness’ residence, carrying burning incense, flowers, and white scarves to welcome and greet Him as He passed by. At Thekchen Choeling Tsuglagkhang and at the entrance to His Holiness’ residence, members of the Tibetan Parliament in Exile and Secretaries of the Central Tibetan Administration lined up to receive Him, while the Deputy Speaker, other Justice Commissioners, Kalons, and heads of the three autonomous bodies gathered at the residence entrance to welcome His Holiness. After leaving Dharamshala, His Holiness the Dalai Lama travelled to Delhi, where he successfully underwent left knee replacement surgery on 8 June. He remained in Delhi during his recovery until 28 June. Following his recovery, His Holiness travelled to Ladakh, where he spent the subsequent two months and seven days engaging in teachings, public audiences, and various public programmes. Over the course of His Holiness the Dalai Lama’s extended stay in Ladakh, His Holiness attended the celebration of His 91st birthday at the Kalachakra Teaching Ground in Leh. He also attended prayer ceremonies at the Buddha statue in Stok and at the Buddha statue and stupa in Gonpa Village, and visited the Buddha Garden at the Mahabodhi International Meditation Centre. His Holiness also attended the final session of the Yarchos Chenmo (Great Summer Debate) at the Matho Teaching Ground, as well as a long-life prayer offering at the Kalachakra Teaching Ground, jointly organised by the Ladakh Buddhist Association, Ladakh Gonpa Association, and the Tibetan Community in Ladakh. A couple of days before His Holiness’ departure from Ladakh, He was honoured with a thanksgiving and farewell cultural programme at the Kalachakra Teaching Ground. During this period, His Holiness also granted public audiences to a total of 21,572 visitors from all walks of life and across all age groups.

title: Tibet Festival Kicks Off in New Delhi, Celebrates Cultural Heritage and Highlights Contemporary Realities
author: OOT - DC
content: New Delhi: The three-day festival, “Spirit of Tibet: Celebrating Culture and Compassion,” commenced today at the India International Centre in New Delhi, bringing together scholars, policymakers, writers, cultural practitioners, spiritual leaders, and members of the public to celebrate Tibet’s rich cultural heritage and foster greater understanding of contemporary issues concerning Tibet. Organised from 3 to 5 September, the festival began with a brief inaugural ceremony at the Gandhi-King Memorial Plaza, featuring prayers led by a Tibetan Buddhist monk, followed by the inaugural address by Sikyong Penpa Tsering. In his address, Sikyong called upon the gathering to remain vigilant regarding developments concerning China, particularly in light of the recently enacted “Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress Law” and its potential implications for Tibetans and other ethnic communities in China. He observed that the legislation appears to be inconsistent with commitments contained within the People’s Republic of China’s own constitutional and legal framework. “Unfortunately, the recently enacted Ethnic Unity Law takes China in precisely the opposite direction. Rather than creating conditions for trust and reconciliation, it institutionalises policies of assimilation under the guise of ‘national unity.’ It replaces dialogue with compulsion and diversity with conformity,” Sikyong Penpa Tsering said. He further emphasised that sustainable peace and stability cannot be achieved through coercion or by suppressing cultural, religious, and linguistic identities. The inaugural seminar, titled “Civilisational Confluence, Present Realities, and Strategic Horizons,” brought together distinguished voices from the fields of strategic affairs, journalism, academia, and China studies. Sikyong Penpa Tsering addressing the gathering. Photo / Tenzin Phende / CTA The panel comprised Sikyong Penpa Tsering; Prof. C. Raja Mohan, leading columnist, contributing editor at The Indian Express, and Visiting Professor at the Institute of South Asian Studies, National University of Singapore; and Brigadier Anshuman Narang, author, China scholar, OSINT expert, and founder of the Atma Nirbhar Soch think tank. The session was chaired by Nitin A. Gokhale, author, journalist, and national security analyst. The seminar examined Tibet’s civilisational heritage, its contemporary realities, and its broader strategic significance within the evolving geopolitical landscape. Throughout the three-day festival, a series of seminars, lectures, and documentary screenings will explore a range of themes relating to Tibet’s culture, history, spirituality, environment, and contemporary relevance. Among the eminent personalities participating on the first day are Prof. Amitabh Mattoo, Dean, School of International Studies, Jawaharlal Nehru University, Delhi; Shri Wajahat Habibullah, former Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities, Government of India; Shri Kabir Bedi, Actor and Author; and Ven. Geshe Dorji Damdul, Director of Tibet House, Delhi. They shared their perspectives on a range of issues concerning Tibet and its cultural and contemporary significance. Alongside the intellectual and academic discussions, the India International Centre has been transformed into a vibrant showcase of Tibet’s diverse cultural traditions. A major attraction of the festival is the creation of a Tibetan Buddhist sand mandala, providing visitors with an opportunity to witness an important dimension of Tibetan Buddhist artistic and spiritual practice. The festival also features cultural performances, an exhibition documenting Tibet’s historical and political evolution, and a hands-on Tibetan wood-painting workshop. Together, these activities offer visitors an immersive experience of Tibet’s enduring cultural traditions while highlighting the depth, continuity, and resilience of Tibetan civilisation. The festival received an enthusiastic response on its opening day, with more than 500 people attending the various programmes and engaging with the cultural exhibitions, performances, and discussions. The three-day festival is being organised by the Department of Information and International Relations (DIIR), Central Tibetan Administration, in collaboration with Foundation for Non-violent Alternatives and The Tibet Fund. Through its diverse programme of cultural, academic, and public engagements, the festival seeks to underscore the enduring relevance of Tibetan culture, compassion, and civilisational values, while providing a platform for meaningful dialogue and promoting greater public understanding of Tibet and its contemporary realities.

Photo: Office of Tibet, Geneva Bern — The Tibetan community in Switzerland and Liechtenstein has launched a week of peaceful rally and solidarity walk from the Swiss Federal Parliament (Bundeshaus) in Bern to the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Zurich, from March 4 to 10, 2026. The aim is to raise public awareness of human rights issues in Tibet and to call the Chinese government for transparency, respect for human rights, and compliance with legal standards in Tibetan regions. According to the Office of Tibet, Geneva, on March 4, 2026, the Tibetan Community of Switzerland and Liechtenstein has inaugurated a week-long peaceful rally and solidarity walk in Bern, they will walk till march 10th, 2026, the Tibetan National Uprising Day, from the Swiss Federal Parliament (Bundeshaus) in Bern to the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Zurich. Around 15 participants, aged between the ages of 35 and 75, represent intergenerational commitment and unity. This event, based on non-violence, dignity, and constructive dialogue, aims to raise public awareness of humanitarian concerns in Tibet and call for transparency, respect for human rights, and compliance with legal standards in Tibetan regions. Representative Thinley Chukki, the Office of Tibet, Geneva, addressed the participants at the launch and she saud,''Today, as we gather in front of the Swiss Parliament, I thank our guest of honour, a Member of Parliament, for inaugurating this peace march. This march coincides with the 90th birthday of His Holiness the Dalai Lama and seeks to draw global attention to the suffering of Tibetans in Tibet. Over one million Tibetan children face forced residential schooling, and in 2024 alone, around 650,000 Tibetans were effected by the forced labour programmes according to the UN reports. Infrastructure projects and dams have displaced nearly one million Tibetans, depriving them of their livelihoods." "We call on the international community to recognise these violations and extend their support. I thank all participants for dedicating seven days of their lives to this cause. May our efforts advance freedom in Tibet, a peaceful resolution of the Sino-Tibetan conflict, and the long life of His Holiness the Dalai Lama," she added. Katharina Prelicz-Huber, Member of the National Council of Switzerland, expressed her support, conveying the solidarity of the Tibetan Parliamentary Group and providing a message to be delivered on 10 March, 2026, marking the 67th anniversary of the Tibetan National Uprising Day. The letter was signed by co-presidents Councillor of States Diana Moser, National Councillor Leonore Borges, National Councillor Nick Gucker, National Councillor Fabian Molina, and Maya Graf, Councillor of States. According to the report, beyond Tibet, the march carries a universal message: in a world affected by war, conflict, and human suffering, peace, dialogue, and non-violence remain essential. Inspired by His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, the Tibetan Community emphasises that lasting solutions come through respect, understanding, and peaceful negotiation. They said that the march from Bern to Zurich stands as both a call for justice in Tibet and a symbolic gesture of solidarity with all peoples affected by war and instability worldwide. Photo: TYC New Delhi — The Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) organised a strong protest outside the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in New Delhi on June 7, 2026. The demonstrators protested against the Chinese government's ongoing political repression in Tibet and the implementation of the so-called "ethnic unity" law, while also paying tribute to the sacrifice of Tibetan patriot Lobga Rangzen, who sacrificed his life for the cause of Tibet. The Tibetan Youth Congress also sent an open letter to the Embassy of People's Republic of China in New Delhi on the same day and they said,"This is not merely a letter. It is a message carried by the final sacrifice of Tibetan patriot Lobga Rangzen, whose body was engulfed in flames because our homeland had been occupied and our people deprived of their freedom. His last act was not one of despair, it was one of resistance. he raised the Tibetan National Flag and he stood on fire, and declared to the world: "Free Tibet, China Out of Tibet." "Rangzen Lobga sacrificed his life because, he view that the root cause of the Tibetan tragedy is simple: China occupied our country, we lost our independence and the continued political control exercised by the so-called People's Republic of China over Tibet. He sacrificed himself for the cause of Tibet and its Independence because decades of political repression, cultural destruction, restrictions on religious freedom, transnational repression, and now the implementation of the so-called "Ethnic Unity Law." "You call it a law of unity. In reality you are trying to legalize the genocide, a legal procedure design to erase the identity of oppressed people. A law that weakens a nation's language, religion, culture, and history cannot be called unity. Unity cannot be imposed through assimilation. Unity cannot be manufactured through fear. Unity without freedom is not unity at all. "For almost seven decades, the so-called Chinese Communist government has attempted to suppress and silence Tibetans inside Tibet and across the world. Military occupation, surveillance, imprisonment, propaganda, misinformation, disinformation campaigns, and enormous financial investment to reshape historical narratives, But failed to extinguish the Tibetan people's aspiration for freedom. "Despite immense pressure, Tibetans have not disappeared. They have become more resilient. Every attempt to erase our identity has strengthened our determination to preserve it. Every effort to silence us has inspired new voices to speak. Every sacrifice has produced a new generation committed to carrying forward the cause of Tibet. "The oppressor dream of creating "one big China" through coercion will remain only that a dream. so as long as Tibetans continue to preserve their national identity and seek justice. Ideas cannot be imprisoned. History cannot be rewritten simply through repetition. National identity cannot be erased by decree. "Rangzen Lobga made his message unmistakably clear: "the root cause of the Tibetan issue is that Tibet lost its independence after China took control of our land." "The Tibetan Youth Congress has never wavered in its position. We firmly stands and believe that the Tibetan people have the right to determine their own future, and our mission remains unchanged: to reclaim our country, Tibet, from the foreign occupation. "This is perhaps one of the most important moments for the so-called Government of the People's Republic of China to resume sincere and meaningful dialogue with the Tibetan Government in Exile, Dialogue is not a sign of weakness. It is the mark of confidence. Nations secure in their legitimacy do not fear conversation. History has shown that governments can suppress protests, imprison individuals, and control information, but they cannot permanently extinguish a people's aspiration for freedom and dignity. "The world has changed. Information travels across borders in seconds. Voices cannot be silenced as they once were. Attempts to conceal injustice face greater international scrutiny than ever before. Rangzen Lobga's sacrifice will not never be a forgotten chapter despite will be the source of motivation. It should serve as a warning that unresolved political conflicts continue to carry profound human consequences. "We therefore call upon the so-called Government of the People's Republic of China to end its illegal occupation of Tibet and respect the Tibetan people's inherent right to self-determination. "The Chinese government must recognize the legitimate aspiration of the Tibetan people and restore Tibet's independence. Lasting peace and stability cannot be achieved through repression, forced assimilation, or military control, but only by ending occupation and respecting the will of the Tibetan people. We urge China to choose justice over oppression, freedom over domination, and peace over continued confrontation. "History will judge not only those who resisted oppression, but also those who had the opportunity to pursue peace and chose otherwise. Act now or regret later," the Tibetan activists of Tibetan Youth Congress said. Photo: File Dharamshala — The Chinese authorities have demolished thousands of residences of Tibetan monks and nuns in Larung Gar, the world’s largest Tibetan Buddhist institute, since 2001. The latest wave of demolitions began in mid-July and is set to destroy 1,060 dwellings of monks and nuns. These demolitions took place following the implementation of China’s new law, so-called the “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress,” which came into effect on July 1, 2026. According to these sources, on July 13, 2026, Chinese authorities began to demolish at least 1,060 dwellings belonging to monks and nuns at the Larung Five Sciences Buddhist Academy, better known as Larung Gar (monastery), located in Sertar County in eastern Tibet; at least six dwellings were demolished till July 15, 2026. These actions occurred following the implementation of so-called China's new “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress” on July 1, 2026, which targets the Tibetan language, identity, culture, and religion as part of a policy of Sinicization and imposes the assimilation of Tibetans into Chinese culture through public institutions. "The demolitions in Larung Gar began around July 13, 2026, and are being carried out at night, which is seen as a tactic by the authorities to prevent public documentation, media coverage, and satellite monitoring. As of July 15, 2026, six dwellings had been demolished, and Chinese authorities continue to destroy the residences; they have targeted at least 1,060 dwellings belonging to monks and nuns for demolition as part of this latest phase of demolitions," the sources said. In 2001, Chinese authorities launched their first large-scale demolition and forced eviction operations at the Larung Gar Buddhist Academy, targeting thousands of monastic dwellings. Since then, the Chinese government has intermittently resumed its destruction activities, notably launching a massive demolitionoperationin July 2016 that reportedly resulted in theexpulsionof more than 4,800 monks and nuns and the demolition of 4,700 dwellings; the most recent wave targeted at least 1,060 dwellings. The the Serta Larung Five Science Buddhist Academy was founded by Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok, Tibetan lama and great scholar in 1980 and has grown to the point where, it hosts between 10,000 and 40,000 residents. It is home to monks, nuns, and students from Tibet and China, as well as from other countries such as South Korea, Singapore, and Malaysia, while tens of thousands of people around the world study Buddhism through online courses taught by Sodargye Rinpoche, a prominent khenpo from Larung Gar. Despite the restrictions imposed by Chinese authorities on Tibetan Buddhism under Chinese occupation, Larung Gar has greatly contributed to the spread of this religion as well as to the preservation and international dissemination of Tibetan culture. Hundreds of eminent Buddhist scholars and practitioners have been educated at Larung Gar. Since the Chinese government began systematically demolishing Larung Gar, the European Parliament, United Nations special rapporteurs, numerous countries, and human rights organisations, including Human Rights have officially condemned the Chinese government’s destruction of Larung Gar and called on it to put an end to these demolitions. "China’s actions, in no doubts, constitute a gross violation of international human rights law, as well as its own Constitution, which obligates China to respect and protect the cultural, social, and religious rights of the Tibetan people. Instead, by forcing mass evictions of Tibetan monastic communities and replacing Tibetan self-governance with direct Chinese Communist Party administration, China is actively dismantling the very fabric of Tibetan life. The human toll of the Larung Gar crackdown that took place in 2016 and 2017 has been disastrous, resulting in profound psychological trauma and tragic suicides, such as the deaths of Tibetan nuns Tsering Dolma and Semgha amid the 2016 demolitions," the UN, EU, and the Human Rights Desk, Tibet Advocacy Section, DIIR, Central Tibetan Administration said. China-Tibet: The one-thing you need to know: Over the past 70 decades, there has been ongoing political repression, social discrimination, economic marginalization, environmental destruction, and cultural assimilation, particularly due to Chinese migration to Tibet which is fueling intense resentment among the people of occupied Tibet. The communist-totalitarian state of China began its invasion of Tibet in 1949, reaching complete occupation of the country in 1959. Since that time, more than 1.2 million people, 20% of the nation's population of six million, have died as a direct result of China's invasion and occupation. In addition, over 99% of Tibet's six thousand religious monasteries, temples, and shrines, have been looted or decimated resulting in the destruction of hundreds of thousands of sacred Buddhist scriptures. Until 1949, Tibet was an independent Buddhist nation in the Himalayas which had little contact with the rest of the world. It existed as a rich cultural storehouse of the Mahayana and Vajrayana teachings of Buddhism. Religion was a unifying theme among the Tibetans -- as was their own language, literature, art, and world view developed by living at high altitudes, under harsh conditions, in a balance with their environment. Tibetans also held a memorial service for Lobga Rangzen at the Tibetan Community Center in New York, followed by his funeral on June 6, 2026. All the Tibetans present were deeply saddened and overcome with grief by the passing of Lobga Rangzen, an independence activist of Tibet. Sikyong Penpa Tsering of the Central Tibetan Administration expressed deep sorrow over the self-immolation of a Tibetan activist, Lobga Rangzen (Lobsang Palden), in front of the UN Headquarters in New York City on 2 July 2026. Sikyong said,"I am deeply saddened by the devastating news of Lobga Rangzen's (Lobsang Palden) self-immolation in front of the UN Headquarters in New York City on July 2, 2026. In a video message posted hours prior, he made it clear that this ultimate sacrifice was undertaken for the Tibetan national cause. While we honor his devotion, human life is precious and must be preserved to serve the long-term struggle for Tibet." "On behalf of the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA), I earnestly urge all fellow Tibetans to cherish your lives. The unfolding genocide inside Tibet and the enforcement of the draconian "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law" on July 1 are what drove Lobga Rangzen la to this tragic decision. He joins at least 157 Tibetans inside Tibet who have offered their lives to draw global attention to the brutal repression endured under Chinese rule," Sikyong said. "Our deepest condolences go out to Lobga Rangzen la's family, friends, and the entire Tibetan community. On behalf of the CTA and the Tibetan people, I solemnly pledge that we will carry the spirit of these sacrifices in our hearts and work relentlessly so they are not in vain. I urgently call upon Tibetans in exile, world governments, and international human rights institutions to recognize the severe crisis inside Tibet, to stand up, and to speak out at this critical moment in our history," Sikyong concluded. Photo:Tenzin Wangdu Rangzen Dharamshala — More than 60 Tibetans shaved their heads in solidarity with Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen and all those who have sacrificed their lives for a free Tibet; Lobga Rangzen had set himself on fire in front of the United Nations headquarters to protest against China's illegal occupation of Tibet, its oppressive actions in the region, and the genocidal policies implementing in Tibet. This Head-shaving movement took place in front of United Nations headquarters, in New York, on July 30, 2026 and it is orgainsed by 19th Regional Tibetan Youth Congress of NY&NY. They said,"This act of sacrifice is a symbol of our unwavering commitment to justice, truth, and the independence of our nation. We call upon the United Nations to uphold the principles it was founded on and stand for justice. The world cannot remain silent." They collected the shaved hair and wrote "Justice for Lobga Rangzen" to commemorate Lhogar Rangren's sacrifice for a free and independent Tibet and to seek justice for him. They also shouted slogans such as "Justice for Lhogar Rangren," "Free Tibet," "China, out of Tibet now," and "United Nations, wake up" in front of the United Nations headquarters in New York. Following the head-shaving movement, hundreds of Tibetans gathered in front of the United Nations headquarters in New York, the site where Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen self-immolated. They protested China's forced invasion of Tibet, destruction of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, environmental damage, and the killing of over two million Tibetans, and its continued repressive and harsh policies against Tibetans, Tibetan culture, language, freedom of expression, religion, and belief, including the arrest, torture, and imprisonment of any Tibetan exercising their basic rights. During their protest, they held up signs that read: "UN, when will you stop being silenced by China?", "UN, how many more lives do you need?", "Tibet belongs to Tibetans, not China", "Communist China, hands off Tibet", We want an independent for Tibet", "Protect Tibet's Faith, Culture and Nation","Lobga Rangzen is a US citizen, we want justice". Jamphel Choesang, President of 19th Regional Tibetan Youth Congress New York/New Jersey addressed the gathering and said, "Dear Tibetan brothers and sisters, Today, I stand before you not only as the President of the 19th Regional Tibetan Youth Congress New York/New Jersey, but as a fellow Tibetan whose heart carries the same hope, pain, and unwavering love for our homeland. "Our martyrs gave everything they had for Tibet. They did not sacrifice for themselves—they sacrificed for all of us, for future generations, and for the dream of a free and independent Tibet. Their courage must never be forgotten, and their sacrifices must never be in vain. "Our beloved Pawo Lobga Rangzen la made the ultimate sacrifice to awaken the conscience of the world and to remind us that Tibet’s struggle is far from over. His message was clear: never give up on Tibet. "Today, I humbly call upon every Tibetan brother and sister: please stand up for our country. Join our protests whenever you can. Raise your voice for justice. Your presence matters. Every person standing together sends a powerful message that Tibet lives in our hearts and that we will never surrender our identity, our culture, or our dream of freedom. "Let us stand united—not divided. Let us work together as one family, one community, and one nation. When we support one another with respect, compassion, and determination, there is nothing stronger than our unity. "The responsibility to continue this movement belongs to every one of us. Whether young or old, student or professional, every effort counts. Every protest, every prayer, every act of service, and every voice raised for Tibet keeps the flame of our martyrs burning brightly. "Let us honor Pawo Lobga Rangzen la and all our martyrs not only with words, but through our actions. Let us continue the path they showed us with courage, discipline, and unwavering commitment. "We call upon the international community and the United Nations to hear the voices of the Tibetan people and to seek justice for Pawo Lobga Rangzen la. His sacrifice deserves to be remembered, and the Tibetan people’s aspirations deserve to be heard. "Together, let us pledge that we will never allow our martyrs’ sacrifices to be forgotten. We will continue to stand for truth, justice, and the freedom of Tibet until the day our nation is free." Photo:file Dharamshala — Shilong-led northeast India Tibetan People's Movement held a press conference at the Guwahatu Press Club, to address the ongoing human rights crisis in Tibet, which led to the self-immolation of Tibetan activist Lobga Rangzen, in front of UN headquarters in New York, on July 2, 2026. They told the media about who is Tibetan independent activist Lobga Rangzen and why he self-immolated in front of UN headquarters in New York. They further recalled China's invasion of Tibet and denounced the Chinese government's eradication of Tibetan language, identity, culture, and religion in the name of so-called China's “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress"; finally they rejected the law by tearing the law paper, in front of reporters. Shilong-led northeast India Tibetan People's Movement, planned to organise a large peaceful protest in Guwahati (Assam) on July 29, 2026, to protest against China's so-called "Ethnic Unity Law" and demand freedom, justice, and respect for human rights in Tibet. Tibetans from various northeastern states—including Dimapur (Nagaland), Tawang (Arunachal Pradesh), Tezpur (Assam), Shillong (Meghalaya), and Guwahati (Assam)—were set to participate; however, due to flooding in Assam, the demonstration had to be postponed, and a press conference was held instead on the originally scheduled date of July 29, 2026. Two former members of Tibetan Parliament-in-exile, Tsering Dolma and Yangchen Dolkar, Tenzin sangmo, media coordinator and Youndoung, secretary of Shilong-led northeast India Tibetan People's Movement held the press conference. The statement of the Shilong-led northeast India Tibetan People's Movement said," Lobga Rangzen, a 52-year-old Tibetan activist, died after a self-immolation protest he carried out in front of the UN headquarters in New York City on July 2, 2026. He called for the restoration of Tibet's independence and spoke against the imposition of China's "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law" that went into force on July 1 in Tibet. Tibetans reject this law as it is designed to legitimise the imposition of sinicization policies in Tibet. Tibetans are not an ethnic minority of China to be subjected to its ethnic unity law in the name of unity and progress. "In 1950, the People's Liberation Army entered Tibet, fundomentally changing the course of Tibetan history. Following the 1959 Tibetan Uprising, His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama and approximately 80,000 Tibetans fled into exile in India. Since China's military occupation of Tibet, Tibetans have lived under policies that many governments, UN experts and international human rights organisations say have severely restricted fundamental rights. "More than 170 Tibetans have self-immolated since 2009, pealing in 2012 with 85 self-immolations in one year. All the self-immolators unanimously called for freedom in Tibet, the protection of Tibetan Identity, the return of His Holiness the Dalai lama to Tibet, and unity among Tibetans. His Holiness the 14th Dalal Lama and the exile government continue to make efforts toward peaceful resolution of the Sino-Tibetan conflict through its "Middle Way Approach". However, China has only turned a cold shoulder to the proposals and responds with rhetoric that undermines the spirit of dialogue. It has put the Tibetans in a difficult position of experiencing the worsening human rights situation in Tibet, while watching China intensify its hold on Tibet. Self-Immolations don't occur in a vacuum, but as a result of deep-seated anguish and exhaustion of tangible recourse. "On July 1, 2026, China's "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law" come into force. According to the Chinese government, the law "promotes national unity". However, eight UN human rights experts and international human rights organisations have warned that it further institutionalizes policies affecting the linguistic, cultural and religious rights of ethnic minorities. There are major factual inaccuracies in the law and in the UN response: • Tibet is not part of China to be absorbed into the project of national unity• Tibetans are minoritised by the Chinese occupation and are not one of the ethnic minority groups China claims to constitute.• China is ethnically Han Chinese dominated, with no historical, cultural, racial, linguistic or political association with the Tibetans, except as the dominast race of the colonising power. "On the ground in Tibet, the law has real time impact on education, language, religion and cultural rights as it mandates cultural integration. The single Chinese national identity it promotes includes provisions with extraterritorial application, raising concerns that it could exacerbate the patterns of transnational repression against individuals and organisations globally. For many Tibetans, the law is seen not as a new policy but as the formal codification of decades of assimilation measures through instrumentalisation of law. "Why should India and northeast care for Tibet. The Tibetan Plateau forms much of the strategic frontier between India and China. Since China's occupation of Tibet, the Himalayan region has become one of Asia's most heavily militarised borders. China has escalated its territorial claims over Arunachal Pradesh, referring to it as "South Tibet," and maintains unresolved border disputes with India in eastern Ladakh. These disputes have contributed to recurring military tensions, including the 2020 Galwan Valley clash. "For the people of Northeast India, Tibet is not only a human rights issue—it is also an environmental and regional concern. The Brahmaputra (Yarlung Tsangpo) originates on the Tibetan Plateau before flowing through Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, sustaining millions of people. Decisions affecting Tibet's rivers and fragile ecosystem-including dam construction, hydropower stations, water diversion, and mining have implications for communities downstream that constitute two billion people." Photo: File Washington — U.S Senator Jacky Rosen,Jeff Merkley, John Curtis, and Jim Banks, introduced a Bipartisan Resolution on the China's “Ethnic Unity and Progress Law” in US Senate on June 24, 2026. The resolution condemns China’s "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law," which entered into force on 1 July 2026, and calls on Beijing to end abuses against ethnic and religious minorities, as well as campaigns of transnational repression affecting people in the United States. The resolution highlighted human rights violations in Tibet, the forced placement of more than one million Tibetan children in colonial-style boarding schools; it also emphasized that the Chinese authorities are violating the fundamental rights and freedoms guaranteed by the Chinese Constitution and international law. It further detailed how the Chinese Communist government imposes repressive policies—both old and new—on Tibetans in Chinese-occupied Tibet; as well as the Sinicisation of the Tibetan language, culture, and religion; the People’s Republic of China’s attempt to control the reincarnation of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama of Tibet; and China’s Ethnic Unity Law, which undermines the unity of minority groups. The resolution states, "Condemning the People's Republic of China's Ethnic Unity and Progress Law, concerned with its implications on the rights and freedoms, as well as survival of the identity, of Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, and other affected communities, and calling on the Government of the People's Republic of China to end its abuses and campaigns of transnational repression that undermine United States sovereignty and threaten the safety and freedoms of people in the United States. "The Constitution of the People's Republic of China guarantees specified rights, including freedom of religious belief and the right of people regarded as minorities to use their own spoken and written languages and preserve their cultural traditions. The People's Republic of China is a State Party to the Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR) and is a signatory to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights. "Chinese authorities have systematically imposed policies that displace ethnic and religious minority communities, separate Tibetan and Uyghur children from their families through state-run boarding schools, limit the use of minority languages, curtail religious practice through intrusive state controls, and compel conformity with ideology mandated by the Chinese Communist Party. "The policies of the People's Republic of China have threatened the rights and freedoms of a broad range of communities, including Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, Christians, and other ethnic and religious groups across China, as well as the people of Hong Kong whose civil liberties and autonomy have been systematically eroded in recent years. "The July 1, 2026, entry into force of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law of the People's Republic of China institutionalizes and expands coercive assimilation and cultural erasure policies directed toward Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, Christians, and other groups.The Ethnic Unity and Progress Law codifies the Chinese Communist Party's campaign of "Sinicization," requiring schools, religious institutions, families, media, and cultural organizations to align their activities with Party-mandated ideology. "The Ethnic Unity and Progress Law criminalizes expression deemed to "undermine ethnic unity" or "create ethnic division", the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law contains extraterritorial provisions authorising Chinese authorities to pursue "legal responsibility" for individuals and organizations outside China, which includes United States citizens who "undermine ethnic unity" or challenge the Chinese Communist Party's official historical narratives." "The Ethnic Unity and Progress Law expands state authority over religious institutions in ways that threaten the ability of Tibetan Buddhist leaders to determine matters of religious tradition, including the succession of the Dalai Lama; and the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law represents a grave escalation in the campaign of the People's Republic of China to suppress ethnic, religious, cultural, and linguistic diversity and, when combined with the Chinese Government's expanding campaigns of transnational repression, illegal overseas police operations, and extraterritorial claims of authority, poses a growing threat to the United States and its allies. Resolved, That the Senate-(1) condemns the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law for institutionalizing coercive assimilation, cultural erasure, and ideological control over ethnic and religious minorities in the People's Republic of China;(2) reaffirms support for the fundamental rights and freedoms of Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, Hui Muslims, Christians, and other ethnic and religious communities in the People's Republic of China;(3) reaffirms the 2021 determination of the United States Department of State that the Government of the People's Republic of China is committing genocide and crimes against humanity against Uyghurs and other predominantly Muslim Turkic people,(4) calls on the Government of the People's Republic of China to repeal the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law;(5) urges the United States Department of State to work with allies and partners, including the European Union, Canada, Japan, Australia, and the United Kingdom, to monitor and report on the impacts of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law and on going transnational repression carried out by the People's Republic of China;(6) calls on the President to evaluate and consider targeted sanctions under the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act (22 U.S.C. 10101et seq.) against individuals and entities responsible for, complicit in, or directly benefiting from gross human rights violations that result from implementing the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law and related laws and policies;(7) recognizes the Dalai Lama and the Central Tibetan Administration for their longstanding commitment to nonviolence and dialogue and reaffirms that, in light of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law's expansion of state authority over religions institutions, decisions regarding the reincarnation or succession of the Dalai Lama are solely the prerogative of Tibetan Buddhist leaders and the Tibetan people, free from interference by the Government of the People's Republic of China, as outlined in the Tibetan Policy and Support Act of 2020; and(8) calls on the Government of the People's Republic of China to resume dialogue with the Dalai Lama or his representatives in order to hold substantive discussions aimed at resolution of the Sino-Tibetan disputes at an early date, without preconditions. Photo: TPI Dharamshala — Tibetans commemorated the 11th anniversary of the passing of Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche, who was assassinated by the Chinese government. They spoke about Rinpoche’s legacy and paid tribute to his bravery, highlighted Tenzin Delek Rinpoche’s contributions in the fields of education, environmental protection and social welfare; how his patriotic commitment and his work in the service of the community had become a source of growing concern for the authorities of the People’s Republic of China.. The Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche Service Committee and the Tibetan Center for Human Rights and Democracy (TCHRD) organised a memorial event on July 13, 2026, at Norbu House in Dharamsala to mark the 11th anniversary of Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche’s death. Rinpoche was murdered by Chinese authorities on July 12, 2015 in a Chinese prison, for fear of his influence on Tibetan society and for courageously protecting Tibetan religion, culture, language and environment. The event included the launch of a book in English recording the evidence of his assassination. The English translation of Nyima Lhamo’s book, titled > was launched by the Speaker of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, Dolma Tsering Teykhang. Speaker Dolma Tsering Teykhang, Tenzin Dawa, Director of the TCHRD, Dorjee Rinchen, author of Tenzin Delek Rinpoche’s books, and Geshe Tsering Dorjee, a student of Tenzin Delek Rinpoche, spoke about Rinpoche’s legacy and paid tribute to his courage and bravery, as he is a true representative of Tibetans who protect the Tibetan environment, teach the Tibetan language and culture as well as Buddhism to the people. More than 50 Tibetans from the Dharamsala area participated in this event. > original in Tibetan, told by Nyima Lhamo and written by Dorjee Rinchen,launchedin 2024; the Chinese version,publishedin 2025, was translated by Loya, while the English version >, launched on July 13, 2026, was translated by the Tibetan writer Bhuchung Sonam. The book is about how Tenzin Delek Rinpoche was arrested without any crime, how he suffered in the Chinese prison, how his students and local Tibetans pleaded for his release, how the Chinese authorities shot at peaceful followers and demonstrators, how Tibetans were beaten and arrested by the Chinese authorities and, finally, how he was murdered by the Chinese, and how the Chinese authorities refused to return Rinpoche's body to his family because they feared that the cause of death would become known to the world, how Rinpoche's niece Nyima Lhamo and other Tibetans were detained and tortured, how she tried to immolate herself in front of the Chinese prison etc. Geshe Tsering Dorjee introduced the event by stating that yesterday was the day, Tenzin Delek Rinpoche was murdered by the Chinese authorities while serving his sentence in a Chinese prison on July 12, 2015. “Today, I wanted to remind all of you of the importance of unity among Tibetans, because those were the last words Tenzin Delek Rinpoche spoke to me as I was preparing to go into exile. We must all unite and fight for our cause; one day, we will achieve our freedom,” he said. Author Dorjee Rinchen recounted how Tenzin Delek Rinpoche founded nine monasteries to promote Tibetan Buddhism, built schools for orphans and other children, and protected Tibet’s fragile environment and wildlife from being slaughtered. He also spoke about how the People’s Republic of China attempted to assassinate Tibetans who were influential figures in Tibetan society, such as Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche, Khenchen Jigme Phuntso, and Geshe Sonam Phuntso in Karze, and how the same thing occurred in other Tibetan regions. These are repressive policies carried out by the Chinese Communist government aimed at eliminating Tibetans, along with their culture, identity, and religion. Speaker Dolma Tsering Teykhang spoke about the courage of Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche by recounting how Rinpoche had secretly met with the first fact-finding delegation from the Tibetan government-in-exile, which included Lobsang Samten, the elder brother of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama. During this meeting, he provided first-hand accounts of the destruction of Lithang Monastery and of the severe restrictions imposed by the People’s Republic of China (PRC) on religious freedom in the region. He also explained how Tenzin Delek Rinpoche had met the 10th Panchen Lama, briefed him in detail on the situation in Lithang and consulted him on the reconstruction of the monasteries at Ngachu and Lithing counties. The Speaker also highlighted Tenzin Delek Rinpoche’s contributions in the fields of education, environmental protection and social welfare; he further explained how his patriotic commitment and his work in the service of the community had become a source of growing concern for the authorities of the People’s Republic of China. Nyima Lhamo, niece of Tenzin Delek Rinpoche said, "Today marks 11 years since the tragic and unjust death of Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche, a revered Tibetan lama, educator, environmentalist, and cultural leader who died under suspicious circumstances after 13 years of imprisonment and relentless torture at the hands of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP)." "His only “crime” was his unwavering commitment to preserving Tibetan religion, identity, and human rights — values that the CCP considers a threat to its authoritarian rule. The CCP feared Rinpoche’s popularity, moral authority, and influence among Tibetans, and thus silenced him through violence and oppression," she added. title: CTA and Tibetans mourn the demise of Kasur Chope Paljor Tsering - Tibet Post International
content: Dharamshala — Central Tibetan Administration and Tibetans mourned the demise of Kasur Chope Paljor Tsering, who devoted more than four decades of dedicated service to His Holiness the Dalai Lama, the Tibetan people, and the Tibetan cause. He has served as the Kalon for Department of Health during the 13th Kashag and served over two decades as the Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama in various countries. The former Kalon Chope Paljor Tsering passed away on June 11, 2026 in Australia. Central Tibetan Administration held a prayer service on June 12, 2026, in Dharamshala, to mourn the passing of former Kalon (Kasur) Choepe Paljor Tsering Namru Ringpapo Ntsang. Kasur Chope was born in 1948 in Namru, in the Northern Tibet. Following the Communist Chinese invasion of Tibet, he fled with his family at around the age of ten. The family eventually settled in Pokhara, Nepal. In 1966, he served as the translator during the establishment of the Tashi Ling Tibetan settlement in Pokhara. From 1968 to 1970, he studied in the United Kingdom before returning to Tashi Ling to serve as a teacher and, later, school principal. From 1973, he served as Tibetan Settlement Officer of Dhorpatan, northern Nepal. From 1978 Kasur Chope served at the Office of the Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama in Nepal. He was then transferred to the Department of Education in Dharamshala as its Deputy Secretary on April 26, 1982. Returning to Nepal, he served as the Central Tibetan Administration’s Education Officer for Nepal. From May 1986, Kasur Chope served as the Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama in Nepal. He went on to serve as Representative for Eastern Europe (1991–1998), for Australasia (1998–2002), and finally for Japan and East Asia (2002–2007). With twenty-one years in the role, he was the longest-serving Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama thus far. In 2007, he was unanimously elected to the 13th Kashag (Cabinet) by the Tibetan Parliament in Exile and served as Kalon (Minister) for Department of Health until 2011. In retirement, he continued to work to preserve and promote Tibetan language and culture through the Global Tibet Institute. He also a book named "The Nature of All Things: The Life Story of a Tibetan in Exile" , an autobiography which recounts his childhood in Tibet, life as a refugee and his experiences in serving His Holiness the Dalai Lama, Tibetan people and Tibetan cause. title: US senators call on PRC to rescind the law aimed at erasing the unique identity of the Tibetan - Tibet Post International
content: Washington, D.C. — In a letter addressed to the Chinese ambassador to the United States, U.S. Senators Lindsey Graham and Sheldon Whitehouse expressed their deep concern regarding the “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress” enacted by the PRC, warning that this law aims to eliminate the distinct identities, religious freedoms, and fundamental rights of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and other ethnic minorities. They further stated that this new law violates the Chinese Constitution and international law, and that it must be repealed. Senators Lindsey O. Graham (Republican) and Sheldon Whitehouse (Democrat) sent a bipartisan letter to Xie Feng, China’s ambassador to the United States, on June 25, 2026. In the letter, they expressed deep concern regarding the “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress” enacted by the People’s Republic of China, warning that this law aims to eliminate the distinct identities, religious freedoms, and fundamental rights of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and other ethnic minorities. They further stated that this new law violates the Chinese Constitution and international law, and that it must be repealed. The senators stated that they joined the European Parliament in condemning the so-called "Ethic Unity law," which is set to take effect on July 1, 2026 and called on the Chinese government to repeal it or revise it thoroughly. They added that they would closely monitor the Chinese Communist Party’s implementation of the law, particularly its impact on Tibetans, Uyghurs and others. The senators wrote in the letter to China’s ambassador to the United States,"We write with grave concern regarding the troubling implications of the People's Republic of China's new Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress which will enter into force on July 1." "As bipartisan and elected representatives of the U.S. Senate, we join the European Union Parliament in condemning the Law's passage and anticipated implementation. We are closely watching actions the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) takes under the Law and would urge your government to rescind or significantly revise the Law given its ramifications on those beyond the borders of the People's Republic of China and on the protection of distinct identities and human rights of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and other nationalities," they added. "We are extremely concerned about Article 63 of the Law, which states "Organizations and individuals outside the [mainland] territory of the People's Republic of China that commit acts aimed at the People's Republic of China that undermine ethnic unity and progress or create ethnic division are to be pursued for legal responsibility in accordance with law." Please be aware that any attempts to surveil, intimidate, or pressure individuals residing in the United States, under Article 63 or any provision of that Law or any other, constitute an unacceptable violation of U.S. sovereignty," they further said. The US senators said, "We are deeply troubled by the codification of the CCP's longstanding practices to extinguish religious freedom, including restrictions on worship, forced ideological instruction, and pressure on communities to abandon or dilute their faith traditions. These practices affect Tibetan Buddhists, Muslims, Christians, and many others - under the guise of combatting extremism and/or preventing separatism." "We are also alarmed by the law's implications for children's rights, particularly in the state-run boarding schools affecting more than one million Tibetan children who have been separated from their families, language, and heritage. Your implementation of the Law will be evaluated for compliance with standards for the protection of children," they said. "Let us be clear: We will not hold back from speaking out when laws or practices violate fundamental rights, including the rights of individuals living on U.S. soil, children's rights, and religious freedoms. The Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress is detrimental to and attempts to eliminate the unique identities of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and others. Furthermore, this Law appears to be at odds with China's own constitution, 1984 Regional Ethnic Autonomy Law, and international commitments," said Senators Lindsey Graham and Sheldon Whitehouse. title: "China's Colonial Game in Tibet" launches ahead of Tibetan National Uprising Day - Tibet Post International
content: Dharamshala — "China's Colonial Game in Tibet" was launched in Dharamsala on March 6, 2026, a few days before Tibetan Uprising Day on March 10, 2026. This book talks about the independent status of Tibet, His Holiness the Dalai Lama, the reincarnation of the Dalai Lama, the Tibetan cultural genocide, the destruction of the environment, education as a colonial tool under the Chinese Communist government, the Tibetan freedom movement, and Tibetan self-immolations. This book brings together 39 authors, including Professor Samdhong Rinpoche, Sikyong Penpa Tsering, Claude Arpi, Professor Robert Destro, Geshe Lhador, Chemi Lhamo, and was edited by Vijay Kranti, a veteran Indian journalist and long-time supporter of Tibet. It is published by the Centre for Himalayan Asia Studies And Engagement (CHASE) in New Delhi. The book launch took place in the hall of the Tibetan Settlement Office, in Dharamshala, on March 6, 2026. Tibetan activist Tenzin Tsundue moderated the event, and Vijay Kranti spoke about his new book, Tsering Choephel, President of the Tibetan Youth Congress, delivered a speech of thanks. Tibetan journalists and Tibetans around the Dharamshala were present at the press conference. While talking about the book, Vijay Kranti said, "CHASE, in collaboration with Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) organised about 30 international webinars on various hot issues related to Tibet and China during 2020-2023 period. We focused on some of the best and experienced communicators as our experts who understand these issues and have long experience in reaching out to their audiences. Finally we selected about 15 webinars which were focused on those issues which Tibet supporters have been raising at various international forums and which present the most inhuman and prominent dimensions of China’s colonial games in Tibet." "Our main challenge was to reproduce the spoken presentations of these experts over the audio-visual platform into essay like written words and present it in the form of a book. This way it is our endeavor to present a wholesome narration of all major colonial problems and issues, being faced by the people of Tibet, into a single book," Vijay Kranti explained. He also spoke about the repressive policies faced by Tibetans in Tibet and the Tibetans who have set themselves on fire to demand freedom in Tibet and the return of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. He said, "Unfortunately this silence of governments, international organizations – especially the United Nations -- and the most influential international media houses who claim to be the greatest champions of human rights and freedom of expression, have been perpetually found wanting on what is going on inside China-occupied colonies like Tibet. Almost all of them have failed individually as well as collectively to take any meaningful action against the blatantly inhuman acts of the Chinese regime against its own people as well as its colonial subjects in occupied countries of Tibet, East Turkestan (Ch: ‘Xinjiang’), Southern Mongolia and Hong Kong." "The saddest and most unfortunate part of this game is that while China’s communist masters have been successful in keeping a strong lid on all these developments, the international community has, in effect, chosen to keep its eyes closed and mouth shut against this ongoing crime against the most helpless section of human society. Hence the need for waking up the world’s conscience before it is too late," he added. He further said, "With the help of 39 well informed experts, observers and researchers from across the world, it is our endeavor at Centre for Himalayan Asia Studies and Engagement (CHASE) to present authentic information on these as well as many other aspects of the colonial games being played by China’s communist masters in China’s colonies. This book is the first and the Tibetan installment in this direction. It is our endeavor to present similar studies on China’s other colonies like East Turkestan, S. Mongolia, Hong Kong, Manchuria etc. in near future." "CHASE organised over 30 international webinars on major issues related to Tibet and China. We organized these webinars with the active participation of Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) which is the largest and true representative of the struggle and aspirations of the people of Tibet – living in exile as well as those living inside Chinese occupied Tibet. We had the privilege of enrolling some of the best known experts and experienced communicators from across the globe who understands these issues deeply. Out of these 30 webinars we have selected 15 which were focused on all those issues related to the denial of human rights to the people of Tibet as a part of the colonial games which the Chinese Communist Party and its leaders have been playing inside Tibet since its occupation in 1951. This collection of essays and presentations covers almost all such issues related to Tibet and China which have been, time and again, raised at various international forums but not followed up to their logical end. This way it has been the endeavor of CHASE to make this book a unique platform which presents a complete, honest and fearless account of all those colonial games which are being played inside occupied Tibet by its Chinese colonial masters," the Vijay Kranti, President of CHASE concluded his talk. Vijay Kranti is a veteran journalist, Tibetologist and photographer. Over past 50 years he has been on the staff of reputed media groups which include India Today, BBC TV, Zee News TV, Aaj Tak TV, DD News, German Radio Deutsche Welle, Radio Voice of America etc. His main focus areas have been Himalayan Buddhist Culture, Tibet, China and J&K. In 1992 he was awarded KK Birla Foundation Fellowship for journalists for his work on Tibet. His study and research on issues related to Tibet and China has received acknowledgement and appreciation at international levels. He is regularly invited to international conferences, seminars, online webinars, TV and Radio shows to speak on these subjects as an expert. Tibet History Independence

title: "Tibet has never been a part of China since ancient times": CTA - Tibet Post International
content: Dharamshala — Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) organised an event to commemorate the 67th National Uprising of Tibet in Dharamshala, on March 10, 2026. Kashag (Cabinet) states, "Tibet has never been a part of China since ancient times and is rather a nation under the illegal occupation of the communist PRC. The fact that the question of Tibet is not an internal affair of China, but rather an unresolved international conflict." Central Tibetan Administration organised the event to commemorate the 67th National Uprising of Tibet in the courtyard of Thekchen Choeling Tsuglakhang, Dharamshala, on March 10, 2026. Dignitaries including Michael Brand, Member of the German Parliament and Parliamentary State Secretary, Germany; Hans-Gert Pöttering, Former President of the European Parliament; Jiří Oberfalzer, Vice President of the Czech Senate; and Juris Vilums, Member of Parliament, Latvia. Brian Joseph, Vice President, National Endowment for Democracy (NED), Cheng Lei, from Australia, Shri R.K Khrimey, National Convenor of Core Group for Tibetan Cause-India, Ms Alice Parma, Italian State parliamentarian, Senator Jiri Dusek, Vice-chairman of the Committee on EU, and Dr Wiebke Winter, Member of Legislative Assembly, Germany. Participants of the Special International Tibet Support Groups Meeting also presented there as special guests and top officals of CTA and Tibetans around the Dharamshala joined the commemoration of the the 67th National Uprising of Tibet. Sikyong Penpa Tsering hoisted of Tibetan National Flag and sang the Tibetan and Indian National Anthem. Then observed a minute of silence as a mark of respect for the Tibetan Martyrs who have sacrificed their lives for the cause of Tibet. March 10 commemoration song sang by the members of the Tibetan Institute of Performing Arts. Then Sikyong read out the statement of Kashag on the the 67th Anniversary of the Tibetan National Uprising Day and he said," Today marks the 67th anniversary of the 1959 Tibetan National Uprising, when Tibetans from all three provinces, monastics and laypeople alike, rose in unison with indomitable courage in Tibet’s capital, Lhasa, to protest the illegal invasion by the People’s Republic of China (PRC) and to safeguard the person of His Holiness the Fourteenth Dalai Lama from imminent threat. On this solemn occasion, the Kashag pays its deepest tribute to all the martyrs who made the ultimate sacrifice for the sake of Tibet, its faith, and its people, and stands in unwavering solidarity with our brothers and sisters inside Tibet, whose resolve to preserve our distinct national identity remains as unyielding as Mount Meru, even in the face of relentless oppression by the government of the PRC. We also express our sincere gratitude to all our distinguished guests present here today for their powerful demonstration of solidarity with the Tibetan people, and to all nations, organizations, and individuals around the world who continue to support the cause of Tibet. " "At present, the government of the PRC is falsely asserting that Tibet and all non-Han nationalities are part of the constructed “Zhonghua Minzu.” It is mobilizing, under the proclaimed mandate of “forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation,” the full machinery of the state to carry out expansive and deeply entrenched policies within Tibet aimed at eradicating both Tibet’s physical environment and its people’s distinct national identity." "The reckless destruction of the Tibetan Plateau, a strategic geographical region also known as the ‘Water Tower of Asia,’ does not merely impact the two billion people who depend on Tibet’s rivers, but also threatens the interests of the entire world in our collective effort to confront the global climate crisis," he added. The statement of the Kashag states, "Tibet has never been a part of China since ancient times and is rather a nation under the illegal occupation of the communist PRC. The fact that the question of Tibet is not an internal affair of China, but rather an unresolved international conflict, has been clearly established in the “Promoting a Resolution to the Tibet-China Dispute Act” enacted by the U.S. government. Regarding the reincarnation of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, the international community, through around 134 formal pronouncements, including legislations, resolutions, and declarations, categorically rejects the PRC’s so-called three conditions put forth in complete disregard for religious tradition and with an abandonment of political morality, and asserts a unified stance of non-recognition whatsoever. Nevertheless, the PRC continues to push its malicious agenda inside China and Tibet. Alongside its intensifying propaganda campaigns, the PRC government is exploiting its state-appointed Panchen Gyaltsen Norbu and a handful of lamas and monks through staged meetings and scripted speeches. It is certain that such orchestrated attempts will never be accepted by anyone, neither now nor at any point in the future. " Khenpo Sonam Tenphel, Speaker of the Tibetan Parliaments-in-Exile read out the statement of the TPiE on the 67th Anniversary of the Tibetan National Uprising Day and he said,"Throughout the period that Tibet has remained under the illegal occupation of China since its armed invasion, the government of China has kept distorting the country’s historical sovereignty with fabricated narratives, sought to corrupt the unique culture of the Tibetan people by adulterating it, used coercion to deprive the people of Tibet of their freedom of religious belief, set out to devastate the territorial and natural environment of Tibet, kept trampling on the human rights of the Tibetan people, shut them up from exercising their freedom of speech, colonized Tibet in the name of economic development and progress, made active efforts to prevent any expression of the oneness of the nationality of the Tibetan people, and disregarded the wishes of the Tibetan people. Apart from these, the ground reality remains that the government of China has thus far never implemented any genuinely intended policy measure which is suited to the needs of the Tibetan people. Rather, it has relied solely on policies of violent reprisal and brutal repression against the people of Tibet. As a result, the Tibetan people, both the old and new generations, have carried out a succession of protest demonstrations in a campaign that began in 1987. In particular, the great Earth-Mouse Year uprising protests carried out simultaneously by the people of all the three traditional provinces of Tibet in 2008, still remain fresh in our minds. Along with that, it is worth noting that since the year 2009, there have been a total of at least 157 incidents in which individual Tibetans in occupied Tibet have carried out protest self-immolations in acts of a non-violent campaign against the government of China. These various types of protests continue to be carried out by the Tibetan people to this day. It is important that the government of China appreciate the enormity of the sacrifices the Tibetan people have been making through those protest campaigns." Above guests addressed the assembly and reaffirmed their support for the Tibetan cause and the fight for freedom and human rights for the Tibetan people. They criticised the Chinese Communist government for violating the human rights of Tibetans, forcing more than a million Tibetan children as young as four into Chinese colonial-style boarding schools, destroying the Tibetan environment, and interfering in the reincarnation of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama.
