title: Two U.S. Bodies Convene China Rights Hearing Before Xi's Arrival
content: Dharamshala — Ranking Member Ro Khanna of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and Ranking Member Jim McGovern of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China jointly held a shadow hearing titled "The Void in China Policy: Why Human Rights Must Be on Trump’s Agenda with Xi at the White House," on September 15, 2026. The testimony featured a panel of witnesses, including Tahir Imin, Founder and Director, Uyghur Post, Palden Gyal, President, International Tibet Media Organization, Yaqiu Wang, Fellow at the Penn Project on the Future of U.S.-China Relations at the University of Pennsylvania, Jonathan Stivers, U.S. Director, Committee for Freedom in Hong Kong; Commissioner, U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission. Representative Greg Stanton said, "In 2024, 650,000 Tibetans were forced from the homes as part of a CCP program to systematically transfer what it called “rural surplus labor.” Since 2000, it is estimated that almost 3.5 million Tibetans have been forced from their homes by the CCP, including through what are called "old village relocation" programs. In 1963, images of a Buddhist monk setting himself on fire to protest the South Vietnamese government shocked the conscience of our world. Since 2009, at least 170 Tibetans have self-immolated to protest the CCP's repression. We have to ask ourselves: where is the conscience of our world today?." Ranking Member McGovern said,"We convene this hearing to shine a light on the severe violations of human rights by the government of China, and to assess our government's performance in holding it accountable. Human rights in China has long been an area of bipartisan concern and productivity here in the Congress. I think of Congresswoman Nancy Pelosi standing in Tiananmen Square with Republican and Democratic colleagues in 1991, bravely unfurling a banner to the victims of the massacre before being whisked away by police." "I think of President George W. Bush and the bipartisan House and Senate leadership in 2007 presenting the Congressional Gold Medal to His Holiness the Dalai Lama. I think of Marco Rubio and myself as co-chairs of the CECC, working together to craft and pass the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act of 2021 into law. I think of institutions we created to monitor the Chinese government's behavior, the CECC, Select Committee, the U.S. Security and Economic Review Commission – and we welcome one of its commissioners today as a witness. There has been consensus that U.S. policy toward China must include a moral dimension; that we must speak out for the freedoms of those who cannot advocate for themselves. That we must deploy policy tools to press the Chinese government to respect human rights," McGovern added. Speaker Emerita Pelosi said,"if we do not speak up for human rights in China because of commercial interest, we lose all moral authority to speak up for human rights any place in the world." Representative Seth Moulton said,"China under Xi Jinping has spent the past decade and a half systematically eroding the rights of everyone living in China. For most of that time, the United States has pushed back in a strongly bipartisan manner." In his statement, Palden Gyal said," Since taking control of Tibet, the CCP has used many tactics to erase Tibetan identity. I know this firsthand, having been born in Tibet and lived there until I was 20, when I escaped into exile. During a brief opening in the 1980s, Tibetans worked hard to preserve their heritage. By the 1990s, the CCP saw that Tibetan language and traditions kept the Tibetan spirit alive, so it began targeting monasteries and schools directly." "In 1996, Beijing launched its "Patriotic Education" campaign, forcing monks, nuns, and students to accept Chinese rule and the Party's version of history. Work teams entered monasteries daily to carry out indoctrination. Monks and nuns are forced to recognize Beijing's chosen Panchen Lama, and denounce His Holiness the Dalai Lama," he added. He continued by saying,"Tibetans have never stopped resisting. Major protests broke out in the late 1980s and in 2008. More than 170 Tibetans have set themselves on fire to protest Chinese repression. Loga Rangzen, a Tibetan American, was the latest, setting himself on fire outside the United Nations building in New York this July 2, 2026." "On March 12, 2026, China's National People's Congress passed a sweeping new law-the 65-article, so-called "Ethnic Unity and Progress Promotion Law"- effective July 1. It pressures Tibetans to give up their language, religion, and traditions and assimilate into mainstream Chinese culture, makes Chinese the primary language of instruction, and expands the state boarding school system," he explained. "China keeps tight control over information coming out of Tibet. Independent journalists are not allowed in. This matters for human rights. Without outside observers, the government can hide abuses. It also gets to decide what story the world hears. That is why restoring Tibetan-language broadcasts by Voice of America (VOA) and Radio Free Asia (RFA) is so important," he said. Palden said, "On September 24, Xi Jinping will visit Washington seeking better relations with the US. But in Tibet, Beijing is accelerating its campaign to erase Tibetan culture under the misleading banner of "ethnic unity." "What is happening today is, in some ways, more dangerous than the Cultural Revolution. The CCP is deliberately cutting generational ties to force complete assimilation. Starting in kindergarten, Chinese is the only language of instruction and nearly one million Tibetan children have been taken from their families and placed in state-run boarding schools," he said. "Just days ago, an 87-year-old grandmother in Tibet told me: 'My heart is warm because His Holiness the Dalai Lama is still alive. But I am deeply saddened because my grandchildren speak to me only in Chinese. I cannot understand them, and we cannot talk.' Her words show how quickly the Tibetan language is disappearing. Losing it means losing an ancient civilization," he explained. Palden further said, "China's Ethnic Unity Law doesn't just apply inside China—it applies to citizens of other countries. Article 63 says China can prosecute anyone, anywhere, for 'undermining ethnic unity.' This means Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, or any American who simply supports their rights could be prosecuted." "I know for certain that any action undertaken by the United States impacts the people of Tibet. Therefore, I would like to make the following recommendations for the US to hold the Chinese government accountable and stand with the Tibetan people in defense of their fundamental rights—these will be a powerful message to Xi Jinping when he visits Washington later this I urge Congress to pass the recently introduced Assuring the Future of Tibet Act (AFTA), which affirmed Tibet's future must be decided by the Tibetan people themselves," he said. "I urge President Trump to directly raise Tibet in his meeting with Xi Jinping, urging him to respect Tibetan human rights and religious freedom and to resume dialogue with His Holiness the Dalai Lama and his representatives," he concludede his statement. Tibet Human Rights China USA

title: TYC pays tribute to the brave Tibetan martyrs on its anniversary
content: Dharamshala — The Tibetan Youth Congress celebrated its anniversary in Dharamsala on Wednesday. They said, "We pay solemn tribute to the brave Tibetan martyrs who have sacrificed their lives, freedom, and livelihoods for the survival of the Tibetan nation, the preservation of our religion, language and culture, and the restoration of Tibet’s independence." The Regional Tibetan Youth Congress (RTYC) in Dharamsala organised a ceremony to mark its anniversary on October 7, 2026, in the hall of the Tibetan Community Office in McLeod Ganj, Dharamsala, Himachal Pradesh, India. Tibetan MP Gyaltsen Choekye was the guest of honour; special guests included Tashi Dharjee, Vice-President of the TYC, and Rangzen Dhondup, President of RTYC Dharamshala. Tsering Tharchen, Secretary-General of the RTYC, hosted the event, which was attended by members of Tibetan NGOs as well as Tibetans. Tsering Tharchen said, "On the occasion of the 56th Founding Anniversary of the Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC), we extend our profound respect and heartfelt greetings to His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama, the great masters of all Tibetan Buddhist traditions, and Tibetans across Tibet and around the world." "We pay solemn tribute to the brave Tibetan martyrs who have sacrificed their lives, freedom, and livelihoods for the survival of the Tibetan nation, the preservation of our religion, language and culture, and the restoration of Tibet’s independence. We express our unwavering solidarity with Tibetan political prisoners and with all Tibetans inside Tibet who continue to resist oppression with courage and dignity," he said. Tashi Dharjee introducted history of TYC and he said, "The Tibetan Youth Congress was founded on 7 October 1970 in Dharamshala, in the blessed presence of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. Its founding was a historic expression of the determination of patriotic and educated young Tibetans in exile to unite the Tibetan people and dedicate oneself to serve for the nation and it’s people, protect the national unity, preserve the distinct culture, Religion and Identity and the restoration of Tibet’s independence." "The founding date also carries profound historical significance. On October 7, 1950, Chinese Communist forces launched their military offensive against Chamdo in eastern Tibet, marking a decisive stage in the military occupation of Tibet. This history remains deeply etched in the memory of the Tibetan people," he added. The Vice President said, "For 56 years, TYC has remained committed to restoring Tibet’s complete independence and sovereignty. Guided by democratic principles and the resolutions of its General Body Meetings and Executive Committee, TYC and its chapters across India, Nepal, Bhutan, North America, Europe, and other parts of the world have consistently worked to advance the Tibetan national cause through peaceful demonstrations, political advocacy, public campaigns, international outreach, and community mobilisation." "Our position remains unequivocal: Tibet is a distinct nation with its own history, language, culture, religion, identity, and political heritage, and the Tibetan people have the inherent right to determine their own political future," he said. Tashi said, "The Chinese Communist government continues to pursue systematic policies of repression and forced assimilation in Tibet. Tibetan language, religion, monasteries, culture, and national identity are under sustained attack. The so-called “Law on Promoting National Unity and Progress,” imposed from 1 July 2026, further institutionalises policies aimed at suppressing the distinct identities and rights of Tibetans and other peoples under Chinese rule. Developments at Larung Gar and Yachen Gar, including the destruction of monastic residences and the expulsion of monks and nuns, further demonstrate the continuing assault on Tibet’s religious and cultural heritage." "In response to these escalating policies, TYC organised the Black Hat March from Dharamshala to New Delhi, bringing the deteriorating situation in Tibet to public attention and presenting our demands to relevant institutions. The march demonstrated that, despite decades of occupation and repression, the Tibetan spirit of resistance remains alive and unbroken. On July 2, 2026, martyr Pawo Lobga Rangzen made the ultimate sacrifice outside the United Nations Headquarters in New York for Tibet Independence. His final testament and his call for Tibet’s freedom deeply moved Tibetans and supporters around the world. In honour of his sacrifice and final wishes, TYC launched a Chain Hunger Strike in Dharamshala, which continued for more than a month before the campaign was carried forward at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. These actions once again carried the voice of Tibet to the international community," he explained. He added by saying, "Recently, on September 12, when Chinese Communist Party leader Xi Jinping visited India to attend the BRICS Summit, the Central and Regional Tibetan Youth Congress chapters jointly launched a two-day, large-scale political campaign in New Delhi under the banner “Chalo Delhi.” Similarly, on September 24, when Xi Jinping visited the United States, the Central and Regional Tibetan Youth Congress chapters in North America organized a major political campaign, “Chalo D.C.” The campaign brought together a historic and unprecedented gathering of Tibetans and supporters, marking one of the largest mobilizations in the history of Tibetan political activism in the United States." "While Tibetans in exile continue to exercise the limited freedoms available to us, Tibetans inside Tibet remain subjected to surveillance, repression, imprisonment, forced assimilation, and restrictions on fundamental freedoms. Yet they continue to preserve their language, religion, culture, traditions, and national identity. Their courage places a profound responsibility upon every Tibetan in exile to remain united, disciplined, and determined," he said. The Vice President said, "On this 56th Founding Anniversary, the Tibetan Youth Congress calls upon all Tibetans to strengthen our unity, national consciousness, and collective determination, while deepening cohesion with governments, organisations, individuals, and peoples who genuinely support the Tibetan cause." "We firmly believe that the day is not far when we will witness a free Tibet, the return of His Holiness the Great 14th Dalai Lama to his homeland, and the long-awaited reunification of the Tibetan people in a free and independent Tibet. That day may be only a few steps away, but those steps require our unwavering determination, unity, courage, and collective action. Let us therefore stand together, strengthen our national unity, and carry forward the torch of our freedom struggle with stronger commitment. Let no obstacle weaken our resolve and let no hardship extinguish the spirit of the Tibetan people. Together, we shall keep the flame of Tibet’s freedom burning until our national aspirations are fulfilled," he concluded. MP Gyaltsen Choekye stated that she had been familiar with the Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) since her school days in Tibet and that the authorities had forbidden Tibetan students from forming any student organisation with the word ‘youth’ in its name, as this was associated with the TYC. The TYC works tirelessly for the restoration of Tibet’s independence and is a thorn in the side of the Chinese government. The TYC can be proud to celebrate 56 years of struggle for Tibet’s independence. Tibet Freedom TYC martyr

title: Xi Jinping Met by Defiant Tibetan Protests in Washington
content: Dharamshala — When Xi Jinping's arrival in Washington, D.C. on Wednesday, the Tibetan Youth Congress, Students for a Free Tibet, the Tibetan Youth Association in Europe, and the International Tibet Network jointly protested against his visit. Demonstrators displayed banner reading: “You are not welcome in the USA,” “Free Tibet,” and “China out of Tibet now,” along the route of Xi Jinping to the hotel. When Xi Jinping's arrival in Washington, D.C. on September 23, 2026 (local date), Tibetans from the Tibetan Youth Congress, Students for a Free Tibet, the Tibetan Youth Association in Europe, and the International Tibet Network strongly protested against his visit in Washington, D.C from September 23 to September 25, 2026. The protestors displayed banner reading: “You are not welcome in the USA,” “Free Tibet,” and “China out of Tibet now,” along the route of Xi Jinping to the hotel. The Tibetan Youth Congress (Centre) released a statement regarding the Xi's visit and it states,"Tibet has been under Chinese occupation for decades, and recent policies, such as the newly implemented 'Ethnic Unity Law', are accelerating the assimilation of Tibetans. These policies include separating children from their families, restricting the Tibetan language, and attempting to erase Tibetan civilization. Even carrying a picture of His Holiness the Great 14th Dalai Lama can result in imprisonment. Over 170 Tibetans have self-immolated in protest, demanding freedom and the return of His Holiness the Dalai Lama to Tibet. Notably, on July 2, 52-year-old Tibetan Lobga Rangzen self-immolated in front of the United Nations in New York, becoming the first Tibetan self-immolation on U.S. soil. His protest was a powerful demonstration of his opposition to China's illegal occupation of Tibet and its oppressive policies." Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) President Tsering Chomphel states that, "the Tibetan Youth Congress unequivocally condemns this visit and urges global leaders to recognize that China's diplomatic assurances cannot be taken at face value when its actions continue to contradict its words. Tibetans will persist in speaking truth to power and demanding justice, freedom, and the restoration of Tibet's rightful independence." Tibetans from across North America will convene in Washington, D.C. on September 24, 2026, for a "Free Tibet Rally" to raise their voices against the visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping. According to the TYC, the rally for a "Free Tibet" in Washington DC will begin with a protest at the Chinese Embassy followed by a march to the US Capitol grounds, where Congressional leaders, former Speaker Nancy Pelosi, Rep. Jim McGovern and other guests will speak. This will be followed by a candlelight vigil with Uyghur, Hong Kong, Taiwan and Chinese Democracy groups at Franklin Park where the day's program will conclude. It is estimated this rally will draw around 5000 Tibetans and Tibet supporters to the capital. "The Tibetan Youth Congress believes that meaningful engagement between Washington and Beijing must not come at the expense of the voices and rights of Tibetans and other oppressed peoples. Tibet must not be erased from the Trump-Xi agenda. The Tibetan Youth Congress calls upon the United States to seize this moment to uphold the principles of freedom, human rights, and self-determination and ensure that the Tibetan people's voices are heard," the TYC said. title: A play about the 1956 Khampa revolution will premiere in Dharamshala
content: Dharamshala — The Tibet Theatre has announced that its new play, entitled PHAYUL (homeland) – a contemporary Tibetan theatre production dedicated to the 1956 Khampa uprising – will premiere in Dharamsala. The cast consists of Tibetan women, whose courage during the early years of the Chinese invasion is rarely highlighted. Rather than a political narrative centred on a few leaders, the play portrays ordinary lives: monks in monasteries, nomadic families and the families of resistance fighters. The Tibet Theatre held a press conference at the Tibetan Institute of Performing Arts (TIPA) in Dharamsala on October 7, 2026, to announce its new play, entitled PHAYUL (homeland). Thakpa Tsering, director of the Tibet Theatre, the German director Harry Fuhrmann, and the actors Pema Tsamchoe and Pema were present at the press conference. Thakpa Tsering announced that his new play, entitled PHAYUL (homeland) – a contemporary Tibetan theatre production dedicated to the 1956 Khampean uprising – will premiere at the Tibetan Institute of Performing Arts (TIPA) in Dharamsala (Himachal Pradesh, India) on 9 and 10 October 2026 (performances to the public). ‘The Phayul’ (The Homeland), a major new play in the Tibetan language written by the renowned Indian playwright Abhishek Majumdar and co-directed by Lhakpa Tsering and the German director Harry Fuhrmann. This new Tibetan-language production, which explores the themes of women, resistance and survival in eastern Tibet in the 1950s, will first be performed for Tibetans, particularly schoolchildren in Dharamsala, before going on tour in India and Europe. ‘The Phayul’ is a two-hour play that serves as a prequel to the Tibet Theatre’s famous production ‘Pah-Lak’. Following its premiere in Dharamsala, the play will tour Tibetan schools and communities across India, before travelling to theatre festivals in India and Europe in 2027. The director Harry, explained why the title “Phayul” was chosen: because “Phayul” means “homeland,” and the homeland is of utmost importance to people who have been forced to flee their native land, such as the Tibetans; they remain attached to it throughout their lives, and it is important to let the rest of the world know what the Tibetans are going through. Tibetans living in Tibet continue to suffer severe repression under the Chinese regime, and because China is attempting to present a distorted version of Tibetan history. In order to raise public awareness of the true history of Tibet, the play “Phayul” recounts the events that took place over a two-week period in eastern Tibet, specifically in Kham. The Tibet Theatre, in collaboration with playwright Abhishek Majumdar and acting coach Harald Fuhrmann, has spent more than three years developing this production for an international audience, with rehearsals having begun on August 31, 2026. Lhakpa said, "Phayul is set during the Chinese occupation of eastern Tibet in the early 1950s. It follows how Tibetans responded through both peaceful resistance and armed struggle and how Tibet ultimately came under Chinese control. At its heart are Tibetan women, whose courage during the early years of the invasion is rarely told. Rather than a political narrative about a few leaders, the play centres on ordinary lives: monks in monasteries, nomadic families, and the families of resistance fighters. It explores their choices, courage, and suffering and connects their story to the agency of people living today." Abhishek Majumdar and Tashi Wangchuk (United States) conducted extensive research in historical texts, while Lhakpa Tsering handled the translation into Tibetan from the English text. The team consists of 10 Tibetan actors, 3 staff members, and 5 volunteers. "By performing the play in Tibetan, our actors engage deeply with their mother tongue within contemporary theatre. This artistic choice also highlights the urgent threats facing the Tibetan language today, including forced assimilation and cultural erosion." - Lhakpa Tsering, Director, Tibet Theatre. "The entire play is performed in Tibetan, with multilingual subtitles. By placing Tibetan at the center of the performance, the production affirms it as a living language of contemporary theatre," he added. In 2022 and 2023, Tibet Theatre staged "Pah-Lak", written by Indian playwright Abhishek Majumdar. The production drew national and international attention to Tibet, with wide coverage in newspapers and magazines of the Tibetan struggle, according to Lhakpa Tsering. "Phayul" has been invited to major theatre festivals including Prithvi Theatre Festival, India (2026), Ruhrfestspiele Recklinghausen, Germany (2027), Theatre Winterthur Festival, Switzerland, the European Tour is supported by Tibet Initiative Deutschland (THD). Lhakpa said, "Phayul is made possible through the generous support of Tibetan Initiative Deutschland German Aid to Tibetans, The Tibet Funds, Deutsche Tibethilfe e.V,, g8tf, the International Campaign for Tibet (ICT) and NYUAD art and humanities whose commitment to Tibetan arts and culture has helped bring this production to the stage. We would like to express our sincere gratitude to them." Tibet Theatre is a Dharamshala-based theatre initiative, which was established in 2011, creating over 100 plays in the Tibetan language. Its productions, including "Pah-Lak" (2022-23) and "Phayul" (2026), bring Tibetan history and lived experience to audiences in India and around the world. Phayul brings an all-Tibetan ensemble to the stage to examine the pivotal events of the 1950s resistance, the human impact of occupation, and the urgency of preserving Tibetan language and heritage. Tibet Free Tibet Resistance

title: The Bipartisan US delegation meets with His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama
content: Dharamshala — The bipartisan US delegation met His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama, the spiritual leader of Tibet, at his residence in Dharamsala, on Wednesday. Brian Mast, Chairman of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee said," Meeting with His Holiness the Dalai Lama is something, I will never forget, we dicussed numbers of things, certainly China was among top issue, freedom of Tibetan people." The bipartisan US delegation met His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama, the spiritual leader of Tibet, at his residence in Dharamsala, on September 30, 2026. The delegation, led by Brian Mast, Chairman of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee, and accompanied by James Gallagher (Republican–California), Jimmy Patronis (Republican–Florida), Haley Stevens (Democrat–Michigan), and Shri Thanedar (Democrat–Michigan). They were accompanied by Sikyong Penpa Tsering and Representative Jigme Tsering of the New Delhi-based Bureau of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. Brian Mast said: “This meeting with His Holiness the Dalai Lama is a moment I will never forget. We discussed many topics, including, of course, China and the freedom of the Tibetan people.” Regarding China's Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress, he stated: “Through this law, China is extending its influence beyond its borders, spreading its reach to every country in the world and monitoring populations; it is sending spies and police officers to various countries, and cracking down on people it does not want to see. We are different from China: we believe in freedom, in democracy for all, and in the fact that individuals are born with certain rights which the government must not suppress, but protect.” Mast said: “The US House of Representatives stands firmly alongside the Tibetan and Uyghur peoples in the face of the repressive measures taken against them by the Chinese government. We commend the commitment shown by so many people to the cause of freedom in Tibet.” When asked about China’s interference in the reincarnation of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama, he replied: ‘This is nothing new. China has previously abducted lama (11th Panchen Lama) recognised by His Holiness the Dalai Lama, and these people have not been heard from since. What is happening now is that China is likely attempting to forcibly appoint a reincarnation of its choosing, a move that is contrary to the wishes of both the Tibetan people and His Holiness the Dalai Lama. This comes as no surprise, as I believe China will stop at nothing to achieve its goal of oppressing the Tibetan people.” “China is not acting in a friendly manner towards the United States of America. It is stealing our intellectual property. It is stealing computer equipment from the United States of America. The scale of its espionage activities against us is constant,” he concluded. Haley Stevens (a Democratic MP) from the State of Michigan said: “We are here to visit His Holiness the Dalai Lama and to stand up for democracy and freedom. We support the oppressed peoples who are marginalised by a cruel government. We must denounce the actions of this government. The Chinese Communist Party must allow the Tibetan people to return to their homeland (Tibet), a people who are among the most peaceful and benevolent and who, like the United States of America, defend democracy and freedom. We see this happening all over the world. That is why I join you here with enthusiasm, optimism and dedication, to fight against artificial intelligence, propaganda and the exploitation of data.” A bipartisan delegation from the United States Congress, led by Representative Brian Mast, Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, received a warm welcome from the Central Tibetan Administration upon its arrival at Kangra Airport on September 29, 2026. The delegation was received by Tsegyal Choekya Dranyi, officiating Sikyong and Kalon of the Department of Religion and Culture; Tashi Gyatso Shadrong, Cabinet Secretary; Jigme Tsering, Representative of the New Delhi-based Bureau of His Holiness the Dalai Lama; and Tempa Gyaltsen Zamlha, Joint Secretary, and Ngawang Choedhar, Protocol Officer, of the Department of Information and International Relations-CTA. During their visit, the delegation toured the Tibet Museum of the Central Tibetan Administration, accompanied by Sikyong Penpa Tsering. In the evening, the 17th Kashag hosted a welcome dinner in their honour in Dharamshala, attended by members of the Central Tibetan Administration leadership. Tibet Dalai Lama USA

title: Five NGOs in Dharamshala mark Tibetan National Uprising
content: Dharamshala — Leading up to the 59th anniversary of Tibetan Uprising Day celebrated on March 10, five Dharamshala-based Tibetan NGOs have called on the international community and the UN to take action in Tibet. In a press conference, the five organizations, Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC), Tibetan Women’s Association (TWA), National Democratic Party of Tibet (NDPT), Gu-Chu-Sum Movement Association of Tibet and Students for a Free Tibet-India (SFT), announced they will be jointly organizing a five-day campaign from March 10 to March 14, 2018. “We call upon the governments around the world, the United Nations and the international human rights organizations to hold China accountable for the rapidly declining situation in Tibet and express strong public condemnation towards China’s poor Implementation of Universal Declaration of human rights,” the five organizations said in its statement. The press release read, "Today marks the 59th anniversary of the Tibetan National Uprising. It has been 59 years since hundreds of thousands of Tibetans rose up in a spontaneous grassroots protest demanding the end to China’s illegal occupation of Tibet. China’s use of extreme force to quell these protests compelled the 14th Dalai Lama to escape to India, where he has lived in exile ever since. "Today also marks the ten years of people’s uprising inside Tibet in 2008, During that time Tibet witnessed a transformation in the strength and breadth of Tibetan non-violent resistance; Tibetans from all walks of life and from all over Tibet took to the streets in large numbers to call for an end to China’s rule. "Despite the harsh crackdown and the threat of arrest, disappearance, torture and death, China has failed to crush Tibetan resistance; it remains exceptionally strong to this very day. Tibetans in Tibet are finding ways to non-violently stand up to and reject China’s rule through cultural resistance actions, assertions of national identity, and non-cooperation. "We mark this day each year to show solidarity with Tibetans inside Tibet and to honor and support the brave resistance to China’s rule that continues to this day." In 2008, protests spread across all of Tibet, the largest protests against Chinese rule in Tibet since the original occupation in 1959. The 2008 uprising was led by over 400 monks of Drepung Loseling Monastery, who marched the streets of Lhasa and subsequent protests had spread throughout the country by March 14. “The uprising was met with a brutal crackdown; peaceful protestors were fired upon, killing at least 225, more than 6800 arrests and sentencing of about 510 Tibetans. On the ground level, death, arrests and enforced disappearances of Tibetan peaceful protestors are far greater in number than internationally reported,” the statement read. The five-day plan will begin with a procession from the main temple in Mcleod Ganj to lower Dharamshala on March 10 to commemorate the Tibetan Uprising Day.

title: 37 US Congressmen Urge Trump to Demand China Repeal ‘Ethnic Unity’ Law
content: Washington D.C — Ahead of the U.S.–China summit, a group of 37 U.S. Congressmembers wrote a formal letter to President Donald Trump, to condemn Beijing's newly enacted "Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress". The bipartisan coalition warned that the legislation grants Chinese authorities "sweeping authority to prosecute Tibetans, Uyghurs, and other ethnic and religious minority groups" under the guise of protecting national unity and Communist Party ideology. The letter sent to President Donald Trump on September 23, 2026, which was led by Representatives Jamie Raskin, Jim McGovern, Gregory Meeks, and signed by Ro Khanna, Member of Congress, Mark Pocan, Member of Congress Member, and Andre Carson, member of Congress, Maxine Waters, Member of Congress, Eleanor Holmes Norton, Member of Congress, Llo Doggett, Member of Congress, Pramila Jayapal, Member of Congress, James R. Walkinshaw, Member of Congress, Richard E. Neal, Member of Congress, Nancy Pelosi, Member of Congress, Grace Meng, Member of Congress, Sydney Kamlager Dove, Member of Congress, Jasmine Crocket, Member of Congres, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Member of Congress, Jake Auchincloss, Member of Congress, Veronica Escobar, Member of Congress, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Member of Congress, Ami Bera, M.D. Member of Congress, Stephen F. Lynch, Member of Congress, Jerrold Nadler, Member of Congress, Jan Schakowsky, Member of Congress, Dina Titus, Member of Congress, Ilhan Omar, Member of Congress, Syavia R. Garcia, Member of Congress, Madeleine Dean, Member of Congress, Steve Cohen, Member of Congress, Kathy Castor, Member of Congress, Shri Thanedar, Member of Congress, Brad Sherman, Member of Congress, Thomas R. Suozzi, Member of Congress, Bradley Scott Schneider, Member of Congress, Al Green, Member of Congress, Mark DeSaulnier, Member of Congress, and George Latimer, Member of Congress The letter stated, "As you engage with President Xi Jinping this month, we urge you to express profound opposition to the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law recently implemented by the Chinese government.' "This law grants Chinese authorities sweeping authority to prosecute Tibetans, Uyghurs and other ethnic and religious minority groups that it broadly accuses of undermining national unity and Communist Party ideology. "Moreover, the extraterritorial scope of the law means that it will dramatically accelerate China's transnational repression of critics living in the U.S.' The State Department has itself recognized these ramifications in a statement calling the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law "problematic.' During your meeting with Xi Jinping, it is imperative that you continue to voice your administration's disapproval of this affront to the fundamental freedoms of minority communities, human rights advocates and U.S. citizens. "Enacted under the guise of promoting "social harmony" on March 12, 2026, the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law is in fact an insidious declaration of China's intent to further repress religious freedom and the freedom of group association. One of the most troubling provisions of the law would require religious activities to undergo "Sinicization," a process championed by Xi Jinping and used in reference to the complete subordination and assimilation of religious and ethnic groups to the political ideology of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). Well before the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law came into effect on July 1, 2026, China had already embarked upon a concerted campaign to destroy the shrines of Uyghur Muslims, remove Tibetan Buddhist statues from monasteries, censor the holy texts read in Christian churches and otherwise purge houses of worship in the name of "Sinicization." With the additional legal cover provided by their new law, Chinese authorities are escalating their systemic persecution of minority faith communities. "Elsewhere in the text of the law, the Chinese government asserts the alarming power to extend its repressive tactics into U.S. borders and against U.S. citizens. Article 63 plainly states that organisations and individuals outside China will be held legally accountable for activities that China deems are undertaken in opposition to national unity and progress.' In codifying this language, China thus purports to exercise jurisdiction over people who are neither Chinese citizens nor residents of the country and who are merely exercising their freedom of expression.' For dissidents who fled China in pursuit of the rights and freedoms we enjoy in America, the clause amounts to a promise that they will continue to be pursued by an oppressive state adamant about suppressing their speech and beliefs. "To grasp the consequences of such a promise, one need only examine the tactics China has increasingly deployed against its U.S.-based critics, including U.S. citizens. In the last couple of years alone, the federal government determined conclusively that Chinese officials intimidated student activists who spoke out against its rule, imposed monetary bounties on Hong Kong activists, launched a cyber-hacking campaign targeting dissidents and employed other sophisticated strategies to silence pro-democracy voices in the U.S." Just this summer, Chinese authorities detained Min Zin, a U.S. citizen and doctoral candidate, upon his arrival in the country for an academic conference. Today, who actively promoted democratization in the South Asia, remains in the Chinese custoday. Absent robust efforts to contest the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law, he will be just one of many more targeted U.S. citizens. "Min Zin's story, along with the broader trends indicating an intensification of China's crackdown on religious minorities and dissent abroad, should serve as a warning to us all. If left in place, the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law will expedite ongoing transnational repression, religiously motivated and identity-based persecution and other anti-democratic maneuvers of the Chinese government. In fact, emerging evidence suggests that China has actively begun to leverage the measure against the communities it has historically sought to marginalize. Uyghur-language signs are reportedly being removed from city streets, and during a recent tour of Tibet, a top CCP leader pressed authorities to "adapt" Tibetan Buddhism in accordance with the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law.' "We greatly appreciated the State Department's earlier statement expressing concerns about the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law. ' However, a president's personal advocacy has unparalleled power to elicit meaningful change. During your upcoming meeting with Xi Jinping, we therefore urge you to ask for the repeal of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law. "At stake are our national security, sovereignty and basic human rights all over the world," the letter concluded. Tibet China Congress US

title: Tibetan Activist Call on Canada to Raise Lobga Rangzen's Self-Immolation at UN
content: Ottawa — Tibetan activist Youngdoung Tenzin called on Canada’s Foreign Minister to urge the UN to break its silence regarding martyr Lobga Rangzen, who self-immolated outside the UN Headquarters in New York. Tenzin further demands that Canada's top diplomat actively raise the worsening Tibetan human rights crisis during direct negotiations with Chinese counterparts. Tibetan activist Youngdoung Tenzin met with the Hon. Esabelle, Policy Advisor to the Minister of Foreign Affairs Anita Anand, on September 28, 2026, to brief her on the self-immolation of Tibetan independence activist Pawo Loga Rangzen. He formally submitted the petition alongside Pawo Rangzen’s final live message translated into English. "Despite his self-immolation outside the UN Headquarters in New York, the United Nations has remained silent. As a UN member state, I appealed to our Foreign Minister to raise this urgent matter both at the UN and directly with their Chinese counterpart," he said. Tenzin has issued a formal appeal to the Honourable Anita Anand, Minister of Foreign Affairs and wrote,"Thank you for providing me with the opportunity to meet with your advisors to brief Global Affairs Canada on the recent self-immolation of Tibetan independence activist Loga Rangzen on July 2, 2026, outside the United Nations Headquarters in New York. "Canada is one of the few nations providing refugee protection to the largest Tibetan diaspora in the West. Tibetan Canadians have successfully integrated into Canadian society, contributing to our country while maintaining a strong community. "Politically, Canada has consistently demonstrated strong support for Tibet and its people through United Nations resolutions, including voting in favor of UNGA Resolution 1353 (1959), UNGA Resolution 1723(1961), and UNGA Resolution 2079(1965), which signify Canadian support at the highest international level. Furthermore, the Parliament of Canada unanimously passed a motion to resume the Sino-Tibetan dialogue on December 14, 2022, and passed a historic motion supporting the Tibetan people's right to self-determination on June 10, 2024. Both the Canadian government and Parliament have steadfastly backed the Tibetan cause, and I express my deep gratitude to the government and people of Canada for their enduring support. "Historically, Tibet was an independent nation. On November 21, 1950, Canada's Secretary of State for External Affairs, Lester B. Pearson, formally stated in an official diplomatic memorandum regarding Tibet's legal status: 'In fact it appears that during the past 40 years Tibet has controlled its own internal and external affairs. Viewing the situation thus, I am of the opinion that Tibet is, from the point of view of international law, qualified for recognition as an independent state'. "Following China's forceful and illegal occupation of Tibet, the Chinese government has systematically dismantled the Tibetan environment, culture, language, religion, and national identity. On July 1, 2026, the Chinese government implemented its "Law on the Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress." Far from promoting unity and progress, this policy legitimizes acts of cultural genocide against Tibet-a nation, rather than a mere ethnic minority —and poses a direct threat to the very survival of the Tibetan identity and Tibetan People. International bodies such as the UN must act to protect the Tibetan people. "Systemic repression by China has driven over 170 Tibetans to self-immolate in protest, calling for the return of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama, independence, and freedom for Tibet. Because these sacrifices have largely gone unaddressed by the UN and the international community, Tibetan Independent activist Loga Rangzen self-immolated on July 2, 2026, outside UN Headquarters in New York to protest Chinese repression and the "Ethnic Unity and Progress" law, while calling for Tibetan independence. Prior to his act, he broadcast a six-minute live stream on Facebook displaying the Tibetan national flag and calling for 'China Out of Tibet'. Despite thousands of Tibetan Americans and Canadians protesting outside the UN Headquarters to urge intervention, the UN remained silent, issuing no official statement and sending no representative to show solidarity-an omission that violates the foundational principles of the United Nations. "As Canada is an influential member state of the UN, I respectfully demand that the Canadian government: • Raise Loga Rangzen's sacrifice at the United Nations General Assembly and join a multilateral Joint Statement on Human Rights regarding Tibet. • Formally include Loga Rangzen's sacrifice and the situation in Tibet in Global Affairs Canada's annual human rights report. • Address Loga Rangzen's message and self-immolation directly with Chinese counterparts during diplomatic engagements, ensuring the Tibetan cause is not compromised for economic interests. • Formally recognize China's "Ethnic Unity and Progress" Law as an illegal policy and an act of genocide. "As a Tibetan Canadian, I was among the first human rights advocates sanctioned by the Chinese government on December 22, 2024, for peacefully advocating for Tibetan freedom on Canadian soil. "This act of transnational repression has subjected me to severe hardship, including death threats and intimidation. However, I remain resolute in my advocacy because I firmly believe in Canada's dedication to freedom, human rights, and democracy. I urge the Canadian government to stand up against China's transnational repression while conducting bilateral relations," he concluded the letter. Tibet Human Rights Canada

title: China remains the world’s biggest jailer of journalists: World media rights watchdog
content: Paris, France — "China remains the world’s biggest jailer of journalists with 60 currently held, of whom three quarters are non-professional journalists," The Paris-based world press freedom watchdog "Reporters Without Borders" said adding: The communist regime "has been near the bottom of RSF's World Press Freedom Index for years and is currently ranked 176th out of 180 countries." A total of 80 journalists were killed this year, 348 are currently in prison, and 60 are being held hostage, according to the annual worldwide round-up of deadly violence and abusive treatment of journalists released today by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), which shows an unprecedented level of hostility towards media personne. The RSF stressed that its "round-up figures have risen in all categories. Murders, imprisonment, hostage-taking and enforced disappearances have all increased. Journalists have never before been subjected to as much violence and abusive treatment as in 2018." "This year has been marked by the number of journalists in all categories who were killed in connection with their work, a figure which increased by eight percent to 80, and by the 15 percent rise in the number of professional journalists killed, from 55 in 2017 to 63 this year," the press freedom watchdog said in a statement dated December 14, 2018, adding: "This number had been declining over the previous three years." "The widely reported murders of Saudi columnist Jamal Khashoggi and the young Slovak data journalist Ján Kuciak highlighted the lengths to which press freedom’s enemies are prepared to go. More than half of the journalists killed in 2018 were deliberately targeted," the statement reads. “Violence against journalists has reached unprecedented levels this year, and the situation is now critical,” RSF Secretary-General Christophe Deloire said. “The hatred of journalists that is voiced, and sometimes very openly proclaimed, by unscrupulous politicians, religious leaders and businessmen has tragic consequences on the ground, and has been reflected in this disturbing increase in violations against journalists. “Amplified by social networks, which bear heavy responsibility in this regard, these expressions of hatred legitimize violence, thereby undermining journalism, and democracy itself, a bit more every day.” With the release of its latest World Press Freedom Index in April, RSF had already expressed alarm over an increased level of hostility towards the media encouraged by politicians, as well as efforts by authoritarian regimes to export their alternative vision of journalism. Speaking about those journalists who were detained or held hostage, the press freedom watchdog said "Afghanistan was the world’s deadliest country for journalists in 2018, with 15 killed. It was followed by Syria, with 11 killed, and Mexico, the deadliest country outside a conflict zone, with nine journalists murdered in 2018. The fatal shooting of five employees of the Capital Gazette newspaper in June brought the United States into the ranks of the deadliest countries." "The number of journalists detained worldwide at the end of the year – 348 – is up from 326 at this time last year. As in 2017, more than half of the world’s imprisoned journalists are being held in just five countries: China, Iran, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Turkey," the RSF said, adding: "China remains the world’s biggest jailer of journalists with 60 currently held, of whom three quarters are non-professional journalists." The number of journalists currently held hostage – 60 – is 11 percent higher than this time last year, when it was 54. All but one are being held in three Middle Eastern countries: Syria, Iraq, and Yemen. They include six foreign journalists. Despite the Islamic State’s defeat in Iraq and retreat in Syria, little information has emerged about the fate of these hostages, except for Japanese journalist Jumpei Yasuda, who was freed after three years of captivity in Syria. A Ukrainian journalist is still being held in the self-proclaimed “Donetsk People’s Republic” by the authorities who accuse him of spying. RSF also registered three new cases of journalists disappearing in 2018, two in Latin America and one in Russia. Compiled by RSF every year since 1995, the annual round-up of abusive treatment and deadly violence against journalists is based on precise data. We gather detailed information that allows us to confirm with certainty or a great deal of confidence that the death, detention, abduction or disappearance of each journalist listed was a direct result of their journalistic work. The media watchdog said that "these figures include professional journalists, non-professional journalists, and media workers." In a joint letter released in last month, Reporters Without Borders and a coalition of human rights NGOs are calling for the immediate release of Huang Qi, a Chinese journalist and human rights activist who is very ill and could die in detention. The NGO coalition that is jointly releasing this letter consists of Amnesty International, the Association of Taiwan Journalists, the China Human Rights Lawyers Concern Group, Chinese Human Rights Defenders, International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH), Freedom House, Frontline Defenders, Human Rights Watch, the International Service for Human Rights, the World Organisation Against Torture, Reporters Without Borders (RSF), Safeguard Defenders, Taiwan Association of Human Rights and The Rights Practice. RSF is an international non-governmental, non-profit organization with a recognized public interest function that has consultative status with the United Nations, UNESCO, the Council of Europe, the International Organization of the Francophonie and the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights. Headquartered in Paris, it has bureaux, sections or representatives in 17 cities (Berlin, Brussels, Geneva, Helsinki, Istanbul, Karachi, Kiev, London, Madrid, Mexico City, Rio de Janeiro, San Francisco, Stockholm, Taipei, Tunis, Vienna and Washington), correspondents in 130 countries and 15 local partner organizations.

title: China Shuts Down Livestream After Tibetan Woman Singing a Tibetan Song
content: Dharamshala — The Chinese government has intensified its Sinicisation policy in Tibet through the so-called “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress." This campaign increasingly targets the Tibetan language by removing it from public signage and forcing Tibetans to speak Mandarin. These restrictions have heavily impacted live streaming, a vital source of income for many Tibetans. Recently, authorities abruptly shut down the live stream of a Tibetan woman simply for singing a Tibetan song. Chinese social media platforms frequently disrupt or shut down live streams when creators speak in Tibetan. Tibetan content creators and e-commerce entrepreneurs on major Chinese applications like Douyin (the Chinese version of TikTok) and Kuaishou have widely documented instances where their live broadcasts were abruptly cut off, muted, or flagged with automated warnings simply for using their mother tongue (Tibetan). On September 16, 2026, a young Tibetan woman shared her experience of having her livestream abruptly interrupted and shut down. The termination occurred immediately after she sang a Tibetan song, which she had performed in an effort to liven up the broadcast. (Editor's Note: To ensure her safety and protect her from potential retaliation, her name and identifying details have been withheld.) Expressing her frustration and disbelief, she said: "I am completely speechless. Just now, when I was live streaming... I sang a Tibetan song to liven up the stream. Shortly after I started singing, they directly kicked me out and shut down the live stream." She added: "I am so angry... Why do they do this? Why are the Tibetan, Mongolian, and Uyghur languages written into the constitution? Did we violate some heavenly law? Why did they shut down the live stream?" She went on to explain the systemic financial and cultural pressures facing Tibetan creators, stating: "What I hear is that if you use the Tibetan language in a live stream, you have to pay the authorities." She added, "They want to silence us and force everyone to speak Chinese. I am speechless—the same thing happened a few days ago. You do not allow us to speak Tibetan, and now you do not allow us to sing a Tibetan song. Are you really that afraid?" Chinese government has intensified its Sinicisation policy in Tibet by closing Tibetan schools and monasteries and forcing Tibetan children and young monks into state-run Chinese colonial boarding schools. In recent months, the Chinese authorities have also cracked down on Tibetans who promote the Tibetan language through detentions, arrests, harassment, humiliation and imprisonment. Live streaming has become a vital source of income for many young Tibetans facing severe unemployment. Job opportunities are limited and local Tibetans face systemic discrimination, often being excluded from positions in corporate offices and government departments. With limited options, many have turned to live streaming to earn a living by selling goods or hosting public debates. However, according to a reliable source, the Chinese government plans to completely ban these live streams by 2028. This upcoming restriction is driven by the rapid growth of the online economy and Beijing's growing fear that sensitive state secrets could be leaked to the outside world. The Chinese communist government’s aggressive suppression of live streaming represents a critical escalation in its Sinicization campaign, systematically dismantling the digital freedom of expression and economic independence of young Tibetans. Under the pretext of enforcing “national security” and so-called the "Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress," state authorities have weaponised automated algorithms to instantly flag, fine, or shut down broadcasts featuring the Tibetan language—even for harmless cultural expressions like singing traditional songs. Tibet Freedom China

title: "Xi Jinping, Stop Genocide Laws in Tibet": Tibetans Protest Leader's Visit to India
content: New Delhi — Hundreds of Tibetans took to the streets in Majnu ka Tila, Delhi, on September 11, 2026, launching a fierce protest against Chinese President Xi Jinping ahead of his arrival for the BRICS summit. The demonstrators issued an urgent call for Beijing to immediately repeal its controversial "Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress," branding it a deceitful policy designed to mask an aggressive assimilation agenda. Protesters warned that while the legislation is framed around national progress, its true, malicious objective is the systematic erasure of the Tibetan language, religion, culture, and unique ethnic identity. The protest was organised by the Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC), the largest Tibetan NGO in exile, the march began at 10:00 AM on September 11, 2026, winding through the streets of Majnu ka Tila, Delhi. Demonstrators flooded the streets holding high-visibility signs that read "Xi Jinping, You Are Not Welcome" and "Repeal the Genocide Law—'Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress.'" As they marched, the air filled with defiant, synchronised chants exposing Beijing's human rights record and cultural suppression. The crowd roared powerful slogans including "Free Tibet," "China Out of Tibet Now," "China Lies, People Die," "Tibet Belongs to Tibetans," and "Tibet Was Never a Part of China." Further condemning the Chinese Communist Party's assimilation policies, protesters shouted "Stop the Genocide in Tibet," "Stop Cultural Genocide," "Stop the Torture, Stop the Killing in Tibet," and "Save Tibetan Language, Save Tibetan Culture." Highlighting the strategic geopolitical stakes for their host nation, the marchers also raised a vital warning: "Tibet's Independence is India's Security!" The Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) held the opening event at the Tibetan Children's Village (TCV) Day School in Majnu ka Tila, Delhi, drawing a prominent delegation of Tibetan leaders who later joined the street protests. The event featured addresses from key political figures, including Gyari Dolma, former Minister (Kalon) of the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA), alongside TYC Vice President Tashi Dharjee, General Secretary Lobsang Tenzin and former Deputy Speaker Acharya Yeshi Phuntsok. Members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile—including Wangdu Dorjee, Kunchok Rinchen, Gyaltsen Choekyi, marched alongside hundreds of protesters to show undivided solidarity against the Chinese regime. Tibetan Youth Congress issued a statement and it said,"The Tibetan Youth Congress congratulates India on hosting the BRICS Summit 2026 and commends its leadership in advancing dialogue, cooperation, partnership, and shared prosperity among BRICS member states. We also express our deep appreciation for India's longstanding hospitality towards the Tibetan people and the Tibetan Government-in-Exile for more than six decades. We extend our best wishes for a successful and constructive summit that strengthens mutual understanding, regional stability. and mcaningful coopcration among participating nations." "The Tibetan Youth Congress vehemently condemns the participation of Chinese President Xi Jinping in the 2026 BRICS Summit. Xi Jinping is the primary architect of the ongoing cultural genocide in Tibet and bears direct responsibility for the systematic loss of Tibetan lives both through state-sanctioned violence and the avoidable tragedies of recent environmental disasters caused by uncontrolled engineering on the Tibetan Plateau," the Tibetan NGO said. "We also urge India and other member states to raise the issue of Tibet with the Chinese leadership at this important meeting to advance international cooperation and strengthen global governance. For the past seven decades. Chinese policies in Tibet have resulted in the systematic erosion of Tibetan culture, language, religion, and identity, such practices that many scholars, parliamentarians, and human rights advocates have described as cultural crasure and forced assimilation. Recent legislation of "promotion of ethnic unity and progress law" has further intensified the systematic assimilation of Tibetans and the marginalization of their distinct cultural identity. The law was imposed on July 1, 2026 and the very next day. Tibctan martyr Lobga Rangzen self-immolated before the UN Headquarters for the cause of Tibet, becoming a tragic reminder of China's repression and nearly 170 Tibetans have self-immolated in protest," the Tibetan activists from TYC said. "During International cooperation among member states, they cannot remain blind to the realities of Chinese colonial rule in Tibet. Genuine global cooperation and responsible governance must also address the human rights, cultural, and political consequences of policies that threaten the survival of Tibet's distinct identity and heritage including other occupied nations of China," the Tibetan activists explained. "We condemn China's interference in Tibetan Buddhism and violating the religious freedom and traditions of Tibetan Buddhists. The recognition of His Holiness the 15th Dalai Lama is a deeply spiritual matter that must be conducted according to Tibetan Buddhist traditions, free from political coercion or state interference. His Holiness the great 14" Dalai Lama has clearly affirmed that the Gaden Phodrang Trust holds sole authority over the recognition of his future reincarnation. China has no legitimate religious authority to dictate or interfere in this process," they added. "China must immediatcly and unconditionally release all Tibetan political prisoners, human rights defenders, climate and environmental activists, religious figures, artist and other Tibetans detained for peacefully exercising their fundamental rights including the 11th Panchen Lama, Gedhun Chockyi Nyima," they demanded. "The Tibetan Youth Congress condemns China's drastic colonial legislation of "Ethnic Unity and Progress law": which seeks to institutionalise the erasure of Tibet's distinct identity, culture, language, religion and heritage under the guise of ethnic unity and development. Since China's military occupation of Tibet. India and China have repeatedly attempted to address their border disputes. yet a lasting solution remains clusive, as there can be no lasting solution without addressing the fundamental issue of Tibet. In the name of development and progress. China has pursued extensive exploitation of Tibet's fragile environment through large-scale mining, dam construction, river diversion and other major infrastructure projects, resulting in degradation of Tibet's environment. The recent flash flood in the Nepal-Tibet border serves as a stark reminder to the global community that no neighboring state can afford to remain silent on the environmental destruction and large-scale dam construction taking place in Tibet," the Tibetan activists explained. TYC said, "Tibet is Asia's water lifeline and one of the world's most fragile and scismically active regions. Unchecked dams, infrastructure projects, and control of Tibet's rivers pose growing environmental and security risks to Tibet and millions of people across India, Bangladesh, and Southeast Asia countries. With climate and scismic risks intensifying, the international community can no longer remain on the sideline." "We call on governments, UN bodies and regional institutions to demand transparency, independent environmental assessments, meaningful consultation with affected communities and binding cooperation on transboundary rivers. China's control over rivers originating from occupied Tibet could have catastrophic consequences for India and Bangladesh including countries across southeast Asia such as Vietnam, Laos,Thailand and Cambodia. Tibet's waters must not be weaponised or used as instruments of gcopolitical control. Protecting these shared rivers is a collective responsibility, essential to the security and future of Asia," they urged. "As India hosts the BRICS Summit, we respectfully remind the international community that Tibet is not a forgotten issue. Tibet is a living question with consequences for human rights, religious freedom, environmental protection, water security, India's national security, and the future stability of Asia," the Tibetan NGO said. "The Tibetan Youth Congress believes that peace cannot be built upon silence, stability cannot be achieved through repression and desclopment cannot justify the destruction of a people's identity or environment. Tibet must not be forgotten. The Tibetans must not be silenced. And the question of Tibet must not be ignored," the Tibetan activists concluded. Tibet Free Tibet TYC

title: China detains three Tibetans suspected of having contact with Tibetans in exile
content: Dharamshala — Chinese police detained three Tibetans, including a monk from Labrang Tashi Kyil Monastery, in Sangchu County, northeastern Tibet, earlier this year. Due to the severe restrictions China imposes on the free flow of information from Tibet, no detailed information is available about them, but according to some sources, they were detained on suspicion of maintaining contact with Tibetans in exile. According to reliable sources to TPI, on March 30, 2026, Jamyang Tashi, a monk from Labrang Tashi Kyil Monastery, along with two other Tibetans, was detained by the Chinese police in Sangchu County, northeastern Tibet, in early February, 2026. In the absence of detailed information, we have been working to confirm the facts and learn more about them; unfortunately, due to China’s severe restrictions on the free flow of information from Tibet, no detailed information obtained. According to the source, the Tibetan monk Jamyang Tashi and two other Tibetans might be detained on suspicion of maintaining contact with Tibetans in exile. Another souce stated that since 2026, Chinese authorities, police and armed forces are tightening restrictions on Tibetans’ freedom and monitoring their social media accounts—particularly those have their family members, relatives, or friends abroad. Chinese authorities and police often detain, arrest, torture, and imprison Tibetans who maintain contact with family members, relatives, or friends abroad and who have made donations to Tibetan monasteries in exile or to their spiritual leader, His Holiness the Dalai Lama. "Chinese police may have accused Jamyang Tashi and two other Tibetans of having been in contact with Tibetans in exile and may have detained them,” the source added. The source said, “Jamyang Tashi was detained in 2025, held for six months, and then released. However, he was detained again in early February 2026. The reasons for this latest detention and his current whereabouts remain unknown. Chinese police have threatened his family not to disclose any information regarding his detention.” According to Article 64 of Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, "Within 24 hours after a person has been detained, his family or the unit to which he belongs shall be notified of the reasons for detention and the place of custody." However, Jamyang Tashi and other two Tibetans detained more than four months and the families of them are not informed by the Chinese police of the reasons for their detention and their whereabouts. Therefore, the Chinese police are breaking their own law. China-Tibet: The one-thing you need to know: Over the past 70 decades, there has been ongoing political repression, social discrimination, economic marginalization, environmental destruction, and cultural assimilation, particularly due to Chinese migration to Tibet which is fueling intense resentment among the people of occupied Tibet. The communist-totalitarian state of China began its invasion of Tibet in 1949, reaching complete occupation of the country in 1959. Since that time, more than 1.2 million people, 20% of the nation's population of six million, have died as a direct result of China's invasion and occupation. In addition, over 99% of Tibet's six thousand religious monasteries, temples, and shrines, have been looted or decimated resulting in the destruction of hundreds of thousands of sacred Buddhist scriptures. Until 1949, Tibet was an independent Buddhist nation in the Himalayas which had little contact with the rest of the world. It existed as a rich cultural storehouse of the Mahayana and Vajrayana teachings of Buddhism. Religion was a unifying theme among the Tibetans -- as was their own language, literature, art, and world view developed by living at high altitudes, under harsh conditions, in a balance with their environment. Tibet Freedom Religion

title: Over 40 TYC activists detained after staging ‘storm protest’ outside the Chinese Embassy
content: New Delhi — Over 40 activists from the Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) staged a strong protest outside the Chinese Embassy in New Delhi, on the China's national founding day, to denounce China’s ongoing oppression, forced assimilation and the erosion of Tibetan identity, culture and language in Tibet. The Tibetan activists have been detained by the police and are currently being held at the Mandir Marg police station. The Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) organised a ‘storm protest’ outside the Chinese Embassy in New Delhi on October 1, 2026 – China’s National Day – to denounce China’s ongoing repression in Tibet, particularly through the so-called ‘Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress’. The protest brought together the TYC’s regional branches and more than 40 activists. After protesting and running towards the embassy, chanting slogans such as “Free Tibet”, “China out of Tibet”, “Stop the killings in Tibet”, “Stop the genocide in Tibet”, "Repeal the Ethnic Law" and “Free the political prisoners”, a large number of police officers arrived and the demonstrators were taken into custody. Tsering Choephel, President of Tibetan Youth Congress said, "On the 77th founding anniversary of the So-called People’s Republic of China, the Tibetan Youth Congress unequivocally condemns the continued assertion of Chinese sovereignty and political control over Tibet, East Turkistan, Southern Mongolia, and Manchuria." “Tibet is never part of China and will never be. Forced invasion and resultant incorporation of erstwhile Independent state of Tibet, and other nation like East Turkistan, Southern Mongolia and Manchuria mark new assault on freedom in general, particularly, its colonialist practice of territorial invasion and border incursion on other neighbouring state reflects imperialist intent of Chinese state existence. No any measure and its colonial law as well as policies will succeed in erasure of Tibetan’s distinct national historical claims, identity and will to determine their own political future," the President added. Lobsang Tenzin, General secretary of Tibetan Youth Congress said: "Tibet was never a part of China. We will continue to raise the demand for Tibet’s independence and carry the flame of Rangzen forward. No matter how long the struggle takes, we will preserve its spirit and pass it on to future generations." Tibetans in Sydney also staged a protest outside the Chinese Consulate in Sydney, Australia, on the same day, to denounce China’s ongoing oppression, forced assimilation and the erosion of Tibetan identity, culture and language in Tibet. The protest was organised by Regional Tibetan Youth Congress in Sydney, Australia. While Beijing and its supporters celebrate this day, exiled Tibetans and international human rights organisations view it as a day of mourning that marks the beginning of the illegal occupation of their homeland. On the occasion of China’s National Day, a coalition of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and Hong Kongers are staging protests outside Chinese embassies and consulates worldwide to denounce Beijing’s intensifying authoritarian policies and systematic human rights abuses. The joint demonstrations are designed to amplify international resistance against China's aggressive "Ethnic Unity" laws, forced cultural assimilation, colonial boarding school systems, transnational repression, and the total erasure of native language, religious freedom, and democratic rights across their respective occupied homelands.
